title: Second Law Of Thermodynamics In Closed Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Yuuya Chiba, Yasushi Yoneta, Ryusuke Hamazaki, And Akira Shimizu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuuya Chiba, Yasushi Yoneta, Ryusuke Hamazaki, and Akira Shimizu

A new theoretical framework reconciles the second law of thermodynamics with quantum mechanics, resolving a long-standing paradox by demonstrating how macroscopic thermodynamic principles emerge even from pure quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043023] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: A new theoretical framework shows how the second law of thermodynamics emerges in closed quantum many-body systems described by pure states.
motivation: There is a long-standing tension between the irreversibility of macroscopic thermodynamics and the unitary, reversible evolution of closed quantum systems.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework analyzing thermodynamic behavior in closed quantum many-body systems, reconciling macroscopic irreversibility with quantum mechanical pure-state evolution.
result: They demonstrate that macroscopic thermodynamic principles, including the second law, can emerge from pure quantum states without invoking external baths or ensemble averaging.
conclusion: The work resolves a conceptual paradox and provides a foundation for understanding thermodynamics in isolated quantum systems.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a conic optimization method for computing finite-size QKD key rates using Rényi entropies, yielding tighter security bounds and faster numerical convergence.
motivation: Finite-size key rate estimation in QKD is a critical bottleneck for practical security proofs, where existing bounds can be loose and numerically demanding.
method: The authors formulate key rate estimation as a conic optimization problem using Rényi entropic quantities, enabling efficient computation of tighter finite-size security bounds.
result: The method provides improved key rate bounds and demonstrates fast numerical convergence compared with existing approaches.
conclusion: This work advances practical QKD security analysis by combining Rényi entropy methods with conic optimization, making finite-size key rate estimation more accurate and computationally tractable.

title: Intrinsic Hamiltonian Of Mean Force And Strong-Coupling Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Author(s): Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, and Ángel Rivas

A unified theoretical framework allows one to measure thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information, offering a practical foundation for designing next-generation quantum thermal devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043014] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a unified theoretical framework for quantifying thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using local information via an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force.
motivation: Strong-coupling quantum thermodynamics is challenging because standard thermodynamic definitions based on global equilibrium fail or require inaccessible global information, limiting the design of quantum thermal devices.
method: The authors formulate an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force to characterize strong-coupling thermodynamics from local observables and subsystem information.
result: They obtain a unified framework that allows thermodynamic quantities to be measured using only local information in strongly coupled quantum systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical foundation for designing next-generation quantum thermal devices operating beyond the weak-coupling regime.

title: Exploring Noisy Quantum Thermodynamical Processes Via The Depolarizing-Channel Approximation
authors: Jian Li, Xiaoyang Wang, Marcus Huber, Nicolai Friis, And Pharnam Bakhshinezhad
abstract:
Author(s): Jian Li, Xiaoyang Wang, Marcus Huber, Nicolai Friis, and Pharnam Bakhshinezhad

Noise and errors are unavoidable in any realistic quantum process, including processes designed to reduce noise and errors in the first place. In particular, quantum thermodynamical protocols for cooling can be significantly affected, potentially altering both their performance and efficiency. Analy…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190401] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how noise, modeled via the depolarizing-channel approximation, affects the performance and efficiency of quantum thermodynamic cooling protocols.
motivation: Noise and errors are unavoidable in realistic quantum processes, and quantum thermodynamic protocols such as cooling can be significantly degraded by such imperfections.
method: The authors use a depolarizing-channel approximation to model noise in quantum thermodynamical processes and evaluate its impact on cooling performance and efficiency.
result: The analysis quantifies how depolarizing noise alters the performance and efficiency of quantum thermodynamic cooling protocols, providing insight into unavoidable operational limitations.
conclusion: Depolarizing-channel modeling offers a useful framework for assessing noise-induced limitations in quantum thermodynamic protocols and for guiding more robust designs.

title: Anti-Zeno Boost In An Autonomous Quantized-piston Thermal Machine
authors: M. Tahir Naseem
abstract:
Author(s): M. Tahir Naseem

Anti-Zeno enhancement of quantum heat machines has been established for working fluids driven by an external classical field, but whether it can enhance extractable-work accumulation in an autonomously evolving quantized piston remains an important question. Here we study an autonomous thermal machi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053708] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies whether anti-Zeno enhancement can boost extractable work in an autonomous thermal machine with a quantized piston.
motivation: Anti-Zeno effects are known to enhance quantum heat machines driven by classical fields, but their role in autonomously evolving quantized-piston machines remained unclear.
method: The author analyzes an autonomous quantum thermal machine with a quantized piston working fluid, assessing anti-Zeno-assisted work accumulation and performance.
result: The paper establishes conditions under which anti-Zeno effects enhance extractable-work accumulation in the autonomous quantized-piston thermal machine.
conclusion: Anti-Zeno boosting is extendable to autonomous quantized-piston thermal machines, providing a route to improved work extraction in quantum thermodynamic setups.

title: Quantum Randomness Certification With Untrusted Measurements And Few Probe States
authors: Makoto Ishihara, Carles Roch I Carceller, Kieran Neil Wilkinson, Casper Ahl Breum, Tobias Gehring, And Jonatan Bohr Brask
abstract:
Author(s): Makoto Ishihara, Carles Roch i Carceller, Kieran Neil Wilkinson, Casper Ahl Breum, Tobias Gehring, and Jonatan Bohr Brask

The authors present a semi-device-independent protocol for certifying quantum randomness from an uncharacterized measurement device by probing it with a small set of trusted states and lower-bounding the output entropy via semidefinite programming. They experimentally demonstrate the approach using optical homodyne detection of the vacuum probed by coherent states, showing that randomness can be certified in the presence of measurement noise, analog-to-digital converter imperfections, and finite-size effects.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052413] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose and experimentally demonstrate a semi-device-independent protocol that certifies quantum randomness from an untrusted measurement device using few trusted probe states and semidefinite programming.
motivation: Certifying randomness from uncharacterized devices is a central goal in quantum information, but fully device-independent protocols are demanding; semi-device-independent approaches offer a practical middle ground.
method: They lower-bound output entropy via semidefinite programming and test the protocol using optical homodyne detection of vacuum probed by coherent states, accounting for measurement noise, ADC imperfections, and finite-size effects.
result: Randomness is successfully certified despite experimental imperfections, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach with a small number of probe states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical semi-device-independent randomness certification scheme and validates it experimentally, advancing quantum randomness certification technology.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse For Fast Analytic Control Of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
authors: Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041018] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables and uses it to design composite pulses for fast analytic control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors require fast, accurate control, but conventional quantum signal processing assumes commuting control variables, limiting analytical pulse design.
method: The authors generalize quantum signal processing to non-Abelian control variables and construct composite pulse sequences for hybrid oscillator-qubit systems.
result: The framework enables analytical control protocols for hybrid oscillator-qubit processors, providing a route to fast and precise manipulation.
conclusion: Non-Abelian quantum signal processing broadens the toolkit for controlling hybrid quantum platforms and may improve gate speed and fidelity in oscillator-qubit architectures.

title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Zhi Li, Takato Mori, And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi Li, Takato Mori, and Beni Yoshida

Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041013] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: Tripartite Haar-random pure states contain no bipartite EPR entanglement that can be distilled by local operations, despite possessing large amounts of bipartite entanglement measures such as entanglement entropy.
motivation: Random states are central to quantum information (holography, random tensor networks, Page-curve arguments), and it is important to know whether their bipartite correlations are operationally useful as EPR entanglement under LOCC.
method: Analytical arguments using the properties of Haar-random tripartite states, together with entanglement distillation / LOCC monotonicity tools to bound distillable bipartite entanglement across any bipartition.
result: It is shown that bipartite EPR entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations, sharpening the gap between entropic entanglement measures and operationally distillable entanglement in random states.
conclusion: Haar-random tripartite states are entanglement-rich by entropic measures yet bipartite-distillation-poor, which has implications for random-state-based models of holography and for resource-theoretic interpretations of random correlations.

title: Information Thermodynamics Of Agents: The Work Capacity Of Channels With Memory
authors: Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, and Hans J. Briegel

An information-theoretic model of agents, i.e., complex self-organizing systems, shows that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an information-theoretic model of agents as complex self-organizing systems and analyzes the work capacity of memory channels, showing that forgetting past actions is necessary for thermodynamic efficiency.
motivation: Understanding how information processing constraints affect the thermodynamics of adaptive agents is central to information thermodynamics, especially when agents must operate efficiently while retaining memory of past actions.
method: The authors construct an information-theoretic framework for agents and study work capacity of channels with memory, linking memory retention, forgetting, and thermodynamic efficiency.
result: They find that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency, revealing a tradeoff between memory and work extraction.
conclusion: The work connects information-theoretic models of agency with thermodynamic bounds, suggesting that forgetting is not merely a limitation but a functional requirement for efficient information processing.

title: On-Demand Millisecond Storage Of Spectrotemporal Modes At Telecom Wavelength
authors: Anuj Sethia, Nasser Gohari Kamel, And Daniel Oblak
abstract:
Author(s): Anuj Sethia, Nasser Gohari Kamel, and Daniel Oblak

The realization of scalable quantum networks for distribution of entanglement over long distances hinges on quantum repeaters. To outperform the exponential transmission loss in optical fibers, quantum repeaters must employ multiplexing schemes in the temporal, spectral, or spatial domain. The perfo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190801] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates on-demand storage of spectrotemporal modes at telecom wavelength for millisecond durations, a key capability for multiplexed quantum repeaters.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks and long-distance entanglement distribution require quantum repeaters that beat exponential fiber loss, which in turn demand multiplexed quantum memories operating at telecom wavelengths with long storage times.
method: The authors implement a quantum memory capable of storing and retrieving spectrotemporal modes at telecom wavelength, characterizing storage time and mode fidelity relevant to temporal/spectral multiplexing schemes.
result: On-demand storage at the millisecond scale is achieved for spectrotemporal modes at telecom wavelength, enabling multiplexed operation compatible with repeater architectures.
conclusion: The demonstrated millisecond telecom-wavelength multimode storage advances the practical building blocks needed for multiplexed quantum repeaters and scalable quantum networks.

title: Quantum Key Distribution With Entanglement-swapped Photons From A Quantum Emitter
authors: Michele B. Rota, Francesco Basso Basset, Alessandro Laneve, Francesco Salusti, Nicolas Claro-Rodriguez, Giuseppe Ronco, Mattia Beccaceci, Tobias M. Krieger, Quirin Buchinger, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Sandra Stroj, Mariia Gumberidze, Vladyslav Usenko, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Mario A. Usuga Castaneda, Armando Rastelli, Klaus D. Jöns, And Rinaldo Trotta
abstract:
Author(s): Michele B. Rota, Francesco Basso Basset, Alessandro Laneve, Francesco Salusti, Nicolas Claro-Rodriguez, Giuseppe Ronco, Mattia Beccaceci, Tobias M. Krieger, Quirin Buchinger, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Sandra Stroj, Mariia Gumberidze, Vladyslav Usenko, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Mario A. Usuga Castaneda, Armando Rastelli, Klaus D. Jöns, and Rinaldo Trotta

Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a fundamental functionality of quantum networks. Extending its range requires quantum repeaters, a technology still under development and not yet demonstrated in combination with quantum cryptographic protocols. Here, we address the elementary operation of a viable …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043096] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates QKD using entanglement-swapped photons emitted by a quantum emitter, realizing an elementary building block for quantum repeater-based networks.
motivation: Extending QKD over long distances requires quantum repeaters, but repeater technology has not yet been combined with quantum cryptographic protocols in a practical demonstration.
method: The authors use photons from a quantum emitter and perform entanglement swapping to establish entanglement between distant parties, then use the swapped entanglement for a QKD protocol.
result: They experimentally demonstrate QKD with entanglement-swapped photons, showing that a quantum-emitter-based elementary repeater operation can support cryptographic functionality.
conclusion: This work connects entanglement swapping, quantum emitters, and QKD, providing an experimental step toward repeater-assisted quantum networks.

title: Symbolic Quantum-Trajectory Method For Multichannel Dicke Superradiance
authors: Raphael Holzinger, Nico S. Bassler, Julian Lyne, Susanne F. Yelin, And Claudiu Genes
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Holzinger, Nico S. Bassler, Julian Lyne, Susanne F. Yelin, and Claudiu Genes

We solve Dicke superradiance with two or more competing collective decay channels of tunable rates using a symbolic quantum-trajectory construction. The method yields closed time-domain populations and observables as finite combinations of exponential terms for arbitrary numbers of emitters and arbi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193602] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a symbolic quantum-trajectory method that analytically solves multichannel Dicke superradiance for arbitrary emitter numbers and tunable competing collective decay channels.
motivation: Dicke superradiance with multiple collective decay channels is important for understanding collective emission in quantum emitter ensembles, but exact time-domain solutions for arbitrary system sizes and channel competition are challenging.
method: They construct a symbolic quantum-trajectory framework that decomposes the dynamics into trajectories and yields closed-form time-domain populations and observables as finite sums of exponentials.
result: The method provides exact analytical expressions for arbitrary numbers of emitters and arbitrary numbers of competing collective decay channels with tunable rates.
conclusion: This work offers a practical analytical tool for studying multichannel collective emission and should be useful for designing and interpreting superradiance experiments in hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Thermodynamics Of A Phaseonium-driven Optomechanical Otto Engine
authors: Federico Amato, Gerardo Adesso, G. Massimo Palma, Salvatore Lorenzo, And Rosario Lo Franco
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Amato, Gerardo Adesso, G. Massimo Palma, Salvatore Lorenzo, and Rosario Lo Franco

We study an optomechanical Otto engine whose working medium is a single-mode cavity driven by beams of coherently prepared three-level phaseonium atoms. The atoms are not thermal reservoirs in the Gibbs sense; rather, their populations and ground-state coherence set the detailed-balance ratio of the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052202] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes an optomechanical quantum Otto engine whose working medium is a cavity driven by coherently prepared three-level phaseonium atoms.
motivation: Quantum heat engines at the nanoscale can exploit nonthermal resources such as atomic coherence, going beyond standard Gibbs-reservoir thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a single-mode optomechanical cavity coupled to beams of phaseonium atoms whose populations and ground-state coherence determine the detailed-balance ratio, and they evaluate the engine's thermodynamic performance in an Otto cycle.
result: The engine's operation and efficiency are shown to depend on the phaseonium coherence and population parameters, which effectively act as a controllable nonthermal reservoir.
conclusion: Phaseonium-driven optomechanical systems provide a viable platform for coherence-enhanced quantum thermodynamic cycles and quantum heat-engine implementations.

title: Chiral Entangled-State Generation Through Dissipative Quantum Dynamics
authors: Huixia Gao, Konghao Sun, Yiwen Han, Lei Xiao, Dengke Qu, Kunkun Wang, Xiang Zhan, Wei Yi, And Peng Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Huixia Gao, Konghao Sun, Yiwen Han, Lei Xiao, Dengke Qu, Kunkun Wang, Xiang Zhan, Wei Yi, and Peng Xue

Dissipation, though often detrimental to quantum entanglement, can be manipulated for the preparation of entangled states, wherein ingeniously designed quantum jump processes drive the system toward the desired steady state. Here we venture beyond this paradigm, and demonstrate a new type of entangl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190403] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a scheme for generating chiral entangled states by engineering dissipative quantum dynamics and quantum-jump processes.
motivation: Dissipation is usually viewed as detrimental to entanglement, but engineered dissipation can drive a system toward a desired entangled steady state; this work extends that paradigm to chiral entangled-state generation.
method: The authors design dissipative quantum dynamics, using tailored quantum-jump processes to steer the system into a target chiral entangled steady state, and demonstrate the effect experimentally or via a physical platform.
result: The scheme produces a new type of chiral entangled state through dissipation, showing that engineered open-system dynamics can generate nontrivial entangled resources beyond conventional steady-state entanglement preparation.
conclusion: Dissipation can be harnessed as a resource for preparing chiral entangled states, broadening the scope of dissipative entanglement engineering.

title: Certifying Localizable Quantum Properties With Constant Sample Complexity
authors: Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, And Xiongfeng Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, and Xiongfeng Ma

Researchers develop a versatile quantum certification framework that verifies global state properties and fidelity using local Pauli measurements.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041027] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a versatile quantum certification framework that verifies global state properties and fidelity using local Pauli measurements with constant sample complexity.
motivation: Certifying global quantum state properties typically requires many measurements, so efficient methods based on local observables are highly desirable for scalable quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop a certification framework based on local Pauli measurements to test localizable quantum properties and estimate fidelity.
result: The framework certifies relevant global state properties and fidelity with constant sample complexity.
conclusion: This provides a scalable and practical approach to quantum property certification using experimentally accessible local measurements.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, And Gauge Fields
authors: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin Demarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041008] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processor framework for simulating interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.
motivation: Quantum simulation of complex many-body and gauge theories is challenging for purely qubit-based processors, motivating hybrid architectures that combine discrete qubits with continuous-variable bosonic modes.
method: The authors develop a hybrid qubit-boson processor framework in which qubits couple to oscillator modes to encode and manipulate fermionic, bosonic, and gauge-field degrees of freedom.
result: The framework enables digital-analog quantum simulation of interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields on hybrid oscillator-qubit hardware.
conclusion: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors offer a promising route for quantum simulation beyond conventional qubit-only architectures.

title: Negative Quasiprobability Trajectories For Bell-diagonal States Under Local Decoherence
authors: Qing Yu, Kun Zhang, Yang-Yang Chen, And Xiao-Hui Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qing Yu, Kun Zhang, Yang-Yang Chen, and Xiao-Hui Wang

The fluctuation theorem (FT) relates microscopic trajectory distributions to macroscopic averages. Using quasiprobability trajectories, this framework has recently been extended to quantum information dynamics. Despite sharing the form of conventional thermodynamic FTs, information FTs involve quasi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054108] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends fluctuation-theorem methods to quantum information dynamics by analyzing negative quasiprobability trajectories for Bell-diagonal states undergoing local decoherence.
motivation: Information fluctuation theorems share the form of conventional thermodynamic fluctuation theorems but involve quasiprobability distributions whose negativity encodes genuinely quantum effects. Understanding how these trajectories behave in decohering quantum information settings is important for connecting information thermodynamics with quantum-information dynamics.
method: The authors study quasiprobability trajectory distributions for Bell-diagonal states under local decoherence and analyze the emergence and role of negative quasiprobabilities in the corresponding information fluctuation theorem.
result: They characterize how local decoherence affects the trajectory quasiprobabilities and identify conditions under which negativity appears, clarifying the quantum-information content of the fluctuation relation for this class of states.
conclusion: The work provides a concrete bridge between fluctuation theorems and quantum-information dynamics, showing that quasiprobability trajectories can reveal nonclassical features of decohering Bell-diagonal states within an information-thermodynamic framework.

title: Enabling Deterministic Passive Quantum State Transfer With Giant Atoms
authors: Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele de Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, And Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele De Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, and Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

Tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide enables deterministic quantum state transfer at above 99% fidelity, without any time-dependent control.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043013] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a passive, deterministic quantum state transfer protocol between giant atoms coupled to a waveguide, achieving above 99% fidelity without time-dependent control.
motivation: Deterministic quantum state transfer is a key primitive for connecting quantum nodes, but usually requires active pulse shaping or precise time-dependent control. Tailored giant-atom couplings may remove this need and simplify network links.
method: The authors design tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide to engineer the system's collective emission and absorption dynamics, enabling directional and deterministic transfer of an arbitrary quantum state.
result: The protocol reaches state-transfer fidelities above 99% passively, i.e., with static couplings and no time-dependent control.
conclusion: Giant-atom waveguide QED provides a practical route toward high-fidelity passive quantum interconnects and state transfer in quantum networks.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation imposes an unavoidable trade-off between the reliability of charging power and the reliability of work deposited in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for future energy storage, but fundamental limits on their charging and discharging performance, especially the reliability of power and work, are not fully understood.
method: The authors derive and analyze a quantum uncertainty relation that constrains fluctuations in charging power and work during quantum battery charging and discharging protocols.
result: The relation establishes a fundamental trade-off: improving the reliability of charging power necessarily degrades the reliability of the deposited work, and vice versa.
conclusion: These limitations provide essential design principles and performance bounds for future quantum energy storage devices, highlighting intrinsic quantum constraints on battery operation.

title: Free Mutual Information And Higher-Point Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators
authors: Shreya Vardhan And Jinzhao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shreya Vardhan and Jinzhao Wang

Researchers introduce a new entropic measure of quantum chaos, providing a physical interpretation to higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlation functions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043017] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces free mutual information as an entropic measure of quantum chaos and relates it to higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlators.
motivation: Higher-point OTOCs are important diagnostics of quantum scrambling, but their information-theoretic meaning is not fully clear. The authors aim to provide an entropic quantity that gives physical interpretation to these correlators.
method: They define a free mutual information for quantum systems and derive its connection to higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlation functions, using it to characterize chaotic dynamics.
result: Free mutual information is shown to capture information contained in higher-point OTOCs and to serve as an entropic diagnostic of quantum chaos and scrambling.
conclusion: The work bridges entropic information measures and quantum chaos, offering a new tool for understanding higher-point scrambling in quantum many-body systems.

title: Ising On The Donut: Regimes Of Topological Quantum Error Correction From Statistical Mechanics
authors: Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, And Dominic J. Williamson
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, and Dominic J. Williamson

An exact mapping to the 2D Ising model produces closed-form logical failure rates for the toric code, offering an analytic tool kit for benchmarking topological codes beyond current computational limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043004] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form logical failure rates for the toric code via an exact mapping to the 2D Ising model, providing analytic tools for benchmarking topological quantum error-correcting codes.
motivation: Topological codes such as the toric code are central to fault-tolerant quantum computing, but benchmarking their performance beyond current computational limits is challenging.
method: The authors establish an exact statistical-mechanical mapping between the toric code's error-correction performance and the 2D Ising model, enabling analytic calculation of logical failure rates.
result: They obtain closed-form expressions for logical failure rates across different regimes, offering an analytic toolkit that can benchmark topological codes beyond numerical simulation limits.
conclusion: This work bridges topological quantum error correction and statistical mechanics, providing practical analytic benchmarks for code performance and deepening understanding of error-correction thresholds.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based theoretical framework optimizes universal quantum gates in superconducting circuits using frequency and amplitude modulation, yielding fast high-fidelity control.
motivation: Superconducting qubit gates require precise control to achieve high fidelity while minimizing gate time and unwanted transitions; modulated drives offer a flexible control knob but need a systematic optimization framework.
method: The authors develop a Floquet analysis of frequency- and amplitude-modulated drives and use it to optimize gate parameters for universal quantum control in superconducting circuits.
result: The framework identifies fast, high-fidelity gate solutions, demonstrating that combined frequency and amplitude modulation can improve gate performance in superconducting qubit architectures.
conclusion: Floquet-based modulation engineering provides a practical route to optimized universal quantum control and is well suited to superconducting-circuit platforms.

title: Witnessing Short- And Long-Range Nonstabilizerness Via The Information Lattice
authors: Yuliya Bilinskaya, Miguel F. Martínez, Soumi Ghosh, Thomas Klein Kvorning, Claudia Artiaco, And Jens H. Bardarson
abstract:
Author(s): Yuliya Bilinskaya, Miguel F. Martínez, Soumi Ghosh, Thomas Klein Kvorning, Claudia Artiaco, and Jens H. Bardarson

We study nonstabilizerness on the information lattice and demonstrate that noninteger local information directly indicates nonstabilizerness. For states with a clear separation of short- and large-scale information, a noninteger total information at large scales [MATH] serves as a witness of l…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190402] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that noninteger local and total information on the information lattice can witness nonstabilizerness, including short- and long-range magic.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key quantum resource, but detecting it efficiently and characterizing its spatial structure remains challenging, especially beyond global magic measures.
method: The authors formulate nonstabilizerness through the information lattice, relating noninteger local information and large-scale total information to magic witnesses for states with separated short- and long-range information.
result: They demonstrate that noninteger total information at large scales acts as a witness of long-range nonstabilizerness, while local information signatures capture short-range nonstabilizerness.
conclusion: The information-lattice approach provides a useful diagnostic for short- and long-range nonstabilizerness, connecting magic resource theory with spatial information structure.

title: Algorithmic Construction Of Gapped Boundaries For Topological Stabilizer Codes: A Route To Low-Overhead Planar qLDPC Codes
authors: Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, And Yu-An Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, and Yu-An Chen (陳昱安)

An algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes enables low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures and fault-tolerant logical operations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043016] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes, enabling low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures and fault-tolerant logical operations.
motivation: Topological stabilizer codes offer robust quantum error correction, but practical planar architectures require systematic methods for designing gapped boundaries that support logical operations with low overhead.
method: The authors develop an algorithmic procedure to construct gapped boundaries for two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes, likely using techniques from anyon condensation or lattice surgery, and apply it to build planar qLDPC code architectures.
result: The framework yields explicit gapped boundary constructions and demonstrates how they enable low-overhead planar qLDPC codes with fault-tolerant logical gates.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation using topological stabilizer codes with planar architectures and reduced resource overhead.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Bell-sampling-based monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity that are experimentally accessible and yield efficient quantum algorithms, while also bounding state-preparation complexity and proving irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key resource for universal fermionic quantum computation, but experimentally practical, operationally meaningful quantifiers were lacking, motivating measures that are both physically measurable and theoretically rigorous.
method: The author develops monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity using Bell sampling protocols, deriving efficient quantum algorithms to estimate them and connecting them to state-preparation complexity and Gaussian conversion irreversibility.
result: The proposed Bell-sampling monotones provide experimentally accessible quantifiers, establish bounds on state-preparation complexity, and demonstrate the irreversibility of exact Gaussian state conversions.
conclusion: The work provides a practical, measurable resource-theoretic framework for fermionic non-Gaussianity, bridging experimental accessibility with rigorous operational characterization.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Researchers demonstrate optical charging of spins in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule, revealing ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics that could enable multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules are promising platforms for spin-based quantum technologies, but controlling spin states while maintaining electrical tunability remains challenging.
method: The authors use optical spectroscopy and electrical gating to charge a single electron spin in a quantum dot molecule and measure the dynamics via time-resolved techniques.
result: They observe extremely long orbital and spin relaxation times, indicating weak coupling to the environment while preserving electrical tunability.
conclusion: This platform could serve as a building block for generating photonic cluster states and advancing quantum information processing.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces logical accreditation, a scalable framework for certifying the accuracy of fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying encoded quantum systems and fault-tolerant computations is challenging because realistic device noise can undermine reliable certification at scale.
method: The authors develop a certification framework that assesses computational accuracy for encoded quantum systems under general noise models.
result: The framework provides a scalable tool for logical accreditation of fault-tolerant computations, enabling efficient verification of encoded quantum outputs.
conclusion: Logical accreditation offers a practical approach to certifying fault-tolerant quantum computations, supporting trustworthy quantum information processing under realistic noise.

title: Level 2.5 Large Deviations And Uncertainty Relations For Non-Markov Self-Interacting Dynamics
authors: Francesco Coghi, Amarjit Budhiraja, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Coghi, Amarjit Budhiraja, and Juan P. Garrahan

We address the general problem of formulating the dynamical large deviations of non-Markovian systems in a closed form. Specifically, we consider a broad class of “self-interacting” jump processes whose dynamics depends on the past through a functional of a state-dependent empirical observable. Expl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 197101] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a closed-form level-2.5 large-deviation framework for non-Markovian self-interacting jump processes and derives associated uncertainty relations.
motivation: Dynamical large deviations are well understood for Markovian stochastic dynamics, but non-Markovian systems with past-dependent self-interactions lack general closed-form large-deviation formulations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
method: The authors introduce a level-2.5 large-deviation approach for self-interacting jump processes whose dynamics depend on the past through a functional of a state-dependent empirical observable, and use it to obtain uncertainty relations.
result: They derive closed-form large-deviation rate functions for this broad class of non-Markovian jump processes and establish uncertainty relations that generalize known Markovian stochastic-thermodynamic bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic large-deviation and uncertainty-relation framework for non-Markov self-interacting dynamics, extending stochastic-thermodynamic bounds beyond the Markovian regime.

title: Universal Relaxation Speedup In Nonequilibrium Quantum Many-Body Systems Through Transient Resetting
authors: Parvinder Solanki, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): Parvinder Solanki, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Speeding up the relaxation dynamics of many-body quantum systems is important in a variety of contexts, including quantum computation and state preparation. We demonstrate that such acceleration can be universally achieved via transient stochastic resetting. This means that during an initial time in…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190404] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that transient stochastic resetting can universally accelerate relaxation in nonequilibrium quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Speeding up relaxation dynamics is important for quantum computation and state preparation, but achieving universal acceleration in complex many-body systems remains challenging.
method: The authors introduce a transient stochastic resetting protocol and analyze its effect on the relaxation dynamics of nonequilibrium quantum many-body systems.
result: Transient resetting is found to universally speed up relaxation toward the steady state across the considered many-body settings.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting can serve as a general control strategy for accelerating relaxation in quantum many-body systems, with potential applications in state preparation and quantum information processing.

title: Harnessing Intrinsic Noise For Quantum Simulation Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Sameer Dambal, Akira Sone, And Yu Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Sameer Dambal, Akira Sone, and Yu Zhang

Simulating open quantum systems on quantum computers is challenging because dissipative dynamics are nonunitary, whereas gate-based quantum algorithms are typically built from unitary operations. Conventional approaches can overcome this mismatch by embedding nonunitary processes into enlarged unita…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052418] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using intrinsic hardware noise as a resource to simulate open quantum system dynamics on gate-based quantum computers.
motivation: Simulating dissipative open quantum systems is difficult on unitary gate-based quantum computers, and conventional dilation-based embeddings can be resource-intensive.
method: Rather than fully suppressing or embedding noise, the authors harness intrinsic noise in the quantum processor to emulate nonunitary open-system evolution.
result: The approach is presented as a way to access open-system dynamics without the overhead of enlarged unitary embeddings, though the abstract omits detailed quantitative benchmarks.
conclusion: Intrinsic noise can be repurposed for quantum simulation of open quantum systems, offering a potential alternative to standard dilation-based simulation strategies.

title: Quantum Steering And Entanglement In A Tritter: Hierarchy Under Loss
authors: Jifeng Sun, Shumin Yang, Teng Zhao, Qingqian Kang, And Liyun Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Jifeng Sun, Shumin Yang, Teng Zhao, Qingqian Kang, and Liyun Hu

We analyze quantum correlations in a three-mode Gaussian state generated by a tritter, driven by a two-mode squeezed vacuum and a coherent state. The coherent amplitude does not affect the correlation structure, which is solely governed by the initial squeezing. For five representative local-loss co…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052414] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how quantum steering and entanglement are distributed and degraded under local loss in a three-mode Gaussian state produced by a tritter.
motivation: Three-mode Gaussian states provide a useful setting to study the hierarchy between different forms of quantum correlations, especially when realistic loss is present.
method: The authors consider a tritter driven by a two-mode squeezed vacuum and a coherent state, characterize the resulting Gaussian correlations, and examine five representative local-loss configurations.
result: They find that the coherent amplitude does not affect the correlation structure, which is governed by the initial squeezing, and they map the loss-dependent hierarchy among steering and entanglement.
conclusion: The work clarifies how local loss affects the ordering and robustness of Gaussian quantum correlations in a three-mode tritter setting, with implications for steering-based quantum information protocols.

title: Geometric Mode Steering Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect
authors: Yingying Hong, Longxing Xu, Weiwei Zhang, Jie Ren, And Jianhui Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yingying Hong, Longxing Xu, Weiwei Zhang, Jie Ren, and Jianhui Wang

The slowest Liouvillian mode often bottlenecks the relaxation of an open quantum system to its steady state. Standard strategies circumvent this bottleneck by selecting special initial states or engineering the dissipator. Here we investigate this problem when the input and the subsequent dissipativ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052203] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies geometric control of Liouvillian modes to steer the quantum Mpemba effect and accelerate relaxation in open quantum systems.
motivation: Relaxation to steady state is often bottlenecked by the slowest Liouvillian mode, and standard approaches rely on special initial states or engineered dissipation.
method: The authors analyze how input states and subsequent dissipative dynamics can be geometrically manipulated to suppress or exploit slow modes associated with the quantum Mpemba effect.
result: They identify geometric mode-steering conditions under which anomalous relaxation, including the Mpemba effect, can be controlled without solely fine-tuning initial states or the dissipator.
conclusion: The work provides a mode-geometric perspective on anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems, relevant to controlling dissipation and thermalization dynamics.

title: Metastable Phase Separation And Information Retrieval In Multicomponent Liquids
authors: Davide Marcato, Rodrigo Braz Teixeira, Izaak Neri, And Pablo Sartori
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Marcato, Rodrigo Braz Teixeira, Izaak Neri, and Pablo Sartori

A thermodynamic theory shows that multicomponent liquid mixtures can store prescribed compositions as metastable states and retrieve them from partial seeds, realizing associative memory in a demixing liquid.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041033] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: A thermodynamic theory shows that multicomponent liquid mixtures can encode prescribed compositions as metastable states and recover them from partial compositional seeds, enabling associative memory in a demixing liquid.
motivation: The work connects thermodynamic phase behavior to information storage and retrieval, asking whether physical many-body systems can perform associative memory tasks through metastable phase separation rather than engineered computational components.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamic theory of multicomponent liquid mixtures, analyzing metastable phase separation and composition retrieval from partial seeds within a demixing-liquid framework.
result: They demonstrate that prescribed compositions can be stored as metastable states and retrieved via partial seeds, realizing associative memory in a multicomponent liquid system.
conclusion: The results suggest that demixing liquids provide a physical substrate for information storage and associative retrieval, extending information-thermodynamic ideas to classical multicomponent fluids.

title: Breakdown Of The Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced By Auxiliary Circuit Modes
authors: Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, And Alexandre Blais
abstract:
Author(s): Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, and Alexandre Blais

Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041012] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Auxiliary circuit modes generate multiphoton resonances that shorten the tunneling time and degrade coherence of the driven Kerr-cat qubit.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits are a promising biased-noise bosonic platform, but their coherence under strong drives is limited by physics beyond the ideal single-mode model, motivating a detailed study of parasitic circuit elements.
method: The authors analyze the Kerr-cat qubit coupled to auxiliary modes of the superconducting circuit, identifying drive-activated multiphoton resonance conditions and computing their effect on the tunneling time (bit-flip rate).
result: Auxiliary modes are shown to induce multiphoton resonances that break down the exponential suppression of bit flips, sharply reducing the effective tunneling time under strong driving.
conclusion: Circuit design must account for auxiliary modes to preserve Kerr-cat coherence, and the results give guidelines for mitigating drive-induced breakdown in bosonic qubit architectures.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an axiomatic quantum-information framework to classify mixed-state topological phases in open quantum systems using phase invariants derived from information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing.
motivation: Topological phases are usually studied for pure states or closed systems, but realistic open quantum systems require understanding mixed-state topological order and robust invariants under decoherence.
method: The authors formulate mixed-state topological phases axiomatically and introduce information-theoretic invariants based on information convex sets, quantum memory capacity, and secret-sharing correlations.
result: They identify phase invariants that characterize mixed-state topological order and show how quantum-information primitives distinguish distinct topological phases in open systems.
conclusion: The work bridges topological phases of matter with quantum information theory, providing a framework for classifying mixed-state topological order via operational information measures.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality Of Scrooge Ensembles In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, and John Preskill

Researchers introduce Scrooge
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Scrooge ensembles to characterize universal randomness and deep thermalization in constrained quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Understanding how chaotic many-body dynamics generate universal random ensembles is central to quantum thermalization and information scrambling.
method: Defines Scrooge ensembles as maximally random distributions consistent with local constraints and analyzes their universality across many-body models.
result: Shows that Scrooge ensembles emerge universally and govern deep thermalization, providing a quantitative framework for constrained randomness.
conclusion: Constrained quantum systems can achieve universal randomness described by Scrooge ensembles, extending deep thermalization theory.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows via statistical-mechanics mappings that quantum information in Moore-Read non-Abelian anyons is robust against arbitrary density dephasing, while Laughlin-state information has infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
motivation: Topological quantum states are promising for storing quantum information, but their resilience to realistic decoherence channels such as density dephasing must be understood.
method: The authors use statistical-mechanics mappings to analyze fractional quantum Hall states under density decoherence and compare robustness in Moore-Read and Laughlin states.
result: Information stored in Moore-Read non-Abelian anyons resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin states exhibit infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
conclusion: The findings clarify how decoherence affects topological quantum information and highlight filling-factor-dependent robustness in fractional quantum Hall platforms.

title: Temporal Entanglement Transition In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
authors: Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Michael Sonner, Qi Camm Huang, Wen Wei Ho, Alessio Lerose, And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Michael Sonner, Qi Camm Huang, Wen Wei Ho, Alessio Lerose, and Dmitry A. Abanin

Applying temporal coarse graining to the influence matrix of chaotic quantum baths reveals an entanglement transition, reconciling global non-Markovian memory with local thermalization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043024] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: Temporal coarse graining of the influence matrix in chaotic quantum baths reveals an entanglement transition that reconciles global non-Markovian memory with local thermalization.
motivation: Chaotic quantum many-body systems exhibit both local thermalization and long-range non-Markovian memory, and understanding how these coexist is a central open problem in quantum dynamics.
method: The authors apply temporal coarse graining to the influence matrix of chaotic quantum baths and analyze the resulting entanglement structure.
result: They find a temporal entanglement transition that separates regimes of global non-Markovian memory from local thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides a framework linking non-Markovian dynamics, quantum chaos, and thermalization in many-body systems.

title: Modeling Logical Gates And Readout Of Superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qubits
authors: Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, And Arne L. Grimsmo
abstract:
Author(s): Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, and Arne L. Grimsmo

Analyzing loss, dephasing, error-spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies in Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits yields a highly-improved understanding of GKP qubits in practice and new strategies for improving performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043020] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper models logical gates and readout for superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits under realistic noise and measurement imperfections.
motivation: GKP qubits are promising for hardware-level quantum error correction, but practical performance is limited by loss, dephasing, error spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies.
method: The authors analyze superconducting GKP qubit dynamics by modeling loss, dephasing, error propagation, and imperfect homodyne readout during logical gate operations.
result: The analysis provides an improved understanding of GKP qubit behavior in practice and identifies strategies for enhancing logical gate and readout performance.
conclusion: The work offers practical guidance for developing more robust superconducting GKP qubits and informs future hardware-level error-correction efforts.

title: High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution Via Full Core-Mode Encoding Over Deployed Multicore Fibers
authors: G. H. Dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, And G. Lima
abstract:
Author(s): G. H. dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, and G. Lima

A four-dimensional quantum key distribution protocol utilizing full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers is demonstrated, establishing a viable architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043012] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: A four-dimensional QKD protocol is demonstrated using full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers, showing a practical route to high-rate quantum-secure communication.
motivation: High-dimensional encoding promises higher information capacity and noise resilience per photon, but its feasibility over installed real-world fiber infrastructure remains largely unexplored.
method: The authors exploit the core and mode degrees of freedom of a deployed multicore fiber to encode four-dimensional states, implementing a full core-mode QKD protocol and characterizing the channel and key rates.
result: The experiment yields viable secret key generation over deployed multicore fiber, confirming that core-mode encoding can support high-dimensional QKD in a realistic network setting.
conclusion: Full core-mode encoding over multicore fibers constitutes a viable architecture for high-rate, high-dimensional quantum-secure communications, bridging lab demonstrations and deployed network scenarios.

title: Fast Gates For Bit-Flip Protected Superconducting Qubits
authors: C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, and J. M. Fink

An architecture design for real-time tunable bit-flip protection yields a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043008] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a superconducting qubit architecture with real-time tunable bit-flip protection, enabling fast gates on a hardware-efficient noise-biased platform suited to error correction and scaling.
motivation: Noise-biased (bit-flip protected) qubits such as bosonic cat qubits promise hardware-efficient error correction, but practical architectures require fast, tunable control and easy reconfiguration of the protection.
method: The authors design a superconducting circuit architecture in which bit-flip protection can be tuned in real time, and analyze its gate speeds, noise bias, and compatibility with scalable fabrication and readout/control schemes.
result: The architecture yields fast gate operations while preserving a strong bias against bit-flip errors, providing a hardware-efficient platform amenable to error correction and scaling.
conclusion: Real-time tunable bit-flip protection offers a practical route toward noise-biased superconducting qubits that combine fast control with error-correction-friendly hardware.

title: Predicting Magic From Very Few Measurements
authors: J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, And R. A. Macêdo
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, and R. A. Macêdo

A near-optimal method quantifies nonstabilizerness—the resource that enables universal quantum computation—from a small number of Pauli measurements, extending its estimation to system sizes beyond the reach of standard techniques.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043009] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a near-optimal method to quantify nonstabilizerness, or magic, using very few Pauli measurements, enabling estimation for system sizes beyond standard techniques.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is the key resource for universal quantum computation, but quantifying it efficiently is challenging because standard approaches require many measurements or exact state tomography.
method: The authors develop a measurement-efficient estimator of magic based on a limited number of Pauli expectation values, likely using randomized or optimized Pauli sampling and a resource-theoretic quantifier of nonstabilizerness.
result: The method provides near-optimal quantification of nonstabilizerness from few Pauli measurements and extends magic estimation to larger system sizes inaccessible to conventional techniques.
conclusion: This work offers a practical and scalable tool for characterizing magic as a quantum resource, with implications for resource theories and experimental quantum information processing.

title: Hole Spin Resilient To Dipole-Induced Thermal Effects
authors: V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. de Franceschi, B. Martinez, And B. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. De Franceschi, B. Martinez, and B. Brun

A silicon hole spin unveils an electric origin of thermal frequency shifts and exhibits a magnetic-field sweet-spot immune to those, guiding the design of thermally robust semiconductor qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043005] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A silicon hole spin qubit shows an electrically driven thermal frequency shift and a magnetic-field sweet spot that suppresses it, informing thermally robust semiconductor qubit design.
motivation: Semiconductor spin qubits are promising for scalable quantum computing, but their operational stability can be degraded by thermal fluctuations and device heating.
method: The authors characterize a silicon hole spin qubit, identify the electric origin of thermal frequency shifts, and locate a magnetic-field sweet spot where the qubit is insensitive to those shifts.
result: The hole spin exhibits a magnetic-field sweet spot that is immune to dipole-induced thermal frequency noise, enabling thermally resilient operation.
conclusion: These findings provide design guidance for thermally robust semiconductor spin qubits and highlight hole spins as a viable platform for stable quantum hardware.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Experiments, theory, and simulations show that readout drive frequency strongly controls readout-induced decoherence in transmon qubits arising from coupling to two-level systems (TLSs).
motivation: Readout is a dominant source of decoherence in superconducting qubit architectures, and the microscopic mechanism by which the readout drive degrades qubit lifetimes is not well understood or controlled.
method: The authors combine measurements of transmon lifetime versus readout drive frequency with a theoretical model of the driven qubit-TLS interaction and numerical simulations, identifying spectral reshaping of the qubit by the readout tone as the key ingredient.
result: Qubit lifetimes degrade strongly at particular readout frequencies where the driven qubit spectrum overlaps TLS resonances, and choosing an appropriate drive frequency minimizes this readout-induced decoherence.
conclusion: Readout drive frequency is a practical, tunable knob for mitigating TLS-mediated decoherence in superconducting qubit readout, with theory and simulation providing guidance for optimizing it.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an in situ method to benchmark fault-tolerant Clifford quantum circuits using existing error syndrome data without extra calibration circuits.
motivation: Benchmarking fault-tolerant quantum hardware and verifying encoded computations typically requires costly calibration circuits, so a method that uses only syndrome data could enable more efficient and scalable validation.
method: The authors develop a protocol that analyzes error syndrome data from fault-tolerant Clifford circuit executions to characterize hardware performance and verify encoded computations in situ.
result: The approach can efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations using only existing syndrome data, avoiding additional calibration overhead.
conclusion: In situ benchmarking with Clifford circuits offers a practical route for validating fault-tolerant quantum computations and assessing hardware performance without dedicated calibration experiments.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations model electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices and identify operating regimes robust against common device imperfections and charge defects.
motivation: Electron shuttling is a promising route for transporting spin qubits in silicon-based quantum processors, but realistic device imperfections and charge defects can degrade shuttling fidelity.
method: The authors perform three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in SiMOS device geometries, incorporating common device imperfections and charge defects to map resilient operating regimes.
result: The simulations identify parameter regimes where electron shuttling remains robust against typical imperfections, providing guidance for device design and operation.
conclusion: The work supports the development of silicon spin-qubit architectures by clarifying how realistic fabrication and charge-environment imperfections affect shuttling performance.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a circuit-based framework for characterizing finite-temperature quantum phases via correlation decay and argues that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Finite-temperature quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memories are important for understanding robust quantum order and practical quantum storage, but a unified circuit-based characterization has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based framework that uses correlation-decay conditions to classify thermal quantum phases and analyze the stability of quantum memories at finite temperature.
result: They establish a correlation-decay criterion for finite-temperature quantum phases and show that self-correction emerges as a universal feature of such finite-temperature quantum memories.
conclusion: The work provides a general circuit-based perspective linking thermal phase structure to self-correcting quantum memory, with implications for quantum error correction and topological quantum order.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general framework for studying statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles, with applications to noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Understanding the statistical behavior of noisy quantum channels is important for analyzing and mitigating noise in near-term quantum algorithms, but a general moment-based framework for channel ensembles has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for computing and analyzing moments of ensembles of quantum channels, likely using tools from quantum information theory and random matrix or ensemble methods.
result: The framework provides new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms by characterizing how channel ensembles behave at the level of statistical moments.
conclusion: This work offers a systematic way to study noisy quantum channel ensembles, potentially enabling better noise analysis and algorithm design for variational quantum computing.

title: From Coherent To Fermionized Microwave Photons In A Superconducting Transmission Line
authors: Alberto Tabarelli de Fatis, Stephanie Matern, Gianluca Rastelli, And Iacopo Carusotto
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Tabarelli de Fatis, Stephanie Matern, Gianluca Rastelli, and Iacopo Carusotto

We investigate superconducting transmission lines as a novel platform for realizing a quantum fluid of microwave photons in a propagating geometry. We anticipate that the strong photon-photon interactions provided by the intrinsic nonlinearity of Josephson junctions are sufficient to enter a regime …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193601] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies superconducting transmission lines with Josephson-junction nonlinearity as a platform for realizing strongly interacting propagating microwave photons, including a fermionization regime.
motivation: Microwave photons in superconducting circuits usually interact weakly, so achieving strong photon-photon interactions in a propagating geometry could enable quantum-fluid and many-body physics with circuit-QED platforms.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a superconducting transmission line whose intrinsic Josephson-junction nonlinearity provides strong photon-photon interactions, and they identify regimes where the microwave photons behave as a coherent quantum fluid and can fermionize.
result: They anticipate that the Josephson nonlinearity is sufficient to reach a strongly interacting regime where propagating microwave photons exhibit fermionized behavior.
conclusion: Superconducting transmission lines are proposed as a novel circuit-QED platform for exploring quantum fluids and fermionization of microwave photons in a propagating geometry.

title: Theory Of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
authors: Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, And Luca V. Delacrétaz
abstract:
Author(s): Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, and Luca V. Delacrétaz

Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041010] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an effective field theory for late-time out-of-time-order correlators to extract hidden transport parameters in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Out-of-time-order correlators are key diagnostics of quantum chaos and scrambling, but their late-time structure and connection to transport are not fully understood.
method: The authors construct an effective field theory capturing the late-time behavior of out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The framework identifies hidden transport parameters encoded in late-time OTOC dynamics.
conclusion: This provides a theoretical link between quantum chaos/scrambling diagnostics and transport properties in many-body systems.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, And Energy Diffusion
authors: J. T. Chalker And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): J. T. Chalker and Dominik Hahn

Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031076] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A solvable many-body model demonstrates that energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to clarify universal connections between transport, many-body chaos, and spectral statistics in quantum dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a solvable many-body quantum model and relate its energy-diffusion behavior to spectral correlation functions.
result: They show that energy diffusion provides the organizing mechanism for spectral correlations in the chaotic regime.
conclusion: Energy diffusion is identified as a key link between dynamical transport and spectral statistics in chaotic many-body quantum systems.

title: Improved Error Correction With Leakage Reduction Units Built Into Qubit Measurement In A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, And Leonardo Dicarlo
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, and Leonardo DiCarlo

Application of simultaneous microwave pulses to a transmon and readout resonator can return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout to improve quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033062] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates leakage reduction units integrated into qubit measurement using simultaneous microwave pulses on a transmon and its readout resonator to improve quantum error correction.
motivation: Leakage out of the computational subspace degrades quantum error correction in superconducting processors, so mitigating leakage during measurement is important for reliable QEC.
