title: Meson Spectroscopy Of Exotic Symmetries Of Ising Criticality In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, and Alexandre Dauphin

A programmable array of atoms reveals how symmetry of the quantum Ising chain transforms when chains are coupled together, providing experimental signatures of a new excitation spectrum.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043018] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: A Rydberg-atom-array experiment probes meson-like excitations and exotic symmetries in coupled quantum Ising chains near criticality.
motivation: Coupled Ising chains can host symmetry structures and excitation spectra beyond simple one-dimensional criticality, but experimental signatures are challenging to access.
method: The authors use a programmable Rydberg atom array to simulate coupled quantum Ising chains and perform spectroscopy of the resulting excitation spectrum.
result: They observe experimental signatures of a new meson excitation spectrum and show how the symmetry of the quantum Ising chain transforms when chains are coupled.
conclusion: Programmable Rydberg arrays provide a viable platform for studying exotic symmetries and meson spectroscopy in quantum critical systems.

title: Theory Of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry With General Markovian Light Sources
authors: Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, And Rahul Trivedi
abstract:
Author(s): Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, and Rahul Trivedi

A new framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources clarifies where realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033069] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework evaluates quantum-enhanced interferometry using general Markovian light sources and identifies when realistic devices can offer a quantum advantage.
motivation: Quantum light sources promise improved interferometric sensitivity, but realistic open-system dynamics make it unclear when a genuine quantum advantage survives.
method: The authors develop a general formalism for Markovian light sources and analyze their performance in interferometric protocols.
result: The framework clarifies conditions under which realistic Markovian light sources can provide quantum advantage in interferometry.
conclusion: The work offers a design and evaluation tool for practical quantum-enhanced interferometry, but it is outside the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based framework derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct Trotter formulas, tightening gate-count estimates for simulating driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
motivation: Product formulas (Trotter-Suzuki decompositions) are the workhorse of digital quantum simulation, but rigorous error bounds for time-dependent Hamiltonians and multiproduct extrapolation schemes have been loose, leading to overly pessimistic resource estimates.
method: The authors recast the stroboscopic dynamics of product formulas as an effective Floquet Hamiltonian and bound the error in terms of nested commutators of the Hamiltonian and its time derivatives, extending the analysis to multiproduct (Richardson-type) formulas.
result: The derived bounds scale more favorably with the number of Trotter steps and reproduce the expected order-by-order error scaling, yielding sharper gate-count estimates for driven-dynamics simulation and adiabatic state preparation.
conclusion: The Floquet-based commutator bounds provide a practical and rigorous tool for resource estimation in time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation, though the contribution is primarily algorithmic rather than information-theoretic.

title: Thermodynamic Space Of Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Shiling Liang (梁师翎), Paolo de Los Rios, And Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract:
Author(s): Shiling Liang (梁师翎), Paolo De Los Rios, and Daniel Maria Busiello

By deriving bounds on reaction affinities and stationary concentrations, this work defines the thermodynamic space of chemical reaction networks and establishes their fundamental thermodynamic constraints.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041026] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper defines a thermodynamic space for chemical reaction networks by deriving bounds on reaction affinities and stationary concentrations.
motivation: Chemical reaction networks are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics, but their fundamental thermodynamic constraints are not fully captured by existing bounds.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds on reaction affinities and stationary concentrations to characterize the feasible thermodynamic space of chemical reaction networks.
result: They establish constraints that define the thermodynamic space accessible to chemical reaction networks and show how affinities and concentrations are bounded.
conclusion: The work provides a general thermodynamic framework for understanding fundamental limits on chemical reaction networks.

title: Multiparameter Quantum Estimation With A Uniformly Accelerated Unruh-DeWitt Detector
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yashu Yang, Wei Ye, Yawen Tang, Hui Cao, Huan Zhang, Zunlue Zhu, Wuming Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yashu Yang, Wei Ye, Yawen Tang, Hui Cao, Huan Zhang, Zunlue Zhu, Wuming Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, and Xingdong Zhao

The uniformly accelerated Unruh-DeWitt detector serves as a fundamental model in relativistic quantum metrology. While previous studies have mainly concentrated on single-parameter estimation via the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, the multiparameter case remains significantly underexplored. In this paper…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052417] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies multiparameter quantum estimation using a uniformly accelerated Unruh-DeWitt detector, extending prior single-parameter relativistic quantum metrology analyses.
motivation: Previous work on Unruh-DeWitt detectors has mainly focused on single-parameter estimation via the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, leaving multiparameter estimation largely unexplored.
method: The authors analyze a uniformly accelerated Unruh-DeWitt detector within a multiparameter quantum estimation framework, likely employing the quantum Fisher information matrix and quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
result: The paper characterizes multiparameter estimation precision for the accelerated detector and identifies how acceleration-related effects influence the achievable bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a multiparameter extension of relativistic quantum metrology with Unruh-DeWitt detectors, though its direct relevance to the listed core research directions is limited.

title: Enhanced Weak-field Sensing Using Detuned Motional Squeezing
authors: Li-Wen Zhang, Yang Liu, Han-Jie Zhu, And Wei Qin
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Wen Zhang, Yang Liu, Han-Jie Zhu, and Wei Qin

Achieving measurement precision beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL) is a fundamental object in quantum metrology. In this manuscript, we propose a streamlined protocol for weak signal sensing in a trapped-ion spin-oscillator system that simultaneously exploits detuned motional squeezing and spin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052411] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a trapped-ion spin-oscillator protocol that combines detuned motional squeezing and spin dynamics to enhance weak-field sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Quantum metrology aims to surpass the standard quantum limit, and trapped-ion spin-oscillator systems offer a controllable platform for precision sensing.
method: The authors design a streamlined sensing protocol using detuned motional squeezing in a trapped-ion system, analyzing its performance for weak signal detection.
result: The protocol is expected to improve weak-field measurement precision beyond the standard quantum limit by exploiting motional squeezing and spin-oscillator coupling.
conclusion: Detuned motional squeezing provides a practical route to enhanced weak-field sensing in trapped-ion platforms, though the work is primarily a metrology application.

title: Non-Markovian Delay-assisted Sensing With Waveguide-coupled Quantum Emitters
authors: Prajit Dhara, Isack Padilla, Saikat Guha, Annyun Das, And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Prajit Dhara, Isack Padilla, Saikat Guha, Annyun Das, and Kanu Sinha

We show that in a minimal setup of two waveguide-coupled quantum emitters, separated by long distances and subject to an external field, time-delayed feedback can be a resource for sensing field gradients. While the field gradient induces a detuning between the emitters, the large interatomic separa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043138] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a waveguide-coupled quantum-emitter setup where time-delayed feedback enables sensing of external field gradients.
motivation: The authors aim to show that non-Markovian delayed feedback in a minimal waveguide-QED system can be exploited as a resource for metrology.
method: Two distant waveguide-coupled quantum emitters subject to an external field are modeled; the field gradient induces detuning while the large separation produces time-delayed feedback.
result: The delayed feedback is found to enhance or enable sensing of the field gradient in this emitter-waveguide configuration.
conclusion: Time-delayed non-Markovian dynamics can serve as a useful resource for quantum sensing in waveguide-coupled emitter platforms.

title: Nested Superstatistics: When The Fluctuation Parameter Fluctuates
authors: Kamel Ourabah
abstract:
Author(s): Kamel Ourabah

Many nonequilibrium systems exhibit a hierarchy of well-separated dynamical scales. Typically, microscopic variables such as energy or velocity evolve rapidly, whereas environmental parameters such as the inverse temperature [MATH] fluctuate more slowly. This separation naturally leads to superstatisti…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043119] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: Introduces nested superstatistics for nonequilibrium systems in which the superstatistical fluctuation parameter itself fluctuates across hierarchical time scales.
motivation: Many nonequilibrium systems exhibit well-separated dynamical scales, with fast microscopic variables and slowly fluctuating environmental parameters such as inverse temperature, motivating extensions beyond standard single-level superstatistics.
method: Develops a nested superstatistical formalism in which the fluctuating parameter is itself superstatistically distributed, leading to compound distributions and generalized thermodynamic averages.
result: Shows that hierarchical fluctuations modify the resulting statistical distributions and thermodynamic behavior, clarifying when a single superstatistical level is insufficient.
conclusion: Nested superstatistics provides a framework for multiscale classical nonequilibrium systems, but it is not directly connected to quantum information or quantum thermodynamic protocols.

title: Experimental Realization Of A Rotating Radio-frequency Ion Trap For Precision Metrology
authors: Sun Yool Park, Anzhou Wang, Kia Boon Ng, Patricia Hector Hernandez, Addison Hartman, Tuan Anh Nguyen, Rohan Kompella, Michail Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, Jun Ye, And Eric A. Cornell
abstract:
Author(s): Sun Yool Park, Anzhou Wang, Kia Boon Ng, Patricia Hector Hernandez, Addison Hartman, Tuan Anh Nguyen, Rohan Kompella, Michail Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, Jun Ye, and Eric A. Cornell

The authors experimentally realize the rotating radio-frequency (rrf) ion trap proposed by Hasegawa and Bollinger two decades ago. Unlike a conventional rf trap, whose potential oscillates back and forth, the rotating potential of the rrf trap averages over angular nonuniformities caused by realistic electrode geometry, yielding more uniform confinement and reduced ion loss at the same central trap strength—properties advantageous for precision measurements.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L050801] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally demonstrate a rotating radio-frequency ion trap that provides more uniform confinement and reduced ion loss for precision metrology.
motivation: The rotating RF trap was proposed two decades ago to average over electrode-geometry nonuniformities and improve confinement uniformity compared with conventional oscillating RF traps.
method: They realize the rotating radio-frequency potential experimentally and compare its trapping performance, specifically uniformity of confinement and ion loss, against conventional RF trapping at the same central trap strength.
result: The rotating RF trap yields more uniform confinement and reduced ion loss, confirming the expected advantages of the architecture for precision measurements.
conclusion: This demonstrates a practical ion-trap platform for precision metrology, though its direct relevance to quantum information processing or qubit hardware is limited.

title: Adiabatic Dressing Of Quantum-enhanced Markov Chains
authors: Wen Ting Hsieh, Alev Orfi, And Dries Sels
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Ting Hsieh, Alev Orfi, and Dries Sels

Quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo, a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm in which configurations are proposed by a quantum proposer and accepted or rejected by a classical algorithm, has been introduced as a possible method for robust quantum speedup. Previous work has identified competing fa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052416] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes adiabatic dressing as a technique to improve quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo, a hybrid quantum-classical sampling algorithm.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced MCMC has been proposed as a route to robust quantum speedup, but previous work identified competing failure modes that limit its performance.
method: The authors study a hybrid scheme where a quantum proposer generates configurations and a classical accept/reject step governs the Markov chain, with adiabatic dressing introduced to modify the quantum proposal.
result: The paper characterizes how adiabatic dressing affects the algorithm's behavior and may mitigate some competing limitations of the quantum proposer.
conclusion: This work contributes to understanding design strategies for quantum-enhanced MCMC, but it is an algorithmic/sampling study rather than a core information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules are shown to have electrically tunable orbital coupling, offering a potential building block for 2D photonic cluster states.
motivation: Photonic cluster states are a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, but scalable generation requires emitters with tunable, coherent coupling between multiple optical transitions; quantum dot molecules in the telecom O-band could provide this while remaining compatible with fiber infrastructure.
method: The authors fabricate InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules emitting in the O-band and use electrical gating to tune the inter-dot orbital coupling, characterizing the resulting emission via photoluminescence/spectroscopy and assessing quantum light emission properties.
result: Electrically tunable orbital coupling between the coupled quantum dots is demonstrated, with associated quantum light emission features in the O-band, indicating control over the molecular level structure.
conclusion: The platform is proposed as a route toward generating 2D photonic cluster states using deterministically coupled quantum dot molecules, though realization of such states remains future work.

title: Computational And Physical Complexity Of Synthesizing Random Multiqudit Quantum States And Unitary Operators
authors: Sahel Ashhab And Bora Basyildiz
abstract:
Author(s): Sahel Ashhab and Bora Basyildiz

We analyze the complexity of synthesizing random states and unitary operators in a multiqudit system in two paradigms. In one case, we consider the situation in which we manipulate the system by applying a sequence of one- and two-qudit quantum gates that constitute the elementary, and universal, ga…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052412] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares the gate-based computational complexity of synthesizing random multiqudit states and unitary operators with the physical complexity (time/energy resources) required to realize those circuits in a multiqudit system.
motivation: Random states and unitaries are benchmarks for quantum advantage and algorithm design, but their practical realization is limited by physical resources; the authors aim to quantify the gap between abstract circuit complexity and the physical cost of implementing such circuits.
method: They consider universal sets of one- and two-qudit gates and derive scaling laws for the number of gates and for physical resource costs (e.g., interaction times or energies) needed to generate random states and unitaries in d-dimensional systems.
result: Explicit expressions for the scaling of gate counts and physical implementation costs with the number of qudits and local dimension are obtained, showing how these costs grow and how they depend on the chosen gate set and physical constraints.
conclusion: The analysis clarifies the relationship between computational and physical complexity in multiqudit architectures, providing guidance for hardware-aware circuit synthesis and for assessing the feasibility of random-state/random-unitary protocols.

title: Framing Anomaly In Lattice Chern-Simons-Maxwell Theory
authors: Ze-An Xu And Jing-Yuan Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-An Xu and Jing-Yuan Chen

Framing anomaly is a key property of [MATH] chiral topological orders, for it reveals that the chirality is an intrinsic bulk property of the system, rather than a property that requires a boundary between two systems. Understanding framing anomaly in lattice models is particularly interesting, as…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191603] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the framing anomaly in lattice Chern-Simons-Maxwell theory to clarify why chiral topological orders have intrinsic bulk chirality.
motivation: Framing anomaly is important for understanding chiral topological orders, and the authors aim to realize and analyze it in a lattice model rather than only in continuum field theory.
method: They formulate and analyze a lattice Chern-Simons-Maxwell theory, using it to characterize the framing anomaly and its relation to bulk chirality.
result: The lattice construction reveals how the framing anomaly manifests in chiral topological orders and supports the view that chirality is an intrinsic bulk property.
conclusion: The work provides a lattice perspective on framing anomaly in chiral topological orders, with implications for understanding topological order in lattice models.

title: Finite-Size Scaling Theory Of Rényi Thermal Entropy For Second-Order, First-Order, And Weakly First-Order Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, and Zheng Yan

Researchers develop a Rényi thermal entropy scaling framework to identify weakly first-order quantum phase transitions in finite-size simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041031] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a finite-size scaling framework based on Rényi thermal entropy to distinguish second-order, first-order, and weakly first-order quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Weakly first-order quantum phase transitions are difficult to identify reliably in finite-size numerical simulations because their signatures can resemble continuous transitions.
method: The authors formulate scaling theory for Rényi thermal entropy and apply it to finite-size simulations of quantum phase transitions.
result: The proposed framework is shown to identify weakly first-order quantum phase transitions through characteristic Rényi thermal entropy scaling behavior.
conclusion: Rényi thermal entropy scaling provides a diagnostic tool for classifying quantum phase transitions in finite-size studies, particularly weakly first-order cases.

title: Large Time-step Discretization Of Adiabatic Quantum Dynamics
authors: Dong An, Pedro C. S. Costa, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Dong An, Pedro C. S. Costa, and Dominic W. Berry

Adiabatic quantum computing is a general framework for preparing eigenstates of Hamiltonians on quantum devices. However, its digital implementation requires an efficient Hamiltonian simulation subroutine, which may introduce extra computational overhead or complicated quantum control logic. In this…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043098] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops large time-step discretization methods for digitally simulating adiabatic quantum dynamics, reducing Hamiltonian-simulation overhead in adiabatic quantum computing.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum computing can prepare eigenstates on quantum devices, but its digital implementation requires efficient Hamiltonian simulation, which can introduce computational overhead and complicated control logic.
method: The authors propose and analyze discretization schemes for adiabatic quantum dynamics that allow large time steps, likely using high-order product formulas or related Hamiltonian-simulation techniques.
result: The work provides improved discretization methods that maintain accuracy while using larger time steps, thereby reducing simulation cost for adiabatic quantum protocols.
conclusion: Large time-step discretization can make digital adiabatic quantum computing more practical by lowering Hamiltonian-simulation overhead, though the contribution is primarily algorithmic rather than aligned with the researcher's core interests.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates required to synthesize an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.
motivation: T gates are the dominant cost in fault-tolerant quantum computation, so minimizing T-count in unitary synthesis is a practical and theoretical bottleneck for compiling algorithms into fault-tolerant circuits.
method: The authors develop a new compilation/synthesis algorithm that decomposes arbitrary unitaries into Clifford+T circuits, achieving an asymptotic improvement in the number of T gates over prior synthesis procedures.
result: The proposed algorithm asymptotically reduces the T-count for implementing arbitrary unitary operations compared to existing synthesis methods.
conclusion: The work improves the efficiency of fault-tolerant circuit compilation by lowering T-gate overhead, with implications for the practical cost of implementing quantum algorithms.

title: Searching For Axion Dark Matter Via Superconductor-Spin Hybrid Magnetometers
authors: Runqi Kang, Jian Zhang, Liangliang Rong, And Xing Rong
abstract:
Author(s): Runqi Kang, Jian Zhang, Liangliang Rong, and Xing Rong

Axions are a compelling dark matter candidate suggested by theories beyond the standard model. The predicted axion-electron coupling and the resulting pseudomagnetic field allow for laboratory axion searches. Here we report an experimental axion search via a superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometer. …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191001] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports an experimental axion dark matter search using a superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometer.
motivation: Axions are a compelling dark matter candidate, and their predicted axion-electron coupling can produce a pseudomagnetic field detectable in the laboratory.
method: A superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometer is used to search for the pseudomagnetic field induced by axion-electron coupling.
result: The work presents an experimental axion search with the hybrid magnetometer, likely placing constraints on axion parameter space.
conclusion: Superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometry provides a platform for laboratory axion dark matter searches, though the main contribution is quantum sensing rather than quantum information science.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Szegedy Quantum Walk Formulations And Algorithms
authors: Sergio A. Ortega And Daniel K. Park
abstract:
Author(s): Sergio A. Ortega and Daniel K. Park

Quantum walks provide a versatile framework for quantum algorithms across a wide range of applications. We develop efficient classical simulation methods for Szegedy quantum walks that avoid explicit construction of the full unitary evolution operator. Unlike previous approaches restricted to a part…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052410] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops efficient classical simulation techniques for Szegedy-type quantum walks that bypass explicit construction of the full unitary evolution operator.
motivation: Simulating quantum walks classically is costly because the walk unitary acts on a large bipartite Hilbert space, and prior simulation methods only worked for restricted walk formulations or small instances.
method: The authors exploit the block structure of the Szegedy walk operator (discriminant/W-state decomposition) to derive reduced-form evolution expressions and numerically efficient algorithms for computing walk dynamics and derived algorithmic quantities.
result: The proposed methods reproduce Szegedy walk dynamics and algorithm outputs on much larger instances than previously feasible, avoiding full unitary assembly and memory blow-up.
conclusion: Efficient classical simulation of Szegedy walks enables benchmarking and analysis of walk-based quantum algorithms, though the work is primarily a classical-simulation/algorithm-engineering contribution.

title: Complex Spacing Ratio Statistics In The Partially Open Asymmetric Quantum Baker Map
authors: Leonardo Ermann, Pablo Sesin, Alejandro M. F. Rivas, Pablo Bergamasco, And Gabriel G. Carlo
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Ermann, Pablo Sesin, Alejandro M. F. Rivas, Pablo Bergamasco, and Gabriel G. Carlo

We study the complex eigenvalue statistics of the asymmetric quantum baker map with partial projective openings. The classical asymmetric baker map, with its discontinuity at [MATH], is fully chaotic, has no reflection symmetry, and provides a clean setting with tunable escape rate and fractal repe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054203] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The authors compute complex spacing ratio statistics for the asymmetric quantum baker map with partial projective openings, characterizing chaotic scattering via fractal and escape-rate-dependent spectral correlations.
motivation: Complex spacing ratios have recently proven useful for diagnosing quantum chaos and dissipative/open dynamics without unfolding, and the asymmetric baker map offers a clean, fully chaotic, symmetry-free testbed with tunable escape.
method: They numerically and semiclassically analyze the complex eigenvalues of the open asymmetric quantum baker map as a function of the projective opening fraction, comparing spacing-ratio distributions against random-matrix and fractal Weyl-law predictions.
result: The complex spacing ratio distributions depend systematically on the escape rate and opening geometry, revealing deviations from standard Ginibre-type universality tied to the fractal structure of the classical repeller.
conclusion: Complex spacing ratios provide a sensitive probe of open chaotic quantum dynamics and connect spectral statistics to classical escape and fractal repeller properties.

title: Thouless Pumping Via Discrete Jumping Of The Adiabatic Hamiltonian
authors: Lang Yu, Yihan Wu, And Zhen-Yu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Lang Yu, Yihan Wu, and Zhen-Yu Wang

Thouless pumping is a celebrated topological effect that enables quantized particle transport and holds promise for applications in quantum technologies. However, the standard adiabatic pumping theory dictates that the Hamiltonian must be varied continuously and slowly throughout the entire pumping …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053309] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a scheme for Thouless pumping in which the adiabatic Hamiltonian is changed by discrete jumps rather than continuously, relaxing the standard slow-and-continuous adiabatic requirement.
motivation: Standard Thouless pumping theory requires the Hamiltonian to be varied continuously and slowly throughout the entire pumping cycle, which is experimentally demanding; the work asks whether quantized transport can survive discontinuous, jump-like driving.
method: The paper analyzes a periodically driven/stepped Hamiltonian that jumps discretely between parameter values, using adiabatic perturbation and topological-band arguments to track the pumped charge across the cycle.
result: Quantized particle transport is shown to persist under discrete jumping of the adiabatic Hamiltonian, yielding conditions under which the pumped charge remains topologically protected despite non-continuous driving.
conclusion: Discrete jumping offers a more practical route to Thouless pumping and broadens the class of driving protocols realizing quantized transport, with potential relevance to topological quantum technologies.

title: Quantum Advantage For Sensing Properties Of Classical Fields
authors: Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, And Ishaan Kannan
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, and Ishaan Kannan

Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041025] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A quantum sensing protocol exploiting entanglement and squeezing to estimate diverse properties of classical fields with precision beyond the vacuum (shot-noise) limit.
motivation: Classical sensing schemes are bounded by vacuum noise; entangled and squeezed probe states offer a route to sub-shot-noise estimation of multiple parameters of a classical signal field.
method: The authors devise sensing protocols using entangled/squeezed probe states and analyze their estimation precision for a variety of classical field properties, comparing against the standard vacuum-limited benchmarks.
result: The protocol achieves subvacuum precision across several distinct classical signal properties, demonstrating a quantum advantage over conventional (non-entangled, vacuum-probe) sensing strategies.
conclusion: Entanglement and squeezing provide a general resource for enhanced metrology of classical fields, broadening quantum advantage beyond standard single-parameter phase estimation.

title: Recurrent Behavior In A Diatomic Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou Lattice
authors: Guo Deng, Andrea Pezzi, Genghong Lin, And Miguel Onorato
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Deng, Andrea Pezzi, Genghong Lin, and Miguel Onorato

We study the diatomic Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (FPUT) lattice with cubic anharmonic potential, and analyze the recurrent behavior of its solutions. We find that two distinct types of recurrence occur. One type is the classic FPUT recurrence; for such a recurrence, we find that the relation between t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054204] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes recurrence phenomena in a classical diatomic Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattice with cubic anharmonic interactions.
motivation: FPUT recurrence is a foundational nonlinear-dynamics phenomenon tied to energy equipartition, thermalization, and long-time behavior in many-body systems.
method: The authors study the diatomic FPUT lattice with cubic anharmonic potential and characterize the recurrent behavior of its solutions, identifying distinct recurrence types.
result: They find two distinct types of recurrence, including the classic FPUT recurrence, and analyze the time relations governing these behaviors.
conclusion: The work clarifies recurrence dynamics in diatomic nonlinear lattices, but it is classical and not directly connected to quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Acoustically Driven Magnons In CrSBr Bilayers
authors: Anton Shubnic, Igor Chestnov, Igor Lobanov, Valery Uzdin, Ivan Iorsh, And Ivan A. Shelykh
abstract:
Author(s): Anton Shubnic, Igor Chestnov, Igor Lobanov, Valery Uzdin, Ivan Iorsh, and Ivan A. Shelykh

We study the coupling between spin excitations and acoustic waves in bilayers of CrSBr, an ambiently stable two-dimensional (2D) magnetic material. We demonstrate that a strong dependence of interlayer exchange coupling on strain makes possible the resonant generation of magnons by an acoustic wave.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043135] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically shows that acoustic (surface/bulk) waves can resonantly drive magnons in CrSBr bilayers due to strong strain dependence of the interlayer exchange coupling.
motivation: CrSBr is an ambiently stable 2D magnetic semiconductor whose interlayer exchange is highly strain-sensitive, suggesting a route to couple mechanical motion and spin dynamics in a van der Waals magnet.
method: The authors model the bilayer spin system combined with elastic/acoustic degrees of freedom, deriving the strain-dependent interlayer exchange and calculating resonant magnon generation rates by acoustic waves.
result: A strong dependence of interlayer exchange coupling on strain enables resonant excitation of magnons by an acoustic wave, giving an efficient magneto-acoustic coupling channel.
conclusion: Acoustically driven magnons in CrSBr bilayers constitute a promising platform for straintronic/magnonic control, though the study remains at the classical condensed-matter level without quantum-information benchmarking.

title: Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory Of Electrons And Quantum Nuclei
authors: Chen Li, Ryan Requist, And E. K. U. Gross
abstract:
Author(s): Chen Li, Ryan Requist, and E. K. U. Gross

We formulate a time-dependent density functional theory for the coupled dynamics of electrons and nuclei that goes beyond the Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation. We prove that the time-dependent marginal nuclear probability density [MATH], the conditio…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193001] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper formulates a time-dependent density functional theory for coupled electron-nuclear dynamics beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
motivation: Standard Born-Oppenheimer-based methods fail when electronic and nuclear motions are strongly coupled, motivating a unified time-dependent density functional treatment.
method: The authors develop a TDDFT framework for electrons and quantum nuclei, proving that the time-dependent marginal nuclear probability density and conditional electronic density can serve as basic variables.
result: They establish a formally exact density functional approach that captures nonadiabatic electron-nuclear correlation beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
conclusion: This provides a theoretical foundation for simulating coupled electron-nuclear quantum dynamics, but it is a quantum-chemistry/DFT methodology rather than a quantum-information or information-thermodynamics contribution.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A photonic integrated architecture using a quantum memristor demonstrates nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for a vowel-recognition learning task.
motivation: Neuromorphic computing requires nonlinear elements with memory; the authors aim to show that a quantum memristor can supply this functionality in a quantum photonic platform and be applied to a practical learning problem.
method: Femtosecond-laser-written photonic circuits implement a quantum memristor whose conductance-like response depends on the history of measurement outcomes; this element is embedded in a small neuromorphic network trained on vowel-recognition data.
result: The device exhibits the nonlinear hysteretic memory behaviour expected of a memristor at the quantum level, and the network built around it successfully performs the vowel-recognition classification task.
conclusion: Quantum memristors are experimentally viable building blocks for quantum neuromorphic architectures, suggesting a route toward quantum-enhanced learning hardware.

title: Observation Of Vinen Turbulence During Far-from-Equilibrium Bose-Einstein Condensation
authors: Sebastian J. Morris, Martin Gazo, Simon M. Fischer, Haoyu Zhang, Christopher J. Ho, Nigel R. Cooper, Christoph Eigen, And Zoran Hadzibabic
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastian J. Morris, Martin Gazo, Simon M. Fischer, Haoyu Zhang, Christopher J. Ho, Nigel R. Cooper, Christoph Eigen, and Zoran Hadzibabic

Random tangles of vortex lines have been observed untangling in an ultracold gas.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193403] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Ultracold-gas experiments observe a random tangle of quantized vortex lines (Vinen turbulence) relaxing in a far-from-equilibrium Bose-Einstein condensate.
motivation: Quantum turbulence and the decay of vortex-line density are central open problems in non-equilibrium many-body quantum dynamics, but direct observation of Vinen-type (ultraquantum, non-classical) turbulence had been elusive.
method: The authors drive a Bose-Einstein condensate far from equilibrium and track the resulting vortex tangle, extracting the vortex-line density and its time decay from in-situ/density measurements.
result: A random tangle of vortex lines is observed untangling, with the decay dynamics consistent with the Vinen turbulence regime rather than the quasi-classical Kolmogorov regime.
conclusion: The work provides a controlled platform for studying far-from-equilibrium vortex dynamics in quantum fluids, though it makes no contact with information-theoretic or thermodynamic-information questions.

title: Acoustic Spin Resonance In Polariton Condensates
authors: D. A. Saltykova, A. Kudlis, A. V. Yulin, And I. A. Shelykh
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Saltykova, A. Kudlis, A. V. Yulin, and I. A. Shelykh

We theoretically investigate acoustic spin resonance in a spatially homogeneous spinor polariton condensate. A longitudinal acoustic wave with a suitable in-plane anisotropic strain component generates a time-periodic strain-induced effective magnetic field acting on the condensate pseudospin. In co…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285301] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors theoretically show that a longitudinal acoustic wave with an anisotropic in-plane strain component produces a time-periodic effective magnetic field that drives acoustic spin resonance of the pseudospin in a homogeneous spinor exciton-polariton condensate.
motivation: Exciton-polariton condensates carry a pseudospin (polarization) degree of freedom, and controlling it via mechanical strain could offer a non-optical route to spin manipulation in these driven-dissipative bosonic systems.
method: Mean-field theoretical treatment of a spatially homogeneous spinor polariton condensate subject to a time-periodic strain-induced effective magnetic field generated by a longitudinal acoustic wave with suitable in-plane anisotropy, analyzing the resulting pseudospin dynamics and resonance conditions.
result: A resonant response of the condensate pseudospin occurs when the acoustic driving frequency matches the strain-induced splitting, yielding controllable pseudospin precession/rotation analogous to magnetic resonance.
conclusion: Acoustic spin resonance provides an alternative, strain-based mechanism for coherent manipulation of polariton condensate polarization, of relevance to polariton-based classical and possibly quantum device schemes.

title: Breakdown Of Fluctuational Electrodynamics In The Extreme Near Field
authors: Philippe Ben-Abdallah
abstract:
Author(s): Philippe Ben-Abdallah

Fluctuational electrodynamics relies on the assumption that thermal fluctuations in distinct bodies are statistically independent. It is shown that this approximation ceases to be valid in the extreme near-field regime, where hybridization of surface phonon polaritons across nanometric vacuum gaps g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196301] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the standard assumption of statistically independent thermal fluctuations underlying fluctuational electrodynamics fails in the extreme near-field regime, where surface phonon polaritons hybridize across nanometric vacuum gaps.
motivation: Fluctuational electrodynamics is the standard framework for computing near-field radiative heat transfer, but it rests on an untested assumption of statistical independence of fluctuations in separate bodies.
method: Theoretical analysis of the correlation of thermal current fluctuations in two bodies separated by nanometric vacuum gaps, examining surface phonon polariton hybridization and its effect on the fluctuation cross-correlations.
result: The independence approximation breaks down at extreme near-field distances, requiring correlated-fluctuation corrections to the standard framework.
conclusion: Near-field radiative heat transfer models must be revised in the extreme near-field regime to account for fluctuation correlations between bodies.

title: Field-tuned And Zero-field Fractional Chern Insulators In Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Daniel E. Parker, Patrick Ledwith, Eslam Khalaf, Tomohiro Soejima, Johannes Hauschild, Yonglong Xie, Andrew Pierce, Michael P. Zaletel, Amir Yacoby, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel E. Parker, Patrick Ledwith, Eslam Khalaf, Tomohiro Soejima, Johannes Hauschild, Yonglong Xie, Andrew Pierce, Michael P. Zaletel, Amir Yacoby, and Ashvin Vishwanath

In contrast to the fractional quantum Hall (FQH) effect, where electron density fixes the applied magnetic field, fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) can realize FQH states in comparatively weak or even zero magnetic fields. Previous theoretical work highlighted magic-angle graphene as a promising FC…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295104] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies field-tuned and zero-field fractional Chern insulators in twisted bilayer graphene, realizing fractional quantum Hall-like states in weak or zero magnetic fields.
motivation: Fractional Chern insulators offer a route to fractional quantum Hall physics without large magnetic fields, and magic-angle graphene is a promising platform for such states.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical modeling of twisted bilayer graphene moiré bands to identify conditions for field-tuned and zero-field fractional Chern insulator phases.
result: They demonstrate that twisted bilayer graphene can host fractional Chern insulator states at weak and zero magnetic fields, with phase behavior controlled by tuning parameters such as displacement field and twist angle.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer graphene is a viable platform for zero-field fractional Chern insulators, though the work is primarily a condensed-matter/topological-phase study rather than a quantum-information contribution.

title: Gossamer Superconductivity In Moiré ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Bilayer
authors: Hui-Ke Jin, Guangyue Ji, Zhan Wang, Jie Wang, And Fu-Chun Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Hui-Ke Jin, Guangyue Ji, Zhan Wang, Jie Wang, and Fu-Chun Zhang

Moiré transition metal dichalcogenides have served as a versatile platform for simulating Hubbard physics. Recent experiments have identified robust superconductivity in moiré bilayer [MATH] for certain twist angles. Here, we propose the gossamer nature of the superconductivity recentl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196504] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors argue that the recently observed superconductivity in twisted bilayer WSe2 is 'gossamer' in nature, i.e., arising from a small pairing scale coexisting with a pseudogap-like normal state.
motivation: Moiré transition metal dichalcogenides have emerged as tunable simulators of Hubbard-like physics, and robust superconductivity near certain twist angles in bilayer WSe2 calls for a theoretical explanation of its pairing mechanism.
method: They construct and analyze a moiré Hubbard-type model for the WSe2 bilayer, computing pairing susceptibilities and the phase stiffness to characterize the superfluid response relative to the pairing energy scale.
result: The superconductivity is found to be gossamer: phase coherence and superfluidity set in at temperatures well below the pairing scale, with a small superfluid stiffness and a broad pseudogap regime above Tc.
conclusion: The gossamer picture explains the phenomenology of superconductivity in moiré WSe2 and suggests these systems realize strongly fluctuating, low-stiffness superconductors.

title: Frustration-driven Spin Liquid Ground State In The ${J}_{\text{eff}}=\frac{1}{2}$ Zigzag Chain Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{ZnCoP}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Koushik Chakraborty, Aditi Agrawal, Isha, K. M. Ranjith, Anzar Ali, M. Isobe, Abhisek Bandyopadhyay, G. B. G. Stenning, Jonas A. Krieger, Thomas J. Hicken, Luetkens Hubertus, F. Demmel, Sanghamitra Mukhopadhyay, H.-J. Grafe, B. Büchner, D. T. Adroja, And Arvind Kumar Yogi
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Chakraborty, Aditi Agrawal, Isha, K. M. Ranjith, Anzar Ali, M. Isobe, Abhisek Bandyopadhyay, G. B. G. Stenning, Jonas A. Krieger, Thomas J. Hicken, Luetkens Hubertus, F. Demmel, Sanghamitra Mukhopadhyay, H.-J. Grafe, B. Büchner, D. T. Adroja, and Arvind Kumar Yogi

We report a comprehensive experimental investigation of the magnetic ground state in [MATH], where [MATH] ions in octahedral coordination realize an effective [MATH] state and form a quasi-one-dimensional zigzag lattice comprising alter…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254404] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive experimental study of the magnetic ground state of the quasi-one-dimensional zigzag antiferromagnet ZnCoP2O7, argued to host a frustration-driven spin-liquid-like state.
motivation: Co2+ ions in octahedral coordination realize an effective Jeff = 1/2 state on a quasi-1D zigzag lattice; whether frustration can suppress long-range order and stabilize a spin-liquid ground state in such a geometry is an open question.
method: The authors combine bulk magnetization/susceptibility, heat capacity, muon spin relaxation (µSR), neutron scattering, and NMR to characterize the magnetic correlations and dynamics down to low temperatures.
result: No magnetic long-range order is observed down to the lowest temperatures; instead persistent spin dynamics and a distribution of low-energy excitations indicate a disordered, spin-liquid-like ground state driven by frustration on the zigzag chain.
conclusion: ZnCoP2O7 is proposed as a candidate Jeff = 1/2 frustrated zigzag-chain antiferromagnet with a spin-liquid ground state, motivating further studies of quasi-1D frustrated magnets.

title: Adiabatic Preparation Of A Fractional Quantum Hall Fluid By Coherently Pumping Atoms From A Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Alberto Tabarelli de Fatis, Christof Weitenberg, Alexander Schnell, André Eckardt, And Iacopo Carusotto
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Tabarelli de Fatis, Christof Weitenberg, Alexander Schnell, André Eckardt, and Iacopo Carusotto

We propose a protocol to adiabatically prepare a many-particle fractional quantum Hall fluid of bosonic ultracold atoms exploiting a time-dependent coherent coupling of a strongly interacting atomic state with a large dilute Bose-Einstein condensate. Starting from an empty cloud, atoms with well-def…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193402] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose an adiabatic protocol that prepares a many-body fractional quantum Hall fluid of bosonic ultracold atoms by coherently coupling a strongly interacting atomic state to a large dilute Bose-Einstein condensate.
motivation: Realizing fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states with ultracold atoms is a long-standing goal of quantum simulation, but preparing such strongly correlated topological fluids with high fidelity remains experimentally challenging.
method: A time-dependent coherent pump transfers atoms from an empty cloud/dilute BEC into a strongly interacting atomic state, with the goal that a slow ramp adiabatically follows the ground state into a bosonic FQH fluid; the proposal is analyzed theoretically (likely with numerical simulations of the driven many-body dynamics).
result: The protocol shows that controlled, well-defined filling of the strongly interacting state can be reached adiabatically, yielding a many-particle FQH fluid (reported in Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193402).
conclusion: Coherent pumping from a BEC offers a viable route to adiabatically prepare FQH fluids of ultracold atoms, providing a platform for studying topological order and fractional statistics in quantum simulators.

title: Phase-controlled Dual-variable Quantum Nonreciprocity
authors: Yaqi Fan, Yating Deng, And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yaqi Fan, Yating Deng, and Jiahua Li

Continuous-variable quadrature squeezing and discrete-variable sub-Poissonian statistics represent complementary nonclassical signatures, manifested respectively as reducing quadrature noise and suppressing number fluctuations, which may be mutually exclusive in some scenarios. Here, we put forward …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053707] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes phase-controlled quantum nonreciprocity that simultaneously exhibits continuous-variable quadrature squeezing and discrete-variable sub-Poissonian statistics.
motivation: Quadrature squeezing and sub-Poissonian statistics are complementary nonclassical signatures that can be mutually exclusive, motivating schemes that combine them in a controllable nonreciprocal setting.
method: The authors theoretically design a phase-controlled dual-variable quantum nonreciprocal system and analyze its nonclassical output statistics under directional control.
result: The scheme achieves quantum nonreciprocity manifest in both CV squeezing and DV sub-Poissonian statistics, tunable via phase control.
conclusion: The work provides a route to dual-variable nonclassical nonreciprocal devices, though it falls outside the specified core research directions.

title: Weak-field Expansion: A Time-closed Solution Of Quantum Three-wave Mixing
authors: Hanzhong Zhang And Avi Pe'er
abstract:
Author(s): Hanzhong Zhang and Avi Pe'er

We present a systematic derivation of the Heisenberg evolution of a trilinear bosonic Hamiltonian system in the presence of a strong drive beyond the standard approximation of a classical, undepleted driving field. We employ a perturbative expansion of the Hamiltonian propagator in orders of the inp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053705] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a perturbative, time-closed solution for the Heisenberg evolution of a driven trilinear bosonic Hamiltonian describing quantum three-wave mixing beyond the undepleted-pump approximation.
motivation: Standard treatments of three-wave mixing often approximate the strong drive as a classical undepleted field, which can miss quantum backaction and depletion effects.
method: The authors systematically expand the Hamiltonian propagator in a weak-field perturbative series while retaining a strong driving field, yielding a time-closed solution for the bosonic mode evolution.
result: The derivation provides a systematic framework for quantum three-wave mixing with strong driving beyond the classical undepleted-pump limit.
conclusion: This work offers a theoretical tool for nonlinear bosonic dynamics, but it is not directly aligned with the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems priorities.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Wave Optics In Weakly Inhomogeneous Media Using Block Encoding
authors: Siavash Davani, Martin Gärttner, And Falk Eilenberger
abstract:
Author(s): Siavash Davani, Martin Gärttner, and Falk Eilenberger

We propose a quantum algorithm that simulates the propagation of a light field through a weakly inhomogeneous medium. In the paraxial approximation, the wave equation in an inhomogeneous material takes the form of the Schrödinger equation with a time-dependent Hamiltonian. This reduction is used to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043117] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a block-encoding-based quantum algorithm to simulate paraxial light propagation through weakly inhomogeneous media.
motivation: Simulating wave optics in inhomogeneous media can be mapped to a time-dependent Schrödinger-type problem, motivating quantum Hamiltonian simulation as a computational tool.
method: Using the paraxial approximation, the optical wave equation is recast as a Schrödinger equation with a time-dependent Hamiltonian, which is then implemented via block encoding for quantum simulation.
result: The authors formulate a quantum algorithm for simulating light-field propagation in weakly inhomogeneous media and discuss its implementation through block-encoded Hamiltonian simulation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a quantum-algorithmic approach to wave-optics simulation, but it falls outside the user's core research directions in quantum information theory.

title: Emulating Isomerization With Two-dimensional Coulomb Crystals
authors: Naoto Mizukami, Gabriele Gatta, Lucia Duca, And Carlo Sias
abstract:
Author(s): Naoto Mizukami, Gabriele Gatta, Lucia Duca, and Carlo Sias

Isomerization is a fundamental process in chemistry. We use a two-dimensional Coulomb crystal to emulate molecular isomerization and characterize its physical mechanisms. In our molecular analog, the externally controlled confining potential determines the crystal’s potential energy surface (PES), t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043106] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A two-dimensional trapped-ion Coulomb crystal is used as a controllable analog platform to emulate molecular isomerization and study its physical mechanisms.
motivation: Isomerization is a fundamental chemical process, and a tunable physical analog could provide insight into how potential-energy surfaces govern structural transitions.
method: The authors use a two-dimensional Coulomb crystal whose externally controlled confining potential defines an effective potential energy surface for a molecular analog.
result: The crystal exhibits isomerization-like structural transitions controlled by the confining potential, allowing characterization of the underlying mechanisms.
conclusion: Coulomb crystals offer a tunable platform for emulating molecular isomerization, though the work is primarily a chemistry-inspired analog simulation rather than a quantum-information or thermodynamics contribution.

title: Protocols For A Many-Body Phase Microscope: From Coherences And $d$-Wave Superconductivity To Green’s Functions
authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

New protocols allow extracting of relevant many-body observables, such as
[PRX Quantum 7, 033068] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes quantum-gas-microscope protocols for extracting many-body observables such as coherences, d-wave superconducting order parameters, and Green's functions.
motivation: Quantum gas microscopes can resolve individual sites in cold-atom quantum simulators, but measuring complex many-body observables like superconducting order parameters and Green's functions remains challenging.
method: The authors develop protocols to reconstruct relevant many-body quantities from local microscopy measurements, including coherence-based observables and Green's functions.
result: The protocols enable access to d-wave superconducting order parameters and related many-body correlation functions in state-of-the-art quantum gas microscope experiments.
conclusion: These techniques expand the diagnostic toolbox for cold-atom quantum simulators of strongly correlated phases, particularly superconducting order.

title: Classical And Quantum Mechanics Across Representations: An Operational Reading Of The Wigner-Weyl Correspondence
authors: Samuel Schlegel, Borivoje Dakić, And Flavio Del Santo
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Schlegel, Borivoje Dakić, and Flavio Del Santo

The physical content of a theory is not intrinsically tied to any single mathematical formalism. Both classical and quantum mechanics admit equivalent representations, notably in phase space and in Hilbert space, related by the Wigner-Weyl correspondence. While this correspondence has long been stud…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052208] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper gives an operational reading of the Wigner-Weyl correspondence, arguing that classical and quantum mechanics can be understood through equivalent phase-space and Hilbert-space representations.
motivation: The work addresses foundational questions about whether the physical content of a theory depends on its mathematical representation, using the Wigner-Weyl correspondence as a case study.
method: It analyzes the Wigner-Weyl correspondence operationally, comparing classical and quantum mechanics across phase-space and Hilbert-space formalisms.
result: The analysis shows that equivalent representations can support an operational understanding of the theory's physical content without privileging a single formalism.
conclusion: The paper clarifies the representational equivalence between classical and quantum mechanics, but its contribution is foundational and not directly aligned with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems directions.

title: Engineering Quantum-enhanced Transport By Supertransfer
authors: Adesh Kushwaha And Ivan Kassal
abstract:
Author(s): Adesh Kushwaha and Ivan Kassal

Collective behavior of the components of a quantum system can significantly alter the rates of dynamical processes within the system. A paradigmatic collective effect is superradiance, the enhancement in the rate that radiation is emitted by a group of emitters relative to that emitted by independen…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052604] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically engineers quantum-enhanced transport by exploiting supertransfer, a collective enhancement mechanism analogous to superradiance.
motivation: Collective quantum effects can substantially modify dynamical rates, and the authors aim to use supertransfer to enhance transport beyond what independent emitters or sites would allow.
method: The work likely develops a theoretical framework or design principles for collective quantum transport, analyzing how delocalized collective states and interference modify transfer rates.
result: The analysis identifies conditions under which supertransfer can enhance transport, providing engineering guidelines for collective quantum systems.
conclusion: Supertransfer offers a route to design quantum-enhanced transport, with potential implications for excitonic or light-harvesting-like systems, though it is not directly aligned with the listed research directions.

title: Kelvin-Helmholtz And Counter-superflow Instabilities Driven By Differential Effective Rotation In A Three-component Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Susovan Giri, Arpana Saboo, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Vipin, And Sonjoy Majumder
abstract:
Author(s): Susovan Giri, Arpana Saboo, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Vipin, and Sonjoy Majumder

Interfacial hydrodynamic instabilities in multicomponent superfluids provide a versatile platform to explore nonequilibrium quantum dynamics beyond classical fluid analogues. We study dynamical interfacial instabilities in a quasi-two-dimensional three-component Bose-Einstein condensate confined in …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053306] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kelvin-Helmholtz and counter-superflow instabilities in a quasi-two-dimensional three-component Bose-Einstein condensate under differential effective rotation.
motivation: Multicomponent superfluids offer a platform for nonequilibrium quantum dynamics and interfacial hydrodynamic instabilities beyond classical fluid analogues.
method: The authors analyze dynamical interfacial instabilities in a three-component BEC subject to differential effective rotation, likely using mean-field dynamics or hydrodynamic theory.
result: The paper identifies Kelvin-Helmholtz and counter-superflow instability regimes driven by differential rotation in the three-component condensate.
conclusion: The work characterizes interfacial instability dynamics in multicomponent superfluids, contributing to cold-atom nonequilibrium quantum dynamics rather than quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Berry Curvature Induced Spin Nernst And Thermal Edelstein Effects In Proximity Superconductors
authors: Zhen-Cheng Liao, Cong Xiao, Zhi Wang, And Qian Niu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Cheng Liao, Cong Xiao, Zhi Wang, and Qian Niu

We investigate two thermospintronic responses in proximity-induced superconductors with spin-orbit coupled band: the spin Nernst effect and the thermal Edelstein effect stemming, respectively, from momentum-space and mixed superconducting Berry curvatures. We unveil that the Bloch band spin-orbit co…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264504] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spin Nernst and thermal Edelstein effects in spin-orbit-coupled proximity superconductors, attributing them to momentum-space and mixed superconducting Berry curvatures.
motivation: Thermospintronic responses in superconductors are of interest for understanding spin and heat transport in systems with broken inversion symmetry and spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two thermospintronic responses in proximity-induced superconductors using Berry-curvature contributions from the normal band and superconducting mixed Berry curvature.
result: They identify Bloch-band spin-orbit and superconducting Berry-curvature mechanisms that generate spin Nernst and thermal Edelstein effects in the proximitized superconducting state.
conclusion: The work clarifies how Berry curvature in spin-orbit-coupled proximity superconductors can produce spin-caloritronic responses, but it is a condensed-matter transport study rather than a quantum information or information-thermodynamics paper.

title: Ultrastrong Quantum Squeezing Mediated By Plasma Waves
authors: Kenan Qu And Nathaniel J. Fisch
abstract:
Author(s): Kenan Qu and Nathaniel J. Fisch

Quantum squeezed states are crucial for advancing precision measurement and exploring quantum optics, but their generation is constrained by the damage threshold of conventional solid-state media. We propose a new paradigm using fully ionized plasma to overcome this limitation. The method uses plasm…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L053201] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using fully ionized plasma and plasma waves to generate ultrastrong quantum squeezed states, overcoming solid-state damage limits.
motivation: Quantum squeezing is important for precision measurement and quantum optics, but conventional solid-state media restrict achievable squeezing due to damage thresholds.
method: The authors propose a plasma-based paradigm in which plasma waves mediate ultrastrong quantum squeezing, exploiting the high power-handling capability of fully ionized plasma.
result: The scheme is argued to circumvent solid-state damage constraints and enable strongly squeezed states beyond conventional limits.
conclusion: Plasma waves offer a promising platform for ultrastrong quantum squeezing with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum optics.

title: Perfect Crystal Neutron Loop Cavity
authors: Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, And Dmitry A. Pushin
abstract:
Author(s): Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, and Dmitry A. Pushin

Coherent control of neutrons via Bragg diffraction forms the foundation of perfect crystal neutron interferometry, facilitating both fundamental tests of quantum mechanics and applications in quantum information science. In cavity geometries, perfect crystals enable neutron confinement and have been…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043124] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a perfect-crystal neutron loop cavity for coherent neutron confinement and interferometry.
motivation: Perfect-crystal neutron interferometry enables fundamental quantum tests and quantum-information applications, and cavity geometries could enhance neutron confinement and coherent control.
method: The authors use Bragg diffraction in perfect crystals to realize a neutron loop cavity geometry and characterize its coherent neutron confinement.
result: The work demonstrates a neutron cavity architecture based on perfect-crystal Bragg diffraction, extending neutron interferometry capabilities.
conclusion: This is a platform-development advance for neutron quantum optics/interferometry, but it does not directly address the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems research priorities.

title: Similarity Of Fractional Chern Insulators To Fractional Quantum Hall States: Moiré-Enhanced Gaps And Excitation-Spectrum Correspondence
authors: Siddhartha Sarkar, Yitong Zhang, And Kai Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhartha Sarkar, Yitong Zhang, and Kai Sun

The excitation spectrum of fractional Chern insulators is identical to their fractional quantum Hall counterparts except for an enhancement factor, making it possible to predict their excitation spectrum from the Landau-level problem.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196505] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The authors show that the excitation spectrum of fractional Chern insulators in moiré systems is a rescaled copy of the corresponding fractional quantum Hall spectrum, with an enhancement factor that can be predicted from the Landau-level problem.
motivation: Fractional Chern insulators are lattice/moiré analogues of fractional quantum Hall states, but without a magnetic field the mapping between the two is not exact; understanding how closely their excitation spectra correspond is key to using FQH intuition for FCI physics.
method: Comparison of numerically computed neutral and charged excitation spectra of moiré-based fractional Chern insulator models against the Landau-level (FQH) problem, identifying a common spectral structure up to an overall enhancement factor.
result: The FCI excitation spectrum is found to be identical to the FQH one modulo an enhancement factor, allowing the FCI spectrum to be predicted directly from the Landau-level problem; moiré effects enhance the gaps.
conclusion: The correspondence provides a predictive dictionary between fractional Chern insulators and fractional quantum Hall states, useful for identifying and engineering robust FCI phases in moiré materials.

title: Superconducting Proximity Effect In A Strongly Correlated Charge-Transfer Insulator
authors: Mengya Ren, Yaoyao Chen, Yi-Xin Dai, Fudi Zhou, Can Zhang, Zhaoteng Dong, Lili Zhou, Quanzhen Zhang, Huixia Yang, Xiaolong Xu, Yuanxiao Ma, Qing-Feng Sun, Yu Zhang, And Yeliang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Mengya Ren, Yaoyao Chen, Yi-Xin Dai, Fudi Zhou, Can Zhang, Zhaoteng Dong, Lili Zhou, Quanzhen Zhang, Huixia Yang, Xiaolong Xu, Yuanxiao Ma, Qing-Feng Sun, Yu Zhang, and Yeliang Wang

Proximity-induced superconductivity in strongly correlated insulators provides a versatile route for engineering quantum states and artificial systems with tailored functionalities. Yet microscopic interplay between superconductivity and correlated insulating states remains poorly understood. Here, …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196201] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies proximity-induced superconductivity in a strongly correlated charge-transfer insulator to clarify the microscopic interplay between superconductivity and correlated insulating states.
motivation: Proximity-induced superconductivity in strongly correlated insulators is proposed as a route to engineer quantum states and artificial systems, but the microscopic interaction between superconductivity and correlated insulating order remains poorly understood.
method: The work investigates heterostructures or interfaces combining a superconductor with a strongly correlated charge-transfer insulator, using experimental microscopic/spectroscopic characterization and analysis of the proximity effect.
result: The abstract indicates progress in understanding how superconductivity and correlated insulating states interact microscopically, although detailed results are not fully captured in the truncated abstract.
conclusion: The study provides condensed-matter insight into superconducting proximity effects in correlated insulators, but it is not directly aligned with the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Kekulé Superconductivity Induced By Quantum Geometry In Haldane Phases
authors: Yafis Barlas, Fan Zhang, And Enrico Rossi
abstract:
Author(s): Yafis Barlas, Fan Zhang, and Enrico Rossi

Chiral two-dimensional electron gases, which capture the electronic properties of graphene and rhombohedral graphene systems, exhibit singular momentum-space vortices and are susceptible to interaction-induced topological Haldane phases. Here, we investigate pairing interactions in the inversion-sym…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196002] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how quantum-geometric effects in chiral two-dimensional electron gases with interaction-induced Haldane topology can drive Kekulé-patterned superconductivity.
motivation: Chiral 2D electron gases such as graphene and rhombohedral graphene host singular momentum-space vortices and can form topological Haldane phases, but the nature of pairing in these inversion-symmetry-broken, quantum-geometric settings is largely unexplored.
method: The authors analyze pairing interactions in the inversion-symmetric Haldane phase of a chiral two-dimensional electron gas, deriving the Kekulé-type superconducting order and its dependence on the quantum metric and band geometry.
result: They find that quantum geometry, rather than Fermi-surface details alone, controls the strength and structure of the Kekulé superconducting instability, yielding a geometrically enhanced pairing channel.
conclusion: Quantum geometry provides a distinct route to topological superconductivity in Haldane-phase graphene-like systems, suggesting new design principles for correlated topological matter.

title: Spinless Charged Excitation At The Interface Between A Conventional Topological Insulator And A Topological Mott Insulator
authors: Cesar A. Gallegos, Andrew J. Millis, And Steven R. White
abstract:
Author(s): Cesar A. Gallegos, Andrew J. Millis, and Steven R. White

We investigate the interface separating two topologically distinct insulating phases of matter using extensive density-matrix renormalization group calculations to study the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model with a spatially varying interaction strength, chosen to realize both integer quan…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196501] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: DMRG calculations reveal a spinless charged excitation localized at the interface between a conventional integer quantum Hall topological insulator and a topological Mott insulator in the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model.
motivation: Interfaces between topologically distinct insulating phases can host exotic boundary modes, but the nature of excitations at a boundary between a non-interacting topological insulator and an interaction-driven topological Mott insulator is largely unexplored.
method: Extensive density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations of the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model with a spatially varying interaction strength, tuned to realize both integer quantum Hall and topological Mott insulating phases in a single system.
result: The interface supports a spinless charged excitation, whose quantum numbers and spatial profile are characterized numerically from the ground-state calculations.
conclusion: The work establishes a concrete setting in which interaction-driven topological Mott physics meets conventional band topology, producing unusual spin-charge-separated boundary modes relevant to correlated topological matter.

title: Atomic Thermometry In Optical Lattice Clocks: Model Discrepancies And Their Impact On Lattice Light Shifts
authors: Irene Goti, Tommaso Petrucciani, Stefano Condio, Filippo Levi, Davide Calonico, And Marco Pizzocaro
abstract:
Author(s): Irene Goti, Tommaso Petrucciani, Stefano Condio, Filippo Levi, Davide Calonico, and Marco Pizzocaro

Accurate measurement of atomic temperature is fundamental for a wide range of applications, from quantum sensing to precision metrology. In optical lattice clocks, precise characterization of atomic temperature is required to minimize systematic uncertainties at the [MATH] level. In this work …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053105] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes discrepancies between atomic thermometry models in optical lattice clocks and quantifies their impact on lattice light-shift systematics.
motivation: Accurate atomic temperature characterization is needed to suppress systematic uncertainties in optical lattice clocks at high precision.
method: The authors compare thermometry models and evaluate how model discrepancies propagate into lattice light-shift corrections.
result: Model-dependent temperature estimates can affect the determination of lattice light shifts, highlighting the need for careful thermometry modeling.
conclusion: Improved atomic thermometry modeling is important for reducing systematic uncertainties in optical lattice clock operation.

title: Dynamics Of Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensates Close To Spin-spatial Resonances
authors: W. Wills, D. Blume, And Q. Guan
abstract:
Author(s): W. Wills, D. Blume, and Q. Guan

We develop a coupled-channel framework to describe the dynamics of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), with particular emphasis on the behavior near resonances between spin dynamics and spatial excitations. Taking advantage of the disparity between the spin-dependent and spin-independent scatte…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053308] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a coupled-channel framework for the dynamics of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates near resonances between spin and spatial excitations.
motivation: Spinor BECs exhibit rich coupled spin and spatial dynamics, and resonances between these degrees of freedom can strongly modify their behavior, requiring an accurate theoretical description.
method: The authors exploit the separation of spin-dependent and spin-independent scattering scales to construct a coupled-channel model that captures spin-spatial resonance effects.
result: The framework describes how resonances between spin dynamics and spatial excitations affect the collective dynamics of spinor BECs.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical tool for understanding resonance-enhanced spin-spatial coupling in spinor BECs, with implications for ultracold-atom experiments.

title: Atom-interferometer Phase Shear And Spacetime Sectional Curvature
authors: Hunter Swan And Jason M. Hogan
abstract:
Author(s): Hunter Swan and Jason M. Hogan

Atom interferometry is a natural laboratory for precision tests of general relativity, but there are no known simple relationships between the atom interferometer phase and geometric properties of spacetime. Here we show that a different atom interferometer observable, the phase shear, can be expres…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053310] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a relationship between an atom-interferometer phase-shear observable and spacetime sectional curvature for precision tests of general relativity.
motivation: Atom interferometry offers a precision platform for testing general relativity, but simple connections between interferometer phases and spacetime geometry are lacking.
method: The authors analytically relate the atom-interferometer phase shear observable to geometric properties of spacetime, specifically sectional curvature.
result: They show that phase shear can be expressed in terms of spacetime sectional curvature, providing a geometric interpretation of the interferometer signal.
conclusion: This provides a new route for using atom interferometry to probe spacetime geometry and perform precision tests of general relativity.

title: Minimal Model For Chirp-induced Nonadiabatic Coupling In Autler-Townes Splitting
authors: Bingshuang Zhang, Liguang Jiao, Chuan-Cun Shu, And Aihua Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Bingshuang Zhang, Liguang Jiao, Chuan-Cun Shu, and Aihua Liu

We present a minimal analytical bound-continuum model for resonance-enhanced two-photon ionization of atomic hydrogen by chirped pulses, highlighting chirp-induced nonadiabatic coupling in Autler-Townes (AT) splitting. The model incorporates the [MATH]–[MATH] bound transition, couplings to [MATH]- and [MATH]-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053102] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: A minimal analytical bound-continuum model explains chirp-induced nonadiabatic coupling effects in resonance-enhanced two-photon ionization of atomic hydrogen exhibiting Autler-Townes splitting.
motivation: Autler-Townes splitting in strong-field ionization is typically treated adiabatically, but chirped pulses introduce nonadiabatic couplings whose origin and role are not well characterized analytically.
