method: The authors construct a minimal analytical model of a bound-continuum system for atomic hydrogen driven by chirped pulses, including the 1s-2p bound transition and couplings to continuum states, and solve for the resulting photoelectron/ionization dynamics.
result: The model reproduces the Autler-Townes split resonance structure and shows that chirp-induced nonadiabatic coupling qualitatively modifies the doublet, providing closed-form expressions for the split line positions and intensities.
conclusion: Chirp-induced nonadiabatic coupling is an essential ingredient in interpreting Autler-Townes splitting in two-photon ionization, and the minimal model offers a tractable analytic tool for coherent-control spectroscopy.

title: Metric Structures Characterized By Norm Properties In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Xin Wang, Hao-Di Liu, And Libin Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Wang, Hao-Di Liu, and Libin Fu

For non-Hermitian quantum systems, metric operators provide a way to define the corresponding inner-product structures. In the entirely real-spectrum regime, a positive-definite metric [MATH] can be introduced such that the Hamiltonian is [MATH]-self-adjoint with respect to the corresponding inner product…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052201] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes metric structures in non-Hermitian quantum systems through norm properties and positive-definite metric operators.
motivation: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with real spectra require a positive-definite metric to define a consistent inner product and self-adjointness structure.
method: It analyzes norm properties to characterize metric operators and the conditions under which a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian is self-adjoint with respect to the associated inner product.
result: The authors identify metric structures that are determined by norm properties in the real-spectrum non-Hermitian regime.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical framework for consistent inner-product structures in non-Hermitian quantum systems, but it is not directly aligned with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems research directions.

title: Spin Filtering By Electron Reflection From Surfaces Of Collinear Compensated Magnets
authors: E. E. Krasovskii And A. N. Yaresko
abstract:
Author(s): E. E. Krasovskii and A. N. Yaresko

Spin-dependent reflection of very low energy electrons from the surfaces of antiferromagnetic NiO and altermagnetic MnTe is studied within a Bloch-waves scattering theory. Significant spin polarization is observed both at normal and at off-normal incidence comparable to that in reflection from ferro…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274411] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A Bloch-wave scattering-theory study showing that very-low-energy electrons reflected from antiferromagnetic NiO and altermagnetic MnTe surfaces acquire substantial spin polarization at both normal and off-normal incidence.
motivation: Spin-dependent electron reflection offers a route to spin filtering without ferromagnets, and compensated magnets such as antiferromagnets and altermagnets are attractive because they produce no stray field.
method: Spin-polarized low-energy electron reflection from NiO and MnTe surfaces is computed within a Bloch-waves scattering theory, evaluating the induced spin polarization of the reflected beam versus incidence angle and energy.
result: Significant spin polarization of reflected electrons is found for both collinear compensated magnets at normal and off-normal incidence, comparable to values obtained from ferromagnetic reflectors.
conclusion: Compensated magnetic surfaces can act as efficient spin filters for low-energy electrons, with potential use in spin-polarized electron sources and spintronic devices.

title: Electrostatic Control Enables Robust Helical Edge-channel Transport In Iii-v Quantum Spin Hall Insulators
authors: Manuel Meyer, Tobias Fähndrich, Sebastian Schmid, Justus Walter, Martin Kamp, Adriana Wolf, Sergey Krishtopenko, Guillaume Sigu, Jean-Baptiste Rodriguez, Eric Tournié, Gérald Bastard, Frédéric Teppe, Fabian Hartmann, Sven Höfling, And Benoit Jouault
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel Meyer, Tobias Fähndrich, Sebastian Schmid, Justus Walter, Martin Kamp, Adriana Wolf, Sergey Krishtopenko, Guillaume Sigu, Jean-Baptiste Rodriguez, Eric Tournié, Gérald Bastard, Frédéric Teppe, Fabian Hartmann, Sven Höfling, and Benoit Jouault

Quantum spin Hall transport in InAs/GaInSb-based two-dimensional topological insulators can be limited by parasitic bulk and edge contributions. We demonstrate that these limitations are effectively mitigated through electrostatic control in dual-gated InAs/GaInSb/InAs trilayer quantum wells grown o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305302] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Electrostatic control in dual-gated InAs/GaInSb quantum wells mitigates parasitic bulk and edge contributions, enabling robust helical edge-channel transport in III-V quantum spin Hall insulators.
motivation: Quantum spin Hall transport in InAs/GaInSb-based two-dimensional topological insulators is often limited by unwanted bulk conduction and parasitic edge effects.
method: The authors use dual-gated InAs/GaInSb/InAs trilayer quantum wells grown by molecular beam epitaxy and apply electrostatic gating to tune the transport regime.
result: The dual-gate control effectively suppresses parasitic contributions and allows observation of robust helical edge-channel transport.
conclusion: Electrostatic control is a viable route to improve quantum spin Hall transport in III-V topological insulator quantum wells.

title: Twinkling Bloch Oscillation In anti-Hermitian Lattices
authors: Xiling Feng, Zhan Liu, Kuoxi Zhang, Shuaishuai Tong, Qicheng Zhang, And Chunyin Qiu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiling Feng, Zhan Liu, Kuoxi Zhang, Shuaishuai Tong, Qicheng Zhang, and Chunyin Qiu

Bloch oscillation (BO)—the oscillatory electron motion in a field-driven periodic lattice—is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum transport. While well established in Hermitian systems, it remains largely unexplored in non-Hermitian settings (especially in experiments). Here, we report distinctive wa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260301] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports distinctive 'twinkling' Bloch oscillation dynamics in anti-Hermitian periodic lattices, extending a fundamental quantum transport phenomenon into the non-Hermitian regime.
motivation: Bloch oscillations are well understood in Hermitian systems but remain largely unexplored in non-Hermitian settings, particularly experimentally.
method: The authors study field-driven wave-packet dynamics in anti-Hermitian lattices, likely combining theoretical analysis with an experimental platform.
result: They observe twinkling Bloch-oscillation behavior that differs qualitatively from conventional Hermitian Bloch oscillations.
conclusion: The work establishes Bloch oscillations in anti-Hermitian lattices and highlights non-Hermiticity as a route to novel quantum transport dynamics.

title: Path To Superconductivity Via Strong Short-range Repulsion In A Spin-polarized Band
authors: Zhiyu Dong And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyu Dong and Patrick A. Lee

We predict that the spin-polarized electrons in a two-dimensional triangular lattice with strong electron-electron repulsion give rise to [MATH]-wave pairing. The key point is that the first-order interaction, which is usually pair breaking, vanishes or nearly vanishes in certain [MATH]-wave channels due …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254504] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The authors predict that spin-polarized electrons on a two-dimensional triangular lattice with strong short-range Coulomb repulsion can form a chiral d+id-wave superconducting state because first-order pair-breaking interactions vanish in certain d-wave channels.
motivation: Strong short-range repulsion normally suppresses Cooper pairing, so identifying conditions under which it instead enables superconductivity is a central problem in correlated-electron physics.
method: Analytical treatment of the effective pairing interaction for a spin-polarized band on a triangular lattice, evaluating first- and higher-order diagrams in various d-wave channels to find where pair breaking cancels.
result: The first-order repulsive interaction vanishes or nearly vanishes for specific d-wave channels, opening a window for d+id-wave pairing in the spin-polarized triangular lattice.
conclusion: Strong short-range repulsion in a spin-polarized triangular band offers a viable route to unconventional chiral superconductivity, with implications for candidate materials and moiré platforms.

title: On-chip Detection Of Anisotropic Thermopolarization In Quartz
authors: Shuichi Iwakiri, Yasumitsu Miyata, And Takao Mori
abstract:
Author(s): Shuichi Iwakiri, Yasumitsu Miyata, and Takao Mori

Temperature gradients are widely used to drive and probe transport phenomena in solids, forming the basis of heat-to-charge conversion processes. In typical experiments, local heating is introduced to generate a temperature gradient, and the resulting electrical response is detected by separate elec…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043115] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate on-chip electrical detection of anisotropic thermopolarization (the Seebeck-like charge response to a temperature gradient) in quartz crystals, resolving the effect's directional dependence in a single device.
motivation: Heat-to-charge conversion in solids is usually probed by applying local heating and detecting the resulting voltage with separate electrodes, which convolves the intrinsic material response with device geometry and contact effects. A cleaner, geometry-controlled measurement of anisotropic thermoelectric response is therefore desirable.
method: A microfabricated on-chip platform is used to impose a controlled temperature gradient on quartz while electrodes patterned along different crystallographic directions record the thermovoltage, allowing the angular anisotropy of the thermopolarization to be extracted without changing the sample.
result: The measured thermopolarization signal varies strongly and reproducibly with the direction of the applied thermal gradient relative to the crystal axes, confirming a pronounced anisotropic thermoelectric response in quartz.
conclusion: The on-chip scheme provides a general route to characterizing anisotropic thermal-to-electrical conversion in dielectric crystals, with implications for thermoelectric and pyroelectric device design.

title: Imaginary-time-enhanced Feedback-based Quantum Algorithms For Ground-state Preparation
authors: Thanh Nguyen van Long, Lan Nguyen Tran, And Le Bin Ho
abstract:
Author(s): Thanh Nguyen Van Long, Lan Nguyen Tran, and Le Bin Ho

Preparing ground states of strongly correlated quantum systems is a central goal in quantum simulation and optimization. The feedback-based quantum algorithm (FALQON) provides an attractive alternative to variational methods with a fully quantum feedback rule, but it fails in the presence of spectra…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043121] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an imaginary-time-enhanced feedback-based quantum algorithm for preparing ground states of strongly correlated quantum systems.
motivation: Ground-state preparation is central to quantum simulation and optimization, and existing feedback-based algorithms such as FALQON can fail for certain spectra.
method: The authors enhance the feedback-based quantum algorithm FALQON by incorporating imaginary-time evolution ideas to improve ground-state preparation.
result: The proposed approach is presented as an improved algorithm for ground-state preparation, addressing limitations of FALQON in the presence of challenging spectra.
conclusion: Imaginary-time-enhanced feedback control offers a promising quantum-algorithmic route for ground-state preparation, though it falls outside the researcher's core quantum-information, thermodynamics, network, and hybrid-system interests.

title: Nonclassical Cutoff Fluctuations In Squeezed-light-driven High-harmonic Generation
authors: Tsendsuren Khurelbaatar, R. T. Sang, And Igor V. Litvinyuk
abstract:
Author(s): Tsendsuren Khurelbaatar, R. T. Sang, and Igor V. Litvinyuk

In the conventional description of strong-field high-harmonic generation (HHG), the atom is treated quantum mechanically while the driving laser is represented by a classical field. Quantum fluctuations of the driver can become relevant in nanoscale interaction geometries, where tight spatial confin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043107] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how quantum (nonclassical) fluctuations of a squeezed driving laser imprint themselves on the cutoff region of high-harmonic generation, going beyond the standard semi-classical treatment that uses a classical driver field.
motivation: In conventional strong-field HHG the atom is quantized but the driving laser is treated classically; in nanoscale, tightly confined geometries the quantum fluctuations of the driver can become non-negligible, motivating a fully quantum treatment of the driving field.
method: The authors model HHG driven by squeezed light and analyze the statistics of the cutoff harmonic fluctuations, comparing them with those obtained for a coherent/classical driver.
result: Squeezed-light driving produces cutoff fluctuations whose character (e.g. reduced or modified variance) departs from the classical-driver prediction, revealing a nonclassical signature in the high-harmonic spectrum.
conclusion: Nonclassical driver fluctuations constitute an observable knob on HHG cutoff statistics, suggesting squeezed light as a tool for probing and controlling strong-field dynamics in confined geometries.

title: Scattering Zones In Quantum Speckle Propagation
authors: Shaurya Aarav, S. A. Wadood, And Jason W. Fleischer
abstract:
Author(s): Shaurya Aarav, S. A. Wadood, and Jason W. Fleischer

Quantum speckles exhibit significantly richer behavior than their classical counterparts due to their higher dimensionality. A simple example is the far-field speckle pattern in one-dimensional (1D) light scattering: Classical light forms 1D speckles defined by the numerical aperture, whereas biphot…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043113] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum speckle formation and propagation in scattering, contrasting biphoton speckle behavior with classical speckles.
motivation: Quantum speckles are expected to show richer spatial structure than classical speckles because photon-pair correlations add higher-dimensional degrees of freedom.
method: The authors analyze far-field speckle patterns from one-dimensional light scattering, comparing classical speckles constrained by numerical aperture with biphoton speckle patterns.
result: Quantum speckle propagation reveals additional scattering zones and correlation structure not captured by classical speckle theory.
conclusion: The work characterizes quantum optical speckle phenomena, but it does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Analytic Phase Solution And Point Vortex Model For Dipolar Quantum Vortices
authors: Ryan Doran And Thomas Bland
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Doran and Thomas Bland

An analytic expression is derived for the phase of a quantum vortex in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate, capturing the anisotropy introduced by the long-range dipole-dipole interactions. Using this phase profile, the dipolar point vortex model is formulated; this model reproduces the anisotropic velocities, deformed orbits, and orientation-dependent motion of vortex pairs found in full numerical simulations of the condensate.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042014] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an analytic phase profile for quantum vortices in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates and uses it to formulate a dipolar point vortex model.
motivation: Dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates feature anisotropic long-range interactions, so standard vortex descriptions need to be extended to capture dipole-induced anisotropy.
method: An analytic expression for the vortex phase is derived, and a point vortex model incorporating dipolar effects is constructed and compared with full numerical simulations.
result: The model reproduces anisotropic vortex velocities, deformed pair orbits, and orientation-dependent vortex-pair motion observed in simulations.
conclusion: The analytic phase solution and dipolar point vortex model provide a useful reduced description of vortex dynamics in dipolar condensates.

title: Trainable, Self-verifying Variational Quantum Eigensolver Using Adiabatic Warm Starts
authors: Bojan Žunkovič, Marco Ballarin, Lewis Wright, And Michael Lubasch
abstract:
Author(s): Bojan Žunkovič, Marco Ballarin, Lewis Wright, and Michael Lubasch

A study looks at the conditions under which an adiabatic variational quantum eigensolver succeeds, where approximate ground states generated along an adiabatic path serve as initial states for successive optimization steps. A self-verification procedure based on energy-standard-deviation measurements is introduced that assesses eigenstate accuracy during run-time and verifies convergence to the target ground state.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042013] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies an adiabatic warm-start variational quantum eigensolver with a runtime self-verification procedure based on energy-standard-deviation measurements.
motivation: Variational quantum eigensolvers can suffer from optimization and convergence issues, so reliable initialization and verification of ground-state convergence are important for practical quantum algorithms.
method: Approximate ground states generated along an adiabatic path are used as initial states for successive VQE optimization steps, and energy-standard-deviation measurements are used to self-verify eigenstate accuracy during the run.
result: The authors identify conditions under which the adiabatic warm-start VQE succeeds and show that the proposed self-verification can assess convergence to the target ground state at runtime.
conclusion: The approach provides a trainable and self-verifying VQE strategy, but the work is primarily a quantum-algorithm/quantum-chemistry simulation contribution rather than a match to the specified research directions.

title: Incoherent Imaging With Spatially Structured Quantum Probes
authors: Anthony J. Brady, Zihao Gong, Alexey V. Gorshkov, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Anthony J. Brady, Zihao Gong, Alexey V. Gorshkov, and Saikat Guha

Researchers introduce spatially structured quantum-optical imaging techniques to overcome resolution limits and achieve quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041030] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces spatially structured quantum-optical probes for incoherent imaging to overcome resolution limits in absorption and fluorescence imaging.
motivation: Incoherent imaging modalities such as absorption and fluorescence face resolution limits that may be overcome using quantum-enhanced probe states.
method: The authors use spatially structured quantum-optical probes to improve imaging performance in incoherent imaging scenarios.
result: They demonstrate quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence imaging with the proposed structured quantum probes.
conclusion: Spatially structured quantum probes can enhance resolution and performance in incoherent quantum imaging applications.

title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy For Near-Integrable Dynamics
authors: Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, And Jacopo de Nardis
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, and Jacopo De Nardis

The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041021] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors generalize the BBGKY hierarchy to near-integrable many-body systems with strong contact and long-range two-body interactions, enabling computation of measurable expectation values and correlations.
motivation: Standard BBGKY hierarchies are poorly suited to near-integrable dynamics, where strong integrable contact interactions coexist with generic long-range couplings and conventional kinetic theory fails.
method: They extend the BBGKY hierarchy by incorporating integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body terms, yielding a systematic framework for classical and quantum correlation dynamics.
result: The generalized hierarchy provides a practical route to experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations in near-integrable systems.
conclusion: This work offers a theoretical tool for nonequilibrium many-body dynamics, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined here.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework treats quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors to show how angular-momentum-dependent lattice geometries generate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated pyrochlore magnets.
motivation: Quadrupolar order and spin-liquid physics on frustrated lattices are poorly captured by standard pseudospin-1/2 semiclassical pictures, motivating a geometric description of quadrupolar degrees of freedom.
method: Quantum quadrupoles are modeled as biaxial tensors within a semiclassical framework, and the resulting angular-momentum-dependent geometries on the pyrochlore lattice are analyzed for their allowed ordered and disordered phases.
result: The approach reproduces generalized nematic phases and identifies regimes supporting quadrupolar spin liquids, showing that the local angular-momentum geometry dictates the phase behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a unified geometric language for frustrated quadrupolar magnetism and predicts exotic nematic and spin-liquid states, but remains a condensed-matter magnetism study without direct quantum-information or thermodynamic implications.

title: Pauli Propagation Enables Fast Classical Simulation Of Strongly Correlated Quantum Systems
authors: Chinmay Shrikhande, Arnab Bachhar, José Aarón Rodríguez-Jiménez, Edward F. Valeev, And Nicholas J. Mayhall
abstract:
Author(s): Chinmay Shrikhande, Arnab Bachhar, José Aarón Rodríguez-Jiménez, Edward F. Valeev, and Nicholas J. Mayhall

A variational double bracket flow algorithm leveraging Pauli propagation efficiently estimates ground-state energies in strongly correlated systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043022] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational double-bracket flow algorithm using Pauli propagation is introduced to efficiently estimate ground-state energies of strongly correlated quantum systems on classical computers.
motivation: Strongly correlated electronic systems are hard to simulate classically, and existing Pauli-based methods face unfavorable scaling; the authors seek a faster classical route to ground-state energies.
method: The work combines a variational double-bracket flow ansatz with Pauli propagation to iteratively minimize energy and truncate operator growth in the Pauli basis.
result: The approach yields efficient ground-state energy estimates for strongly correlated systems, presumably outperforming comparable classical simulation techniques on benchmark problems.
conclusion: Pauli propagation with double-bracket flow offers a practical classical algorithm for strongly correlated quantum many-body and quantum-chemistry problems.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A resource analysis of a fault-tolerant end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics, quantifying bottlenecks and the achievable (bounded) quantum speedup.
motivation: Nonlinear fluid simulations are classically expensive, so the authors ask whether fault-tolerant quantum computers can offer a genuine end-to-end advantage once state preparation, nonlinearity handling, and readout costs are included.
method: The authors construct a full quantum algorithmic pipeline for nonlinear fluid equations and perform a gate/resource-count analysis under fault-tolerant assumptions to locate dominant costs.
result: They derive explicit resource scalings and identify the regimes where a bounded quantum advantage over classical solvers can be claimed, along with the bottlenecks that limit it.
conclusion: Quantum speedups for nonlinear fluid dynamics exist but are constrained; careful end-to-end accounting is essential before claiming practical advantage.

title: Breathing Mode Of Quantum Droplets In Dipolar Quantum Gases: A Sum-rule Analysis
authors: Xinran Zhang, Junli Liu, Huiyun Xiao, Xiao-Long Chen, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xinran Zhang, Junli Liu, Huiyun Xiao, Xiao-Long Chen, and Yunbo Zhang

We investigate theoretically the ground-state properties and breathing-mode collective excitations of three-dimensional dipolar Bose gases in anisotropic harmonic traps incorporating quantum fluctuations. Combining a Gaussian variational ansatz with a sum-rule analysis, we derive explicit analytical…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053307] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies ground-state properties and breathing-mode excitations of three-dimensional dipolar Bose gases with quantum fluctuations in anisotropic harmonic traps.
motivation: Dipolar quantum droplets and their collective excitations are interesting many-body phenomena arising from the interplay of dipole-dipole interactions, quantum fluctuations, and trap anisotropy.
method: The authors combine a Gaussian variational ansatz with a sum-rule analysis to derive analytical results for the ground state and breathing modes.
result: They obtain explicit analytical expressions for the breathing-mode frequency and analyze how dipolar interactions and quantum fluctuations affect the mode in anisotropic traps.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into collective excitations of dipolar quantum droplets, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Susceptibility-driven Mott Criticality In The Two-component Bose-Hubbard Model With Local Rabi Coupling
authors: Tomasz Polak
abstract:
Author(s): Tomasz Polak

We investigate the Mott-superfluid transition in a two-component Bose-Hubbard model with local Rabi coupling, focusing on the asymmetric regime where interaction, hopping, and chemical-potential imbalances compete with coherent interconversion. We show that the transition is governed by the softenin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274504] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the Mott-superfluid transition in a two-component Bose-Hubbard model with local Rabi coupling, identifying a susceptibility-driven critical mechanism in the asymmetric regime.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how interaction, hopping, and chemical-potential imbalances compete with coherent interconversion in a two-component lattice boson system.
method: They analyze the two-component Bose-Hubbard model with local Rabi coupling, focusing on the softening of a susceptibility mode to characterize the Mott-superfluid transition.
result: The transition is shown to be governed by susceptibility softening, revealing critical behavior driven by the interplay of asymmetry and Rabi coupling.
conclusion: The work clarifies the criticality of the Mott-superfluid transition in asymmetric two-component Bose-Hubbard models with local interconversion, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platform characterization.

title: Observation Of Rabi-oscillation-driven Cyclical Noise Squeezing In Active Quantum Dot Ensembles
authors: Ori Gabai, Amnon Willinger, Igor Khanonkin, Vitalii Sichkovskyi, Johann Peter Reithmaier, And Gadi Eisenstein
abstract:
Author(s): Ori Gabai, Amnon Willinger, Igor Khanonkin, Vitalii Sichkovskyi, Johann Peter Reithmaier, and Gadi Eisenstein

Squeezed light is usually generated using parametric processes in various nonlinear materials. Semiconductor lasers and optical amplifiers (SOAs) also offer nonlinearities, but they differ in that they add amplified spontaneous emission originating from population inversion, which represents a therm…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043131] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports observations of cyclical noise squeezing in active quantum-dot ensembles, driven by Rabi oscillations, in a semiconductor optical amplifier/laser setting.
motivation: Squeezed light is typically produced by parametric nonlinear processes, but active semiconductor gain media introduce amplified spontaneous emission and thermal-like noise, motivating study of whether nonclassical noise reduction can persist in such systems.
method: The authors experimentally characterize noise squeezing in active quantum-dot ensembles, likely using noise-spectrum or correlation measurements while varying operating conditions to connect the observed cyclical behavior with Rabi oscillations.
result: They observe cyclical noise squeezing in the active quantum-dot ensemble, indicating that the squeezing is modulated by Rabi-oscillation dynamics in the gain medium.
conclusion: The work identifies a Rabi-oscillation-driven mechanism for cyclical noise squeezing in active quantum-dot gain media, broadening the contexts in which squeezed light can be generated but remaining primarily a semiconductor laser/amplifier physics result.

title: Magnon Superlattices Around Skyrmions In Frustrated Magnets
authors: Adarsh Hullahalli, Christos Panagopoulos, And Christina Psaroudaki
abstract:
Author(s): Adarsh Hullahalli, Christos Panagopoulos, and Christina Psaroudaki

Dynamic magnetic textures provide a versatile platform for controlling magnon states in spintronic systems. Here, we identify a class of crystal-like dynamical magnon patterns in centrosymmetric frustrated magnets. Their periodicity originates from the interference of symmetry-related finite-wave-ve…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043116] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies crystal-like dynamical magnon superlattice patterns arising around skyrmions in centrosymmetric frustrated magnets due to interference of finite-wave-vector modes.
motivation: Dynamic magnetic textures such as skyrmions offer a platform for controlling magnon states in spintronic systems, motivating the search for periodic magnon patterns that could enable magnon manipulation.
method: The authors analyze magnon dynamics in frustrated centrosymmetric magnets, focusing on interference of symmetry-related finite-wave-vector magnon modes around skyrmion textures.
result: They find a class of periodic magnon superlattice patterns whose periodicity emerges from mode interference around skyrmions.
conclusion: These magnon superlattices provide a route to controlling magnon states via skyrmion textures in frustrated magnetic systems.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Their Thermodynamic Fate In Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
authors: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, And Haruki Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, and Haruki Watanabe

A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041016] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of arbitrary-spin classical pyrochlore spin ice shows that spin-3/2 magnets can exhibit an abrupt transition between two spin-liquid states that survives thermal fluctuations, unlike other transitions that become crossovers.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a general framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice and clarify which topological phase transitions remain sharp at finite temperature versus being washed out into crossovers.
method: They construct and analyze a theoretical model of classical pyrochlore spin ice for general spin S, identifying spin-liquid states and studying their thermodynamic stability under thermal fluctuations.
result: They find that for S = 3/2 the system switches abruptly between two distinct spin-liquid states, and this transition survives thermal fluctuations, whereas all other transitions become crossovers.
conclusion: The work highlights a special thermodynamic robustness of a topological transition in spin-3/2 pyrochlore spin ice, distinguishing it from other cases where thermal fluctuations destroy sharp transitions.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A frustrated pyrochlore spin model is shown to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase and mixed magnetic orders due to thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries.
motivation: The paper studies how frustration and competing interactions in pyrochlore magnets can suppress conventional magnetic order and produce exotic nematic or mixed phases.
method: The authors analyze a frustrated pyrochlore spin model, likely using symmetry arguments and thermodynamic or mean-field/fluctuation-based techniques to identify stable phases.
result: Thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries are found to suppress conventional order and stabilize a magnetic nematic phase, with mixed magnetic phases appearing in parts of the phase diagram.
conclusion: The work clarifies how competing orders on the pyrochlore lattice can lead to nematic and mixed magnetic phases, offering insights into frustrated magnetism rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Diffusion And Singular Transport From Hydrodynamic Recoupling
authors: Ewan Mcculloch, Romain Vasseur, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Ewan McCulloch, Romain Vasseur, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

In charge neutral fluids, such as the Dirac fluid in graphene at the Dirac point, charge transport remains diffusive despite the presence of ballistically propagating sound waves: sound waves “hydrodynamically decouple” from the slower charge fluctuations. For quasi-one-dimensional charge neutral fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196304] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anomalous diffusion and singular charge transport arising from hydrodynamic recoupling in charge-neutral quasi-one-dimensional fluids.
motivation: Charge transport in neutral fluids such as graphene's Dirac fluid is usually diffusive even when sound modes propagate ballistically; the authors investigate when hydrodynamic coupling between sound and charge modes changes this picture.
method: The authors analyze hydrodynamic theories of charge-neutral quasi-one-dimensional fluids, focusing on recoupling between ballistic sound modes and slower charge fluctuations.
result: They identify regimes where hydrodynamic recoupling leads to anomalous diffusion and singular transport rather than conventional diffusive charge dynamics.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic mode coupling can qualitatively alter transport in neutral quantum fluids, producing anomalous scaling not captured by standard decoupled sound/charge descriptions.

title: Fate Of An Impurity Strongly Interacting With A Thermal Bose Gas
authors: Jiří Etrych, Sebastian J. Morris, Simon M. Fischer, Gevorg Martirosyan, Christopher J. Ho, Moritz Drescher, Manfred Salmhofer, Zoran Hadzibabic, Tilman Enss, And Christoph Eigen
abstract:
Author(s): Jiří Etrych, Sebastian J. Morris, Simon M. Fischer, Gevorg Martirosyan, Christopher J. Ho, Moritz Drescher, Manfred Salmhofer, Zoran Hadzibabic, Tilman Enss, and Christoph Eigen

We spectroscopically study mobile impurities immersed in a homogeneous bosonic bath (a box-trapped Bose gas), varying the bath temperature and the strength of impurity-bath interactions. We compare our results to those for a quasipure Bose-Einstein condensate, and find that for strong impurity-bath …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193405] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Spectroscopic study of mobile impurities strongly coupled to a homogeneous thermal Bose gas, mapping how temperature and impurity-bath interaction strength modify polaron-like quasiparticle properties.
motivation: Impurity physics in ultracold Bose gases (Bose polarons) has been extensively studied near zero temperature, but the fate of an impurity coupled strongly to a thermal, non-condensed bath remains poorly characterized experimentally.
method: The authors perform radio-frequency spectroscopy of impurities immersed in a box-trapped homogeneous Bose gas, varying bath temperature and interaction strength, and compare the thermal-bath spectra with those obtained in a quasipure Bose-Einstein condensate.
result: For strong impurity-bath interactions the spectral signatures deviate markedly from the condensate case, revealing how thermal excitations of the bath modify the impurity's energy spectrum and quasiparticle residue.
conclusion: The measurements provide benchmark data for theories of impurities in finite-temperature quantum gases and delineate the regime where condensate-based polaron descriptions break down.

title: Ultracold Three-body Recombination In Homonuclear Lithium And Sodium Systems
authors: Hiroya Suno
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroya Suno

We study ultracold three-body recombination of spin-polarized [MATH] and [MATH] atoms using realistic triplet diatomic interaction potentials. The three-body Schrödinger equation is solved in the [MATH] symmetry using the hybrid slow variable discretization–adiabatic hyperspher…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052806] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of ultracold three-body recombination rates for spin-polarized lithium and sodium atoms using realistic triplet interaction potentials.
motivation: Three-body recombination limits the lifetime of ultracold atomic gases and is important for understanding few-body collision dynamics in trapped atomic ensembles.
method: The three-body Schrödinger equation is solved in a given symmetry using the hybrid slow-variable-discretization–adiabatic-hyperspherical approach with realistic triplet diatomic potentials.
result: Recombination rates and scattering length dependence are computed for homonuclear Li and Na trimers, revealing the few-body resonance and threshold behavior characteristic of the Efimov-like ultracold regime.
conclusion: The results provide quantitative predictions for loss rates in ultracold Li and Na samples, useful for cold-atom experiments but not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Demonstration Of A Spherical Penning Trap For Single Electrons
authors: Zirui Fang And Xing Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Zirui Fang and Xing Fan

A spherical Penning trap has sparse, well-separated microwave resonances, making it attractive for precision measurements of the electron magnetic moment and for dark-photon and axion searches with trapped electrons. We demonstrate single-electron trapping in a spherical Penning trap and characteriz…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052805] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates single-electron trapping in a spherical Penning trap and characterizes its sparse microwave resonances for precision measurements.
motivation: A spherical Penning trap offers well-separated microwave resonances that are attractive for precision measurements of the electron magnetic moment and for dark-photon and axion searches.
method: The authors trap single electrons in a spherical Penning trap and characterize the trap's microwave resonance structure.
result: Single-electron trapping is demonstrated in the spherical geometry, enabling characterization of the trap's sparse microwave resonances.
conclusion: The platform is promising for precision electron magnetic moment measurements and fundamental physics searches, but it is not directly aimed at quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Superconducting Diode Effect In Magnetic Superconductors Realized By Nonreciprocal Domain-wall Dynamics
authors: Dong Hui Han, Suk Bum Chung, And Se Kwon Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Dong Hui Han, Suk Bum Chung, and Se Kwon Kim

The authors propose here a route to the superconducting diode effect through nonreciprocal magnetic domain-wall dynamics in ferromagnetic superconductors. Applied magnetic fields break time-reversal and inversion symmetries, producing direction-dependent critical currents for Walker breakdown—the onset of sustained domain-wall precession. Owing to the order parameter redundancy, the precession generates nonsingular phase slips. By connecting magnetic dynamics with superconducting transport, the authors identify a mechanism for realizing the superconducting diode effect without the need for complex heterostructures.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264410] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a mechanism for the superconducting diode effect in ferromagnetic superconductors based on nonreciprocal magnetic domain-wall dynamics and Walker breakdown.
motivation: Realizing the superconducting diode effect typically requires complex heterostructures or engineered asymmetry; the authors seek an intrinsic single-material route.
method: They combine magnetic domain-wall dynamics with superconducting transport theory, showing that applied fields break time-reversal and inversion symmetry and yield direction-dependent critical currents for Walker breakdown, producing nonsingular phase slips via order-parameter redundancy.
result: A direction-dependent critical current arises from nonreciprocal domain-wall precession, yielding a diode effect without heterostructures.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal domain-wall dynamics offers a viable intrinsic mechanism for superconducting diodes in magnetic superconductors.

title: Disorder Effects On The Anomalous Hall Conductivity Of A Two-dimensional Ferromagnetic Rashba Model
authors: Bing Liu, Hongchao Yang, Ye Yang, Xiaole Qiu, Lianzhen Cao, And Weiwei Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Bing Liu, Hongchao Yang, Ye Yang, Xiaole Qiu, Lianzhen Cao, and Weiwei Chen

The anomalous Hall conductivity of a ferromagnetic two-dimensional electron gas with a Rashba spin-orbit interaction is studied in the presence of Gaussian white noise. In this condition the anomalous Hall conductivity can be separated into two parts, intrinsic and side jump. The intrinsic contribut…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274410] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes how Gaussian white-noise disorder modifies the intrinsic and side-jump contributions to the anomalous Hall conductivity of a two-dimensional ferromagnetic electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Anomalous Hall transport in ferromagnetic Rashba systems is sensitive to spin-orbit coupling and impurity scattering, and a quantitative separation of intrinsic versus side-jump contributions in the presence of disorder is needed to interpret experiments.
method: Analytical transport theory for a ferromagnetic two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit interaction, treating Gaussian white-noise disorder and separating the conductivity into intrinsic and side-jump parts.
result: The disorder-averaged anomalous Hall conductivity is decomposed into intrinsic and side-jump terms, with their dependence on disorder strength and Rashba spin-orbit parameters characterized.
conclusion: Disorder qualitatively and quantitatively reshapes the anomalous Hall response of such Rashba ferromagnets, clarifying which contribution dominates in different regimes.

title: Tuning The Interlayer Electronic Coupling Of Twisted Bilayer Graphene By Pressure
authors: Yanlin Mou, Qiaoxia Xing, Xingding Li, Lei Mu, Boyang Yu, Yixuan Ma, Junwei Ma, Chenghao Pan, Quan Wan, Maoliang Li, Jihui Yang, Shenyang Huang, And Hugen Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Yanlin Mou, Qiaoxia Xing, Xingding Li, Lei Mu, Boyang Yu, Yixuan Ma, Junwei Ma, Chenghao Pan, Quan Wan, Maoliang Li, Jihui Yang, Shenyang Huang, and Hugen Yan

The interlayer electronic coupling in twisted bilayer graphene results in band anticrossing of the intersected Dirac cones. The shifts of the two new band extrema relative to the original intersection point are crucial for the electronic and optical properties. However, such shifts, particularly, th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291403] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Pressure is used to tune the interlayer electronic coupling and the resulting band anticrossing shifts in twisted bilayer graphene, probed optically.
motivation: The shifts of the two new band extrema relative to the Dirac cone intersection strongly affect the electronic and optical properties of twisted bilayer graphene, but these shifts had not been well characterized or controlled.
method: Infrared/optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer graphene under applied pressure, extracting the band anticrossing parameters and their pressure dependence.
result: The interlayer coupling and the band-extrema shifts vary systematically with pressure, providing a quantitative handle on the moiré band structure.
conclusion: Pressure offers an effective knob for engineering the interlayer electronic coupling and optical response of twisted bilayer graphene.

title: Chiral Vortical Effect And Boundary-induced Vortical Pumping In Finite Weyl Systems
authors: Boqun Song And Pavan Hosur
abstract:
Author(s): Boqun Song and Pavan Hosur

The chiral vortical effect (CVE)—an axial current driven by rotation in chiral matter—appears in systems ranging from relativistic fluids to Weyl semimetals. We present a quantum treatment of a rotating Weyl fermion in a finite cylinder that reproduces the on-axis current density obtained by Vilenki…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305104] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a quantum treatment of a rotating Weyl fermion in a finite cylinder that reproduces the chiral vortical effect's on-axis axial current density and reveals a boundary-induced vortical pumping contribution.
motivation: The chiral vortical effect — an axial current driven by rotation in chiral matter — is known from relativistic hydrodynamics and observed in Weyl semimetals, but its quantum-mechanical derivation in finite, bounded samples is incomplete.
method: A quantum-mechanical calculation of Weyl fermions on a finite cylinder subject to rotation, comparing the resulting current density with the semiclassical/field-theoretic CVE result and isolating geometry-dependent boundary contributions.
result: The quantum treatment reproduces the on-axis current density obtained in earlier field-theoretic treatments and identifies an additional boundary-induced vortical pumping effect arising from the finite sample geometry.
conclusion: Finite-size boundaries qualitatively modify vortical transport in Weyl systems, so the CVE in real semimetal samples must account for boundary-induced pumping beyond the bulk anomaly-based picture.

title: Quantitative Access To Inelastic Tunneling Channels From Plasmon-mediated Photon Emission
authors: Germar Hoffmann
abstract:
Author(s): Germar Hoffmann

Scanning tunneling microscope–induced light emission is an established technique for probing local electronic processes via optical spectroscopy. Local surface plasmons within the tunnel junction drive photon emission from metallic systems. Previous experimental and theoretical studies solidified ou…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305408] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a quantitative framework for extracting inelastic tunneling channels from plasmon-mediated light emission in scanning tunneling microscope junctions.
motivation: STM-induced light emission is used to probe local electronic processes, but disentangling the contributions of different inelastic tunneling channels from the plasmon-mediated emission signal remains difficult.
method: The author analyzes tunneling-junction plasmon-driven photon emission spectra, combining experimental signatures with theoretical modeling to quantify the relative weight of individual inelastic tunneling channels.
result: The analysis provides a quantitative route to assign and weight inelastic tunneling channels contributing to the measured emission, clarifying how plasmon modes mediate the photon yield.
conclusion: The approach improves the interpretability of STM-based optical spectroscopy for local electronic characterization of metallic systems.

title: Fluctuations In Aharonov-Bohm Electrodynamics
authors: F. O. Minotti And G. Modanese
abstract:
Author(s): F. O. Minotti and G. Modanese

We consider the application of the fluctuation dissipation theorem to the electrodynamics of Aharonov-Bohm, which differs from Maxwell's electrodynamics in that it allows for local nonconservation of charge. For the case of a system of nonconserved charges at thermal equilibrium we obtain the same s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054114] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to Aharonov-Bohm electrodynamics, which permits local charge nonconservation, and studies equilibrium fluctuations of nonconserved charges.
motivation: Aharonov-Bohm electrodynamics generalizes Maxwell theory by allowing local nonconservation of charge, so its fluctuation properties at thermal equilibrium are not automatically covered by standard Maxwell fluctuation-dissipation results.
method: The authors use the fluctuation-dissipation theorem for a system of nonconserved charges at thermal equilibrium within the Aharonov-Bohm electrodynamic framework.
result: They obtain fluctuation relations for this non-Maxwellian electrodynamic theory, finding similarities to the standard case under certain equilibrium conditions.
conclusion: The work extends fluctuation-dissipation analysis to a generalized electrodynamics with local charge nonconservation, but it is not directly related to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Scaling Of Long-range Loop-erased Random Walks
authors: Tianning Xiao, Xianzhi Pan, Zhijie Fan, And Youjin Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Tianning Xiao, Xianzhi Pan, Zhijie Fan, and Youjin Deng

We study the scaling properties of long-range loop-erased random walks (LR-LERW), where the underlying random walker performs Lévy-flight-like jumps with a power-law step-length distribution [MATH]. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we measure the scaling rela…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054110] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Monte Carlo study of the scaling properties of long-range loop-erased random walks with power-law Lévy-flight step distributions.
motivation: Loop-erased random walks are a canonical statistical-mechanics model whose long-range variants with power-law jumps have not been fully characterized numerically.
method: Extensive Monte Carlo simulations of LR-LERW with step-length distribution decaying as a power law, extracting scaling relations and critical exponents.
result: The authors measure scaling exponents and verify scaling relations for the long-range loop-erased walk as a function of the Lévy exponent.
conclusion: The numerically determined exponents characterize the universality class of long-range LERW, with results expected to be relevant to statistical-physics and graph-related problems.

title: Enhanced Dumbbell Diffusion In A Periodic Potential By The Elevator Effect
authors: B. A. Kiang And H. Schiessel
abstract:
Author(s): B. A. Kiang and H. Schiessel

We present Brownian dynamics simulations of the random walk of a dumbbell—two beads connected by a spring—in a one-dimensional periodic potential and compare our results in limiting cases to theoretical analytical equations. The relevant parameters in this system are the spring constant, the equilib…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054105] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: Brownian dynamics simulations of a spring-linked dumbbell diffusing in a one-dimensional periodic potential reveal enhanced diffusion via the 'elevator effect' in limiting regimes.
motivation: The authors aim to characterise how internal degrees of freedom (a harmonic spring) modify the thermally activated hopping of a two-bead object through a periodic landscape, a scenario relevant to polymer and motor-protein transport.
method: Langevin/Brownian dynamics simulations of a dumbbell in a 1D periodic potential are performed across parameters (spring constant, equilibration length, potential amplitude) and compared with analytic limiting-case formulas.
result: Diffusion is substantially enhanced relative to a single bead in certain parameter regimes, an enhancement attributed to the elevator effect where the two beads sequentially climb and pull each other over barriers.
conclusion: The simulation results match the derived analytic expressions in the limiting cases tested, providing a quantitative picture of dumbbell transport in periodic potentials.

title: Machine Learning Prediction Of Explosive Death In Coupled Oscillator Networks
authors: Zhonghua Zhang, Liang Wang, Xinyi Li, Ludovico Minati, Michael Small, Stefano Boccaletti, And Wei Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhonghua Zhang, Liang Wang, Xinyi Li, Ludovico Minati, Michael Small, Stefano Boccaletti, and Wei Xu

The accurate prediction of first-order phase transitions such as explosive death is essential for preventing irreversible dynamical collapse in complex networks. Many existing approaches struggle to scale to high-dimensional networks and to identify critical transitions driven by parameter variation…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054207] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses machine learning to predict explosive death (a first-order collapse transition) in networks of coupled oscillators, aiming at scalable early-warning detection of critical transitions.
motivation: Irreversible dynamical collapse in complex networks caused by explosive death transitions is hard to anticipate, and existing prediction methods do not scale to high-dimensional networks or handle parameter-driven critical transitions well.
method: The authors train machine-learning models on simulated time-series or structural data from coupled-oscillator networks to forecast the onset of explosive death as a control parameter is varied, testing scalability to larger network sizes.
result: The trained predictors are reported to anticipate the critical transition threshold with good accuracy and to outperform conventional indicators when applied to high-dimensional oscillator networks.
conclusion: Machine learning offers a practical route to early warning of explosive transitions in complex networks, though the work is confined to classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Framework For Proto-immunity In Open Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Yannick de Decker
abstract:
Author(s): Yannick De Decker

We introduce a framework for immune-like protection in chemical reaction networks obeying deterministic evolution laws. We consider open networks with fixed chemostats and define proto-immunity as the capacity of such systems to preserve a prescribed minimum nonequilibrium throughput, despite the in…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054306] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework for 'proto-immunity'—the capacity of open chemical reaction networks with chemostatted species to maintain a prescribed minimum nonequilibrium throughput against perturbations.
motivation: Biological immune-like robustness is typically studied in complex living systems; the author asks whether an analogous protective property can be formalized and quantified in well-mixed, deterministic open chemical reaction networks far from equilibrium.
method: Open chemical reaction networks with fixed chemostats are modeled under deterministic mass-action-type dynamics, and proto-immunity is defined via constraints on sustained nonequilibrium fluxes/throughput, with conditions derived for when the network can preserve a minimal throughput despite changes in the environment or network parameters.
result: The framework yields criteria characterizing when a network can buffer perturbations and maintain a prescribed minimum dissipative throughput, relating immune-like protection to the underlying stoichiometric and thermodynamic structure of the network.
conclusion: Proto-immunity provides a tractable, thermodynamically grounded notion of robustness in open chemical networks, suggesting a bridge between non-equilibrium chemical kinetics and immune-like functional persistence.

title: Lévy Walks With Permanent Immobilization Characterized By Non-normalized Flight Time Distribution
authors: Heyu Yuan And Xudong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Heyu Yuan and Xudong Wang

Permanent particle immobilization widely emerges across complex transport systems, ranging from intracellular transport to active matter in disordered media, and constitutes a hallmark feature of such systems. Starting from the standard Lévy walk with power-law distributed flight time [MATH],…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054102] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the standard Lévy walk model to include permanent particle immobilization arising from a non-normalized (improper) flight-time distribution, and derives the resulting transport statistics.
motivation: Permanent immobilization is ubiquitous in complex transport systems, from intracellular transport to active matter in disordered media, but existing Lévy walk models assume normalizable flight-time distributions and cannot capture particles that stop indefinitely.
method: Starting from the standard Lévy walk with power-law flight times, the authors modify the flight-time distribution so that it is non-normalized, assigning finite weight to infinite trapping times, and analyze the resulting propagator and moments via continuous-time random walk / fractional-diffusion style techniques.
result: The modified model yields a fraction of permanently immobilized particles coexisting with a mobile population, altering the asymptotic spreading laws, the effective diffusion exponent, and the shape of the position distribution relative to conventional Lévy walks.
conclusion: Non-normalized flight-time statistics provide a natural, analytically tractable route to describing transport with permanent trapping, with implications for anomalous transport in disordered and biological media.

title: Anisotropic Diffusion In A Layer Of Varying Thickness
authors: Pavol Kalinay
abstract:
Author(s): Pavol Kalinay

In order to describe diffusion of a particle in a thin layer of varying thickness, the author uses a mapping procedure originally derived for one-dimensional channels to obtain an effective two-dimensional equation. The resulting description of diffusion in such a confined geometry can be useful for systems like particles moving in thin films and particle separators.

#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054104] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an effective two-dimensional diffusion equation for particles confined in a thin layer whose thickness varies spatially, using a mapping procedure adapted from one-dimensional channel models.
motivation: Diffusion in confined geometries with non-uniform thickness is common in thin films and particle separators, but a reduced-dimension effective description is needed to avoid solving the full three-dimensional problem.
method: A mapping procedure previously developed for one-dimensional channels is generalized to project the 3D diffusion problem onto an effective 2D anisotropic diffusion equation with geometry-dependent coefficients.
result: The resulting effective 2D equation captures anisotropic diffusion induced by the varying layer thickness, providing a tractable reduced description of transport in such confined geometries.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical effective-equation tool for modeling particle transport in thin films and separator systems, though it remains a classical diffusive transport result.

title: Terahertz Lattice Imprint Of A Hidden Multipolar Ordering Transition In ${\mathrm{Gd}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ru}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Nicolas M. Kawahala, Rafael L. Sabainsk, Esteban Marulanda, Rafael S. Freitas, And Felix G. G. Hernandez
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas M. Kawahala, Rafael L. Sabainsk, Esteban Marulanda, Rafael S. Freitas, and Felix G. G. Hernandez

Magnetic order carried by higher-rank multipoles produces no net moment and couples only weakly to conventional dipolar probes. Recently, the lattice has been proposed as an alternative detection channel for the associated ordering transitions. Here, we report magneto-terahertz time-domain spectrosc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043114] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: Magneto-terahertz time-domain spectroscopy is used to detect a hidden multipolar ordering transition in Gd2Ru2O7 via its imprint on the crystal lattice.
motivation: Higher-rank multipolar magnetic order carries no net dipole moment and couples only weakly to conventional dipolar probes, so alternative detection channels are needed; the lattice has been proposed as one such channel.
method: Magneto-terahertz time-domain spectroscopy measurements on Gd2Ru2O7, analyzing the lattice (phonon) response as a function of temperature and magnetic field to identify the ordering transition.
result: A terahertz lattice imprint associated with the hidden multipolar ordering transition is observed, providing a spectroscopic signature of the multipolar phase.
conclusion: Terahertz lattice spectroscopy offers a viable route to detect and characterize hidden multipolar order in correlated magnets such as Gd2Ru2O7.

title: Direct Observation Of Thermal Spin Depolarization In A Type ${\mathrm{I}}_{\mathrm{B}}$ Half-metal $\mathrm{Ni}{\mathrm{Co}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$ By Spin-resolved Photoemission
authors: Hirokazu Fujiwara, Tomoki Higashikawa, Enda Xiao, Terumasa Tadano, Lingling Xie, Daisuke Kan, Yuichi Shimakawa, Kaishu Kawaguchi, Ryo Mori, Ayumi Harasawa, Takeshi Kondo, And Takayoshi Yokoya
abstract:
Author(s): Hirokazu Fujiwara, Tomoki Higashikawa, Enda Xiao, Terumasa Tadano, Lingling Xie, Daisuke Kan, Yuichi Shimakawa, Kaishu Kawaguchi, Ryo Mori, Ayumi Harasawa, Takeshi Kondo, and Takayoshi Yokoya

Half-metals (HMs), characterized by 100% spin polarization at the Fermi level ([MATH]), are ideal candidates for future spintronic memory devices. However, their spin polarization rapidly decreases with temperature, limiting their practical implementation. While this degradation has been…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043099] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Spin-resolved photoemission reveals the microscopic origin of the temperature-driven loss of spin polarization in the type-I_B half-metal NiCo2O4.
motivation: Half-metals promise 100% spin polarization for spintronic memory, but their polarization degrades rapidly with temperature, and the mechanism behind this degradation was unclear.
method: The authors perform spin-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on NiCo2O4 (with supporting first-principles calculations by Tadano) to track the spin polarization of states near the Fermi level as a function of temperature.
result: A direct observation of thermal spin depolarization at the Fermi level is reported, showing that spin-polarized spectral weight is lost with increasing temperature in this half-metallic oxide.
conclusion: The findings identify thermal spin fluctuations/ depolarization as a fundamental limit for half-metallic spintronic devices and clarify the mechanism of polarization loss in NiCo2O4.

title: Unveiling The Bose-Einstein Condensate-droplet Crossover With Rayleigh Superradiant Scattering
authors: Mithilesh K. Parit, Mingchen Huang, Ziting Chen, Yifei He, Haoting Zhen, And Gyu-Boong Jo
abstract:
Author(s): Mithilesh K. Parit, Mingchen Huang, Ziting Chen, Yifei He, Haoting Zhen, and Gyu-Boong Jo

Rayleigh superradiant scattering is used to probe a dipolar
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042012] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: Rayleigh superradiant scattering is used to probe the crossover between a Bose-Einstein condensate and a dipolar macrodroplet.
motivation: The work aims to characterize the BEC-droplet crossover in a dipolar gas using a light-scattering probe sensitive to the transition.
method: The authors measure Rayleigh superradiant scattering efficiency and light-induced atom depletion dynamics across the crossover, varying the magnetic field orientation.
result: Scattering efficiency peaks near the crossover, and expansion dynamics differ distinctly between the BEC and droplet regimes, with a crossover shift depending on magnetic field orientation.
conclusion: Rayleigh superradiant scattering provides a useful probe of the crossover physics in dipolar quantum gases.

title: Emergent Gauge Flux In Mixed ${\mathrm{QED}}_{3}$ With Flavor Chemical Potential: Implications For Magnetized U(1) Dirac Spin Liquids
authors: Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, And Zi Yang Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, and Zi Yang Meng

Quantum Monte Carlo simulations reveal that a Zeeman field drives Dirac spin liquids into a chiral flux phase, forming relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless photon excitations of the emergent gauge field theory.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041029] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations show that a Zeeman field drives Dirac spin liquids into a chiral flux phase with relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless emergent gauge photons.
motivation: The work aims to understand how magnetized U(1) Dirac spin liquids respond to a flavor chemical potential and whether emergent gauge flux phases arise in mixed QED3.
method: The authors use quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a mixed QED3 theory with flavor chemical potential to probe field-induced phases of Dirac spin liquids.
result: A Zeeman field is found to stabilize a chiral flux phase featuring relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless photon excitations of the emergent gauge field.
conclusion: The results establish a concrete route to magnetized U(1) Dirac spin liquids and highlight emergent gauge-flux physics in correlated spin systems.

title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism In Hematite
authors: Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, And Tsuyoshi Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, and Tsuyoshi Kimura

X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field uncovers signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041015] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Electric-field-dependent X-ray absorption spectroscopy of hematite reveals signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles, supported by theoretical calculations.
motivation: Higher-order magnetic multipoles in antiferromagnets such as hematite are difficult to observe directly, and the authors aim to uncover them via an applied electric field.
method: X-ray magnetic circular/linear dichroism measurements under an applied electric field, combined with theoretical multipole calculations of the absorption spectra.
result: An electric-field-induced nonreciprocal X-ray dichroism is observed, indicating the presence of hidden higher-order magnetic multipole order in hematite.
conclusion: The technique provides a spectroscopic probe of exotic multipolar order in magnetic crystals, of interest for condensed-matter and materials physics rather than quantum information.

title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness And Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$
authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, And B. J. Ramshaw
abstract:
Author(s): Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, and B. J. Ramshaw

Ultrasound measurements in uranium ditelluride (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041006] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements on UTe2 reveal superconducting phase fluctuations extending to twice Tc, implying vanishing phase stiffness and fluctuation-dominated superconductivity with large kinetic inductance.
motivation: UTe2 is an unusual heavy-fermion superconductor whose pairing state and low superfluid density remain debated; the authors aim to probe the superfluid response and the role of phase fluctuations directly via the elastic/ultrasonic response.
method: Temperature-dependent ultrasound (elastic modulus) measurements are used to extract the superfluid stiffness and identify precursor superconducting fluctuations above the critical temperature, interpreted within a phase-fluctuation framework.
result: The measurements show a strongly suppressed phase stiffness that vanishes near the transition, with fluctuation signatures persisting up to roughly 2Tc, indicating an unusually high kinetic inductance in this clean material.
conclusion: Superconductivity in UTe2 appears to be limited by phase fluctuations rather than pair breaking, which constrains interpretations of its pairing symmetry and suggests routes to fluctuation-based device applications.

title: Observation Of Wannier-Rydberg And Charge-Transfer Hybrid Moiré Excitons Under Pressure
authors: Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, And Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, and Yang Xu

Hydrostatic pressure continuously tunes the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, driving a crossover to a strong-moiré regime that hybridizes Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041007] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Hydrostatic pressure is used to tune moiré potentials in semiconductor superlattices, revealing a strong-moiré regime where Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons hybridize.
motivation: Moiré superlattices host excitonic states whose character depends sensitively on the interplay between moiré potential depth and Coulomb binding, and tunable control over this crossover is desirable for designing excitonic quantum materials.
method: The authors apply hydrostatic pressure to continuously vary the moiré potential in a semiconductor superlattice and perform optical/photoluminescence spectroscopy to track exciton resonances across the weak-to-strong moiré crossover.
result: They observe the emergence of hybrid exciton states combining Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer characters in the strong-moiré regime, identified through pressure-dependent spectral evolution.
conclusion: Pressure provides a clean knob for engineering hybrid moiré excitons, offering a route to tunable excitonic physics in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the mean-squared increment as a new statistic for analyzing single-particle tracking data and distinguishing ergodic from non-ergodic stochastic processes.
motivation: Single-particle tracking often requires robust methods to assess ergodicity and classify stochastic processes, and existing approaches can be imprecise or ambiguous.
method: The authors define and analyze the mean-squared increment of positional time series and use it to characterize ergodic and non-ergodic behavior across classes of stochastic processes.
result: The mean-squared increment provides a more precise and unambiguous diagnostic than previous statistics for evaluating ergodicity in single-particle tracking data.
conclusion: The proposed statistic improves the discrimination of genuine versus spurious non-ergodicity and offers a practical tool for stochastic-process classification.

title: Superconductivity In Monolayer-Trilayer Phase Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Under High Pressure
authors: Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, and Meng Wang

High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of .6 K, proving that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031072] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure measurements on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 show a strongly suppressed superconducting Tc of about 0.6 K, indicating that coupled bilayer NiO2 motifs are required for the ~80 K superconductivity seen in the bilayer phase.
motivation: The discovery of high-Tc superconductivity in pressurized bilayer La3Ni2O7 raised the question of which structural motifs—specifically the coupled NiO2 bilayers—are responsible for the high transition temperature.
method: The authors synthesize and characterize the 1313 monolayer-trilayer stacking polymorph of La3Ni2O7 and perform high-pressure electrical transport measurements to determine its superconducting transition temperature.
result: The 1313 phase superconducts with a Tc of only ~0.6 K, dramatically lower than the ~80 K reported for the bilayer 2222 phase.
conclusion: The strong suppression of Tc in the absence of coupled bilayer motifs demonstrates that the bilayer NiO2 structural unit is essential for high-temperature superconductivity in the La-Ni-O system.

title: Pomeranchuk Instability Induced By An Emergent Higher-Order Van Hove Singularity On The Distorted Kagome Surface Of ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, And Haim Beidenkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, and Haim Beidenkopf

Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031069] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Surface distortion of the kagome lattice in Co3Sn2S2 flattens saddle points into a higher-order Van Hove singularity that drives a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic electronic order.
motivation: Van Hove singularities near the Fermi level enhance electronic instabilities, and higher-order (flattened) singularities are predicted to produce stronger correlation effects, but such emergent singularities from surface lattice deformation had not been clearly resolved.
method: The authors combine spectroscopic imaging (quasi-particle interference/STM) and photoemission measurements with tight-binding and effective-model calculations of the distorted kagome surface band structure.
result: A higher-order Van Hove singularity with quartic band dispersion is identified at the surface Brillouin zone, and the measured spectra resolve a Pomeranchuk instability leading to a nematic state splitting the kagome bands.
conclusion: Surface engineering of kagome lattices can generate higher-order Van Vove singularities, offering a tunable route to nematic and other correlation-driven electronic phases in topological kagome metals.

title: Erratum: Faster Quantum Chemistry Simulations On A Quantum Computer With Improved Tensor Factorization And Active Volume Compilation [prx Quantum 6, 030337 (2025)]
authors: Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, And Christofer S. Tautermann
abstract:
Author(s): Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, and Christofer S. Tautermann
[PRX Quantum 7, 049901] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This is a publisher erratum correcting the authors' earlier PRX Quantum paper on faster quantum chemistry simulations via improved tensor factorization and active-volume compilation.
motivation: The original work aimed to reduce quantum resource requirements for molecular energy estimation by improving tensor factorization of the Hamiltonian and compiling circuits using only an 'active volume' of qubits.
method: The erratum note itself provides only a citation-level correction (PRX Quantum 7, 049901) to the original article; no new methodology is described in the record.
result: No new scientific results are reported; the entry documents a correction to the published record of the original simulation protocol.
conclusion: The item is a metadata-level erratum for an applied quantum-chemistry simulation paper, with no content relevant to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Path To Quantum Simulations Of Topological Phases: $(2+1)\mathrm{D}$ Quantum Electrodynamics With Wilson Fermions
authors: Sriram Bharadwaj, Emil Rosanowski, Simran Singh, Alice Di Tucci, Changnan Peng, Karl Jansen, Lena Funcke, And Di Luo
