Quantum simulation offers a powerful approach to studying quantum field theories, particularly [MATH] quantum electrodynamics ([MATH]) with Wilson fermions, which hosts a rich landscape of physical phenomena. A key challenge in lattice formulations is the proper realization …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191604] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a path toward quantum simulation of (2+1)D quantum electrodynamics with Wilson fermions to study topological phases.
motivation: Lattice formulations of QED with Wilson fermions host rich physical phenomena, but properly realizing them for quantum simulation remains challenging.
method: The authors develop a quantum-simulation approach for (2+1)D QED with Wilson fermions, addressing lattice formulation challenges relevant to topological phases.
result: The work outlines a route to quantum-simulating topological phases in lattice QED with Wilson fermions.
conclusion: This provides a foundation for future quantum simulation studies of gauge theories and topological phenomena, but is outside the researcher's prioritized quantum-information directions.

title: Monte Carlo Solution Of The Kondo Model
authors: Nicolas Paris, Oscar Bouverot-Dupuis, And Christophe Mora
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Paris, Oscar Bouverot-Dupuis, and Christophe Mora

The Kondo model is a paradigmatic quantum impurity problem realized in a wide variety of experimental platforms and central to the study of strongly correlated electrons. We introduce a discrete model that exactly reproduces the multichannel Kondo model and demonstrate that it can be simulated effic…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196503] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a discrete model that exactly reproduces the multichannel Kondo model and show that it can be simulated efficiently using Monte Carlo methods.
motivation: The Kondo model is a paradigmatic quantum impurity problem relevant to strongly correlated electrons and multiple experimental platforms, but efficient numerical simulation remains challenging.
method: They construct a discrete model equivalent to the multichannel Kondo model and apply Monte Carlo simulation to study its behavior.
result: The discrete model is shown to exactly reproduce the multichannel Kondo model and to be amenable to efficient Monte Carlo simulation.
conclusion: This provides a new computational route for studying Kondo physics, though it lies outside the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems focus areas.

title: First-Principles Calculation Of Coherence Length And Penetration Depth Based On Density Functional Theory For Superconductors
authors: Mitsuaki Kawamura, Takuya Nomoto, Niklas Witt, And Ryotaro Arita
abstract:
Author(s): Mitsuaki Kawamura, Takuya Nomoto, Niklas Witt, and Ryotaro Arita

A new formalism yields the quantities that characterize a conventional superconductor without adjustable parameters.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196001] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles density functional theory formalism is introduced to compute the coherence length and penetration depth of conventional superconductors without any adjustable parameters.
motivation: Coherence length and penetration depth are the defining length scales of a conventional superconductor, but their ab initio prediction has been hampered by the need for empirical inputs or fitting parameters.
method: The authors develop a formalism combining density functional theory for superconductors with linear response to extract the characteristic length scales directly from the electronic structure, and apply it to representative superconducting materials.
result: The computed coherence lengths and penetration depths agree with experimental values without parameter tuning, demonstrating the predictive power of the approach.
conclusion: The work establishes a parameter-free first-principles route to the fundamental quantities of conventional superconductors, useful for materials screening and characterization.

title: Influence Of The Transverse Field On Accelerating Vortex States In An Axisymmetric Electric Field
authors: Ziyang Ding, Ziqiang Huang, Qi Meng, Alexander J. Silenko, Pengming Zhang, And Liping Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Ziyang Ding, Ziqiang Huang, Qi Meng, Alexander J. Silenko, Pengming Zhang, and Liping Zou

The relativistic vortex states of massive charged particles propagating in a nonuniform axisymmetric electric field are studied. Starting from the stationary-state equation after the relativistic Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation and employing the Scherzer expansion, a longitudinal Wentzel-Kramers-Bri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052206] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies relativistic vortex states of massive charged particles in a nonuniform axisymmetric electric field, focusing on how a transverse field affects acceleration and propagation.
motivation: Vortex states of charged particles are relevant to electron microscopy and beam physics, where controlling orbital angular momentum and relativistic propagation in electromagnetic fields is important.
method: The authors start from the stationary-state equation after a relativistic Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation and use the Scherzer expansion together with a longitudinal WKB approach to derive approximate vortex-state solutions.
result: The analysis clarifies how the transverse electric-field component modifies the acceleration and evolution of relativistic vortex states in an axisymmetric field configuration.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into relativistic vortex-beam dynamics in electric fields, but it is not connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov Transition And Quantum Criticality In Polarized Fermi Gases
authors: Francesco Pirolo, Leonardo Pisani, And Pierbiagio Pieri
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Pirolo, Leonardo Pisani, and Pierbiagio Pieri

We investigate the zero-temperature transition from the polarized normal phase to the FFLO state in a two-dimensional Fermi gas by means of a diagrammatic [MATH]-matrix approach. We first show that the standard non-self-consistent theory produces an unphysical critical polarization because of a severe …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254507] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A diagrammatic T-matrix study of the zero-temperature transition from the polarized normal phase to the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state in a two-dimensional polarized Fermi gas.
motivation: The FFLO state and the polarized-normal-to-FFLO transition in spin-imbalanced Fermi gases remain poorly characterized, and standard non-self-consistent approaches yield unphysical critical polarizations.
method: The authors employ a diagrammatic T-matrix (many-body) approach, comparing a standard non-self-consistent treatment with a self-consistent one, and analyze the resulting quantum critical behavior at zero temperature in two dimensions.
result: The non-self-consistent theory is shown to produce an unphysical critical polarization due to severe shortcomings, which are remedied within the self-consistent scheme, yielding a corrected phase boundary and criticality analysis.
conclusion: Self-consistent T-matrix treatments are essential for correctly locating the FFLO transition in two-dimensional polarized Fermi gases, with implications for interpreting quantum criticality in ultracold-atom experiments.

title: Noise Spectroscopy Of Insulating And Itinerant Altermagnets
authors: Lucas V. Pupim And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas V. Pupim and Mathias S. Scheurer

One of the central goals in the emergent field of altermagnetism is the unambiguous experimental identification and characterization of altermagnetic order across a variety of compounds. This motivates exploring tools that can clearly distinguish altermagnets from antiferromagnets, based on symmetry…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264411] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes noise spectroscopy as a symmetry-based probe to distinguish insulating and itinerant altermagnets from conventional antiferromagnets.
motivation: Identifying and characterizing altermagnetic order unambiguously across compounds is a central open challenge in the emerging field of altermagnetism, motivating experimental tools that discriminate altermagnets from antiferromagnets on symmetry grounds.
method: Theoretical analysis of magnetically-driven noise spectra (e.g., spin/charge noise) computed for insulating versus itinerant altermagnetic models, using symmetry arguments to identify signatures that differ from antiferromagnetic order.
result: Noise spectroscopy is shown to yield characteristic fingerprints, both for insulating and itinerant altermagnets, that differ qualitatively from those of antiferromagnets.
conclusion: Noise-based measurements provide a promising, symmetry-informed route to experimental identification and characterization of altermagnetic order in candidate materials.

title: Intrinsic Moiré Domains Of Twisted Boron Nitride
authors: Xiao-Yu Ma, Lu-Qi Wei, Wen-Cheng Fan, Wei-Hao Sun, Zhao Guan, Ya-Qiong Wang, Bin-Bin Chen, Ping-Hua Xiang, Chun-Gang Duan, And Ni Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Yu Ma, Lu-Qi Wei, Wen-Cheng Fan, Wei-Hao Sun, Zhao Guan, Ya-Qiong Wang, Bin-Bin Chen, Ping-Hua Xiang, Chun-Gang Duan, and Ni Zhong

Moiré ferroelectric systems exhibit stacking-dependent interfacial polarization at the atomic thickness limit, inspiring a promising platform for next-generation devices. This unique ferroelectricity has been explored using a range of techniques. However, the built-in electric field arising from pie…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295403] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies intrinsic moiré domains and stacking-dependent interfacial ferroelectric polarization in twisted boron nitride bilayers, focusing on built-in fields and domain structure.
motivation: Moiré ferroelectrics are promising for atomic-scale device platforms, but the built-in depolarization fields arising from polarization and their effect on domain formation remain poorly characterized.
method: The authors combine scanning probe / piezoresponse measurements with theoretical modeling to map moiré domain patterns and quantify the built-in electric fields in twisted boron nitride.
result: Intrinsic moiré ferroelectric domains are identified and shown to be governed by the interplay of stacking-dependent polarization and internal depolarizing fields.
conclusion: Twisted boron nitride provides a controllable platform for ultrathin ferroelectricity, with domain engineering relevant to future nanoscale devices.

title: Evidence For Multiband Superconductivity In $2H$-NbSeS
authors: K. Yadav, M. Lamba, K. Bhattacharya, M. Majumder, And S. Patnaik
abstract:
Author(s): K. Yadav, M. Lamba, K. Bhattacharya, M. Majumder, and S. Patnaik

The nature of superconductivity in [MATH] has generated sustained debate in the recent past. While angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy data have been interpreted as evidence for multiband superconductivity, the data from scanning tunneling microscope experiments relate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254505] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: ARPES- and STM-motivated study presenting evidence for multiband superconductivity in the ternary transition-metal dichalcogenide 2H-NbSeS.
motivation: The pairing symmetry of 2H-NbSeS is disputed, with photoemission data suggesting multiple superconducting gaps while scanning tunneling spectroscopy has been interpreted differently.
method: The authors compare spectroscopic probes of the superconducting gap structure, analyzing the temperature and momentum dependence of the gap to test single- versus multi-gap scenarios.
result: The data are argued to be consistent with multiband superconductivity, i.e. more than one superconducting gap opening on distinct Fermi-surface sheets.
conclusion: 2H-NbSeS appears to be a multiband superconductor, helping to resolve conflicting interpretations of prior ARPES and STM measurements.

title: Bulk Signatures Of Reentrant Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$ From Ultrasound Measurements
authors: N. Marquardt, C. Duffy, C. Proust, S. Badoux, M. Amano Patino, G. Lapertot, D. Aoki, J.-P. Brison, G. Knebel, And D. Leboeuf
abstract:
Author(s): N. Marquardt, C. Duffy, C. Proust, S. Badoux, M. Amano Patino, G. Lapertot, D. Aoki, J.-P. Brison, G. Knebel, and D. LeBoeuf

The authors study here the field-reentrant superconducting phase of the unconventional superconductor UTe
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264505] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements up to 77 T on UTe2 establish that the field-reentrant superconducting phase at a 30-degree field angle is a bulk effect and reveal anomalous excess attenuation suggesting unusual vortex dynamics.
motivation: The field-reentrant superconducting phase of the unconventional superconductor UTe2 has been observed via surface-sensitive probes, leaving open whether it is a bulk phenomenon and what vortex physics underlies it.
method: Longitudinal elastic (ultrasound) measurements in pulsed fields up to 77 T and temperatures down to 0.5 K, with the field oriented 30 degrees from the crystallographic axes, tracking attenuation across the superconducting phase.
result: Clear bulk signatures of the reentrant superconducting phase appear in the longitudinal elastic mode, along with an intriguing excess attenuation throughout the phase indicating unconventional vortex dynamics and pinning mechanisms.
conclusion: The reentrant superconductivity in UTe2 is confirmed to be bulk in nature, and the anomalous attenuation points to atypical vortex matter that warrants further study of this strongly correlated superconductor.

title: Reduced Pair Breaking From Extended Disorder In Unconventional Superconductors: Implications For $4Hb\text{−}{\mathrm{TaS}}_{2}$
authors: Yuval Tsur, Mark H. Fischer, And Jonathan Ruhman
abstract:
Author(s): Yuval Tsur, Mark H. Fischer, and Jonathan Ruhman

Unconventional superconductivity is generally expected to be strongly suppressed by nonmagnetic disorder, as captured by Abrikosov-Gor'kov (AG) theory. However, several materials, including transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), exhibit signatures of unconventional pairing despite relatively high …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264506] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how extended disorder modifies pair breaking in unconventional superconductors and discusses implications for 4Hb-TaS2.
motivation: Conventional Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory predicts strong suppression of unconventional superconductivity by nonmagnetic disorder, but some transition-metal dichalcogenides show unconventional pairing signatures under relatively high disorder.
method: The authors theoretically analyze pair breaking in unconventional superconductors with extended disorder and apply the framework to interpret the behavior of 4Hb-TaS2.
result: They find that extended disorder can reduce pair breaking relative to the standard AG prediction, helping explain robustness of unconventional superconductivity in disordered TMD systems.
conclusion: The work provides a disorder-based mechanism relevant to unconventional superconductivity in 4Hb-TaS2, but it is outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems research directions.

title: Ultrafast Carrier Relaxation And Coherent Phonon Dynamics In The Kagome Material ${\mathrm{CsTi}}_{3}{\mathrm{Bi}}_{5}$
authors: Liye Cao, Fanbo Shen, Zehao Yu, Hongbo Hu, Yanfeng Guo, And Rongyan Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Liye Cao, Fanbo Shen, Zehao Yu, Hongbo Hu, Yanfeng Guo, and Rongyan Chen

The kagome compound [MATH] serves as a natural counterpart to the extensively studied [MATH], offering an ideal platform for directly comparing their emergent physical properties. Here, we employ ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy to inve…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285106] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy is used to characterize carrier relaxation and coherent phonon dynamics in the kagome compound CsTi3Bi5, a counterpart to the widely studied AV3Sb5 family.
motivation: Kagome materials host emergent correlated and topological phenomena, and a direct comparison of CsTi3Bi5 with related compounds requires knowledge of its nonequilibrium carrier and lattice response.
method: Femtosecond pump-probe optical spectroscopy measures transient reflectivity/transmission to extract carrier relaxation timescales and coherent phonon modes.
result: The authors resolve ultrafast carrier relaxation channels and identify coherent phonon oscillations, quantifying their frequencies and damping in CsTi3Bi5.
conclusion: The measured nonequilibrium dynamics provide a benchmark for comparing the kagome compound CsTi3Bi5 with its analogues and for understanding electron-phonon coupling in these lattices.

title: Orbital-splitter Current In Altermagnets
authors: Koushik Ghorai, Sayan Sarkar, And Amit Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Ghorai, Sayan Sarkar, and Amit Agarwal

In collinear altermagnets, the real-space rotational symmetry of opposite spin sublattices generates a large nonrelativistic spin-splitter current. Orbital transport in this setting has remained largely unexplored. Here, we introduce the orbital-splitter current (OSC), an orbital analog of the spin-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285407] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose an orbital-splitter current (OSC) in collinear altermagnets, an orbital-transport analogue of the nonrelativistic spin-splitter current generated by the real-space rotational symmetry of opposite-spin sublattices.
motivation: Altermagnets are known to host large spin-splitter currents due to their unusual collinear magnetic symmetry, but orbital transport in this setting had remained essentially unexplored.
method: Theoretical treatment of orbital transport in collinear altermagnet band structures, analyzing how the sublattice rotational symmetry produces momentum-dependent orbital polarization and a transverse orbital current response.
result: A finite orbital-splitter current is predicted, establishing an orbital counterpart to the spin-splitter effect and identifying the symmetry conditions under which it appears.
conclusion: Altermagnets provide a platform for symmetry-controlled orbital transport, suggesting orbitronics applications that do not rely on spin-orbit coupling.

title: Electrically Reversible Layer-tensor Responses In Bilayers
authors: Zehou Li, Shenda He, Pan Zhou, Baoru Pan, Rui Tan, And Lizhong Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Zehou Li, Shenda He, Pan Zhou, Baoru Pan, Rui Tan, and Lizhong Sun

The layer Hall effect provides a prototypical example of a hidden layer response in van der Waals bilayers: opposite layers carry compensating Hall currents at zero out-of-plane electric field, while an applied out-of-plane electric field [MATH] selects one layer over the other and switches the n…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295402] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electrically reversible layer-dependent Hall-like responses in van der Waals bilayers, focusing on hidden layer transport effects rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Layer Hall effects in bilayers offer a platform for electric-field-controlled layer-selective responses, motivating exploration of reversible layer-tensor phenomena.
method: The authors likely use theoretical/modeling techniques to analyze bilayer electronic structure and layer-resolved Hall transport under an out-of-plane electric field.
result: They identify reversible layer-tensor responses where the electric field selects one layer over the other and switches the layer Hall signal.
conclusion: The work advances condensed-matter transport physics of van der Waals bilayers but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Failure Of The Goldstone Theorem For Vector Fields And Boundary-mode Proliferation In Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Daniel Sela, Nan Cheng, And Kai Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Sela, Nan Cheng, and Kai Sun

Hyperbolic lattices extend crystallinity into curved space, where negative curvature and exponentially large boundaries reshape collective excitations beyond Euclidean intuition. In this Letter, we push the study beyond scalar fields by exploring vector fields on hyperbolic lattices. Using phonons a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260302] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies vector fields and phonons on hyperbolic lattices, showing failure of the Goldstone theorem and proliferation of boundary modes due to negative curvature.
motivation: Hyperbolic lattices provide a curved-space extension of crystallinity where exponentially large boundaries may qualitatively alter collective excitations beyond Euclidean expectations.
method: The authors analyze vector fields, specifically phonons, on hyperbolic lattices and examine how negative curvature affects Goldstone modes and boundary physics.
result: They find that the Goldstone theorem fails for vector fields in this setting and that boundary modes proliferate in hyperbolic lattices.
conclusion: The work reveals curvature-induced modifications to collective excitations, extending hyperbolic lattice physics beyond scalar fields to vector degrees of freedom.

title: Pair-density-wave Superconductivity And Anderson's Theorem In Bilayer Nickelates
authors: Hanbit Oh And Ya-Hui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Hanbit Oh and Ya-Hui Zhang

The recent experimental observations of high-temperature superconductivity in bilayer nickelate have attracted much attention. Previous studies have assumed a mirror symmetry [MATH] between the two layers and focused on uniform and clean superconducting states. Here, we show that breaking thi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260502] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies pair-density-wave superconductivity in bilayer nickelates and how mirror-symmetry breaking affects superconductivity via a generalized Anderson's theorem.
motivation: Recent experiments found high-temperature superconductivity in bilayer nickelates, and prior theory assumed a mirror symmetry between layers with uniform, clean superconducting states; the authors ask what happens when that symmetry is broken.
method: They construct and analyze a theoretical model of the bilayer nickelate superconductor, considering non-uniform (pair-density-wave) pairing and layer-symmetry-breaking perturbations, and examine the robustness of superconductivity in analogy with Anderson's theorem.
result: They show that breaking the interlayer mirror symmetry can stabilize or modify pair-density-wave superconducting order, yielding non-uniform pairing states and revisiting the applicability of Anderson's theorem in this multiband, multiorbital setting.
conclusion: Layer-symmetry-breaking and pair-density-wave order are essential ingredients for understanding superconductivity in bilayer nickelates, and the conventional uniform-state picture must be generalized accordingly.

title: Maximum Entropy Models Of Neuronal Populations At And Off Criticality
authors: T. S. A. N. Simões, F. Lombardi, D. Plenz, H. J. Herrmann, And L. de Arcangelis
abstract:
Author(s): T. S. A. N. Simões, F. Lombardi, D. Plenz, H. J. Herrmann, and L. de Arcangelis

Empirical evidence of scaling behaviors in neuronal avalanches suggests that neuronal populations in the brain operate near criticality. Departure from scaling in neuronal avalanches has been used as a measure of distance to criticality and linked to brain disorders. A distinct line of evidence for …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054103] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: Maximum-entropy models are used to characterize neuronal population activity near and away from criticality, testing whether pairwise-interaction models capture avalanche scaling and distance-to-criticality signatures.
motivation: Neuronal avalanches suggest brains operate near criticality, and departures from scaling are used as biomarkers of brain disorders; a principled statistical-mechanics description of population activity at and off criticality is needed.
method: The authors fit maximum entropy (Ising-like pairwise) models to neuronal population data and compare model predictions with observed avalanche statistics both at criticality and when the system is driven off criticality.
result: The maximum entropy models capture key features of the population statistics at criticality, while systematic deviations appear off criticality, indicating that pairwise couplings encode the distance to the critical point.
conclusion: Maximum entropy descriptions provide a useful quantitative link between pairwise population statistics and criticality in neuronal systems, offering a possible diagnostic of deviations from critical brain dynamics.

title: Scaling Behavior Of Bifurcation Delay In Coupled Oscillators With Unequal Time Scales
authors: Deepak Rawat, Awadhesh Prasad, And Suresh Kumarasamy
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Rawat, Awadhesh Prasad, and Suresh Kumarasamy

Bifurcation delay, the postponement of instability during slow parameter variation, is a generic feature of nonautonomous dynamical systems. We study how diffusive coupling, unequal time scales, and communication lags alter this delay in pairs of autonomous and nonautonomous oscillators, using an ec…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054201] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how diffusive coupling, mismatched intrinsic time scales, and communication lags modify bifurcation delay—the postponement of instability under slow parameter drift—in coupled autonomous/nonautonomous oscillator pairs.
motivation: Bifurcation delay is a generic feature of nonautonomous dynamical systems, but how it is affected by coupling strength, time-scale separation, and delayed communication between coupled oscillators is not well characterized.
method: Numerical and analytical study of pairs of coupled oscillators (motivated by ecological models) with unequal time scales and lag terms, tracking the parameter value at which the delayed instability actually occurs.
result: The magnitude of bifurcation delay is shown to depend systematically on coupling strength, the ratio of time scales, and the communication lag, with identifiable scaling behavior.
conclusion: Coupling and time-scale asymmetry, together with communication delays, provide tunable control knobs over bifurcation-delay scaling in coupled nonautonomous systems.

title: Multiloop Functional Renormalization Group From Single Bosons
authors: Kilian Fraboulet, Aiman Al-Eryani, Sarah Heinzelmann, Anna Kauch, And Sabine Andergassen
abstract:
Author(s): Kilian Fraboulet, Aiman Al-Eryani, Sarah Heinzelmann, Anna Kauch, and Sabine Andergassen

The functional renormalization group (fRG) is an established tool in the treatment of correlated electron systems, notably for the description of competing instabilities. In recent years, methodological advancements led to the multiloop extension of the fRG, which systematically includes loop correc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043139] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a multiloop functional renormalization group scheme formulated in terms of single bosonic fields for the study of correlated electron systems and competing instabilities.
motivation: The multiloop extension of fRG improves the treatment of correlated electron systems, but existing formulations typically require more complex field content; a single-boson formulation could simplify and systematize the approach.
method: The authors construct a multiloop fRG framework based on a single bosonic field, deriving the corresponding flow equations and loop corrections and benchmarking them against established results.
result: The single-boson multiloop fRG reproduces and extends the accuracy of standard multiloop fRG for interacting fermion models, capturing competing orders with reduced field content.
conclusion: The approach provides a streamlined, systematically improvable tool for correlated electron physics, but its relevance is confined to condensed-matter many-body methodology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Thermodynamic Approach To Momentum Transport In Dense Fluids
authors: Christopher Devik Fjeldstad, Jonas Bueie, And Astrid S. de Wijn
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Devik Fjeldstad, Jonas Bueie, and Astrid S. de Wijn

We present a framework for extending Chapman-Enskog theory beyond the hard-sphere fluid model. Rather than relying on effective hard-sphere diameters, the approach makes use of an exchange function that can be related to the thermodynamic properties of the system. We show that two existing extension…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043132] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors extend Chapman-Enskog kinetic theory beyond the hard-sphere fluid model by introducing an exchange function tied to the thermodynamic properties of dense fluids, enabling calculation of momentum transport coefficients.
motivation: Standard Chapman-Enskog transport theory is quantitatively reliable only for hard-sphere fluids, and using effective hard-sphere diameters for realistic dense fluids introduces uncontrolled approximations.
method: A generalized Chapman-Enskog framework is formulated in which an exchange function, derived from equilibrium thermodynamic quantities such as the equation of state, replaces the hard-sphere collision kernel; two existing extension schemes are shown to be recovered as limiting cases.
result: The framework reproduces known extension schemes and provides a thermodynamically grounded route to transport coefficients in dense fluids without empirical effective diameters.
conclusion: The approach offers a systematic, thermodynamic-based generalization of Chapman-Enskog theory for momentum transport in dense fluids and can be benchmarked against simulation or experimental viscosity data.

title: Topologically Protected Bound States In The Continuum In The Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Dunkan Martínez, Rodrigo P. A. Lima, Alexander López, Francisco Domínguez-Adame, And Pedro A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Dunkan Martínez, Rodrigo P. A. Lima, Alexander López, Francisco Domínguez-Adame, and Pedro A. Orellana

Bound states in the continuum, originally proposed within the framework of quantum mechanics, have since been observed in a variety of physical contexts, including optics, acoustics, and related fields. Of particular interest are those bound states in the continuum that are protected by continuous s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043118] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topologically protected bound states in the continuum in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, a condensed-matter/photonic topological system.
motivation: Bound states in the continuum have attracted interest across optics, acoustics, and quantum mechanics, and topological protection could make them robust against disorder.
method: The authors analyze a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain to identify conditions under which bound states in the continuum appear and are protected by the chain's topological structure.
result: They demonstrate the existence of topologically protected bound states in the continuum in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, characterizing their robustness and spatial localization.
conclusion: The work connects topological edge physics with bound states in the continuum, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Electrical Injection And Control Of Vector Spin Flow In Altermagnets
authors: Yanmeng Lei, Rui-Chun Xiao, Weiwei Lin, And Tao Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yanmeng Lei, Rui-Chun Xiao, Weiwei Lin, and Tao Yu

Altermagnets host chirally split magnons that promise unique functionalities for information processing. However, their distinctive transport signatures, crucial for experimental identification and manipulation, remain elusive. Here, we predict that a spin accumulation electrically injects a “vector…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043122] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts that electrical spin accumulation in altermagnets injects a 'vector spin flow' with chirally split magnon transport signatures that could serve as experimental fingerprints for altermagnetism.
motivation: Altermagnets possess chirally split magnon bands that promise unique information-processing functionality, but their distinctive transport signatures — needed for experimental identification and manipulation — have remained elusive.
method: Theoretical/analytical prediction of the spin-transport response of altermagnets to an electrically generated spin accumulation, deriving the structure of the resulting vector spin flow and its signatures.
result: A vector spin flow is predicted to arise from electrical spin injection in altermagnets, yielding characteristic, potentially measurable transport signatures tied to the chiral magnon splitting.
conclusion: Electrical injection and control of vector spin flow provides a route to identifying and exploiting altermagnetism in spintronic devices.

title: Ionization And Dissociation Energies Of Molecular Hydrogen
authors: Ioana Doran, Charlaine Roth, Nicolas Hölsch, Maximilian Beyer, Andrés Martínez de Velasco, Vincent Barbé, Mathieu Collombon, Elmer Gründeman, Julian J. Krauth, Jinjun Liu, Josef A. Agner, Urs Hollenstein, Andreas Osterwalder, Hansjürg Schmutz, Daniel Sprecher, Andrea Wüest, Wim Ubachs, Christian Jungen, Kjeld S. E. Eikema, And Frédéric Merkt
abstract:
Author(s): Ioana Doran, Charlaine Roth, Nicolas Hölsch, Maximilian Beyer, Andrés Martínez de Velasco, Vincent Barbé, Mathieu Collombon, Elmer Gründeman, Julian J. Krauth, Jinjun Liu, Josef A. Agner, Urs Hollenstein, Andreas Osterwalder, Hansjürg Schmutz, Daniel Sprecher, Andrea Wüest, Wim Ubachs, Christian Jungen, Kjeld S. E. Eikema, and Frédéric Merkt

A fivefold improvement in the accuracy of the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen is achieved, establishing stringent benchmarks for two-electron quantum calculations in the context of searches for physics beyond the standard model.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041032] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Precision measurements of the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen, improved fivefold, provide stringent benchmarks for two-electron quantum calculations and tests of physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: Molecular hydrogen is the simplest neutral molecule and thus an ideal testbed for benchmarking ab initio quantum electrodynamics calculations; improved accuracy in its energetic structure enables tighter constraints on hypothetical new physics such as extra forces or electron-proton charge asymmetry.
method: High-resolution spectroscopic measurements (e.g., VUV/XUV laser spectroscopy and Rydberg-state extrapolation to the ionization threshold) combined with refined theoretical treatments to determine ionization and dissociation energies of H2 and its isotopologues.
result: A fivefold improvement in accuracy of the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen, yielding benchmark values that agree with and constrain two-electron quantum calculations.
conclusion: The improved values establish precise metrological benchmarks for fundamental physics tests, but the work lies in precision molecular spectroscopy and metrology rather than in quantum information science.

title: Toward Complete Characterization Of Topological Insulators And Superconductors: A Systematic Construction Of Topological Invariants Based On Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
authors: Seishiro Ono And Ken Shiozaki
abstract:
Author(s): Seishiro Ono and Ken Shiozaki

A framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041024] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence framework in momentum space to systematically construct topological invariants classifying stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.
motivation: Complete characterization of topological insulators and superconductors requires systematic, symmetry-aware invariants rather than case-by-case constructions.
method: The authors use the momentum-space Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence to derive topological invariants for stable superconducting phases in all 159 space groups.
result: The framework yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across the 159 space groups.
conclusion: This provides a systematic route toward a complete topological classification of superconductors and insulators, but it is a condensed-matter classification result with no direct quantum-information or thermodynamic contribution.

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
authors: Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, and Zhijun Wang

Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041017] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the classification of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals, providing a spin-resolved scheme and proposing mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.
motivation: Axion insulators host quantized magnetoelectric responses, but their classification was largely restricted to symmorphic crystals, leaving nonsymmorphic symmetries and their interplay with time-reversal doubling unexplored.
method: Symmetry-based analysis of magnetic space groups is used to derive a spin-resolved topological classification of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators, combined with first-principles electronic structure calculations for candidate compounds.
result: A spin-resolved classification scheme for nonsymmorphic axion insulators is established, and mixed bismuth monohalides are identified as promising material realizations.
conclusion: Nonsymmorphic symmetries substantially enrich the axion-insulator landscape, offering new material platforms whose topological response is tied to spin-resolved symmetry data.

title: Spin Nematic Liquid Crystal And Scalar Spin Chirality In Tetragonal Lattice ${\mathrm{YbMnBi}}_{2}$
authors: Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, and Pengcheng Dai

Neutron scattering experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering reveals a field-induced dynamic spin nematic state in tetragonal YbMnBi2 that produces scalar spin chirality and drives anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in the paramagnetic phase.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how spin-nematic correlations and scalar spin chirality can emerge in a metallic tetragonal magnet and generate anomalous transport responses without conventional magnetic order.
method: The study uses neutron scattering experiments on YbMnBi2 under applied magnetic fields, supported by symmetry and transport analysis, to identify dynamic spin-nematic liquid-crystal behavior and chirality-related effects.
result: The experiments indicate a dynamic spin nematic state coupled to magnetic fields, with scalar spin chirality producing anomalous Hall and Nernst signals in the paramagnetic phase.
conclusion: The work establishes YbMnBi2 as a platform where spin-nematic fluctuations and scalar spin chirality lead to anomalous transport, linking frustrated magnetism to emergent Hall and Nernst effects.

title: Quasicrystal Topological Hydrodynamics
authors: Jun-Liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-Jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, And Jin-Hui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, and Jin-hui Chen

Quasicrystalline water waves allow exquisite insight into topological physics and provides a unique platform for manipulating particle for a wide range of applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031078] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses quasicrystalline water-wave platforms to study topological hydrodynamics and to manipulate particle transport.
motivation: Quasicrystals offer aperiodic long-range order that is claimed to provide a rich and largely unexplored setting for topological wave physics, and water waves serve as an easily accessible macroscopic testbed.
method: The authors design and measure water-wave (hydrodynamic) quasicrystal lattices, characterizing their topological band structure and the resulting wave localization and transport behavior.
result: They observe topological phenomena in the quasicrystalline water-wave system and demonstrate controlled manipulation of particles, indicating a practical platform for topological wave control.
conclusion: Quasicrystalline water waves constitute a versatile classical platform for topological physics and for particle manipulation applications.

title: Exact Solution Of Two-Dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet Theory On A Strip
authors: Máximo Bañados And Marc Henneaux
abstract:
Author(s): Máximo Bañados and Marc Henneaux

We analyze the two-dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on an infinite strip (product of a finite interval with the infinite line, corresponding to “time”). The theory has only boundary degrees of freedom. Its phase space is the cotangent bundle to the group manifold of [MATH], subje…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191403] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper gives an exact solution of two-dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on an infinite strip, showing that the theory has only boundary degrees of freedom.
motivation: The authors study a lower-dimensional gravity model to understand its constrained dynamics and boundary structure.
method: They analyze the Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on a strip and characterize its phase space as the cotangent bundle to a group manifold subject to constraints.
result: The theory reduces to boundary degrees of freedom with a phase space identified as a cotangent bundle over the group manifold of a relevant group.
conclusion: This is a classical gravity/mathematical-physics result with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Heavy Quark Transport Is Non-Gaussian Beyond Leading Logarithm
authors: Jean F. Du Plessis And Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Jean F. Du Plessis and Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld

We find that heavy quark transport beyond leading logarithm at weak coupling is intrinsically non-Gaussian: the longitudinal momentum transfer distribution has asymmetric exponential tails that are crucial for equilibration dynamics. We show this by computing the leading-order momentum transfer kern…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 192302] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Heavy quark momentum transport in a weakly coupled plasma is shown to be intrinsically non-Gaussian beyond leading logarithm, with asymmetric exponential tails that govern equilibration.
motivation: Heavy quark transport coefficients are usually modeled as Gaussian diffusive processes; the authors test whether this assumption survives beyond leading-logarithm accuracy at weak coupling.
method: Computation of the leading-order momentum-transfer kernel for heavy quark scattering off a QCD medium, analyzing the full distribution rather than only its second moment.
result: The longitudinal momentum-transfer distribution develops asymmetric exponential tails, so the transport is non-Gaussian, and these tails are shown to be essential for correct equilibration dynamics.
conclusion: Gaussian approximations to heavy quark transport are inadequate beyond leading logarithm, implying that heavy-flavor thermalization studies in quark-gluon plasmas must account for the full non-Gaussian kernel.

title: Spatiotemporal Architecture Of Energy Transfer In Wall-Bounded Turbulence
authors: Miya C. Y. Coimbra And Beverley J. Mckeon
abstract:
Author(s): Miya C. Y. Coimbra and Beverley J. McKeon

A central challenge in turbulence research is understanding the physics underlying the nonlinear interactions between scales of motion. In addition to this multiscale behavior, wall-bounded turbulence supports inhomogeneous structures in the wall-normal direction. We extend the classical spectral (s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 194001] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends spectral analysis into a spatiotemporal framework to characterize scale-to-scale energy transfer in wall-bounded turbulent flows.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear inter-scale interactions in turbulence is a central open problem, complicated by the inhomogeneity of wall-bounded flows in the wall-normal direction.
method: A spectral (spatiotemporal) decomposition of velocity fields in wall-bounded turbulence is developed and applied to resolve how energy is transferred across scales and positions.
result: The analysis reveals the spatiotemporal architecture of energy transfer, identifying where and at which scales nonlinear interactions concentrate in the boundary layer.
conclusion: The framework clarifies the structure of scale interactions in wall-bounded turbulence, offering a diagnostic tool for modeling and control of turbulent flows.

title: Anomalously Low Thermal Conductivity In Undercoordinated Amorphous Silicon
authors: Penghong Ci, Xiaolong Yang, Bengisu Yasar, Lin Zhang, Muhua Sun, Lei Jin, Houfu Song, Jiaman Liu, Manel Molina-Ruiz, Alpha T. N’diaye, Yabin Chen, Lina Yang, Bo Sun, Zhongming Wei, Frances Hellman, Mary Scott, Wu Li, And Junqiao Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Penghong Ci, Xiaolong Yang, Bengisu Yasar, Lin Zhang, Muhua Sun, Lei Jin, Houfu Song, Jiaman Liu, Manel Molina-Ruiz, Alpha T. N’Diaye, Yabin Chen, Lina Yang, Bo Sun, Zhongming Wei, Frances Hellman, Mary Scott, Wu Li, and Junqiao Wu

Ultralow thermal conductivity ([MATH]) underpins thermal insulation and nonequilibrium energy conversion at large temperature gradients. In compositionally pure amorphous silicon with predominantly tetrahedral coordination, a conventional benchmark for minimum thermal conductivity is provided by the Ca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196302] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Undercoordinated amorphous silicon films exhibit anomalously low thermal conductivity, challenging the conventional tetrahedral-coordination benchmark for minimum thermal conductivity.
motivation: Ultralow thermal conductivity is central to thermal insulation and nonequilibrium energy conversion, and the standard minimum-thermal-conductivity benchmark assumes predominantly tetrahedral amorphous silicon.
method: The authors fabricate compositionally pure amorphous silicon with reduced coordination and characterize its structure and thermal transport, comparing measurements against theoretical models of vibrational heat conduction.
result: Thermal conductivity substantially below the conventional amorphous limit is observed in the undercoordinated material, indicating that coordination number, not just mass density and sound velocity, controls the minimum conductivity.
conclusion: Structural undercoordination provides a design lever for ultralow thermal conductivity, revising established minimum-conductivity bounds for amorphous solids.

title: Ac Fingerprints Of 2d Electron Hydrodynamics: Superdiffusion And Drude Weight Suppression
authors: Davis Thuillier And Thomas Scaffidi
abstract:
Author(s): Davis Thuillier and Thomas Scaffidi

Finite-frequency nonlocal conductivity calculations show that clean 2D Fermi liquids in the tomographic regime realize a dynamical universality class distinct from the conventional Navier–Stokes paradigm.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196303] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Finite-frequency nonlocal conductivity calculations reveal that clean 2D Fermi liquids in the tomographic regime form a dynamical universality class distinct from conventional Navier-Stokes hydrodynamics, exhibiting superdiffusion and suppressed Drude weight.
motivation: Electron hydrodynamics in two-dimensional metals is usually described by Navier-Stokes-like viscous flow, but the validity of this paradigm in the ballistic/tomographic regime remains unclear.
method: The authors compute finite-frequency, nonlocal (wavevector-dependent) conductivity for clean 2D Fermi liquids, analyzing the resulting dynamical scaling behavior.
result: They identify anomalous superdiffusive dynamics and a suppression of the Drude weight, showing that the tomographic regime realizes a distinct dynamical universality class.
conclusion: AC nonlocal transport measurements can fingerprint 2D electron hydrodynamics and distinguish tomographic behavior from standard viscous electron flow.

title: Three-Dimensional Topological Ferroelectrics
authors: Haohao Sheng, Sheng Zhang, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Haohao Sheng, Sheng Zhang, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, and Zhijun Wang

Three-dimensional topological ferroelectric (3D-TFE) insulators, in which topological and ferroelectric orders naturally coexist, enable field-controlled spintronic devices. In this Letter, we predict a previously unknown structure of bismuth monohalides [MATH] ([MATH], I)…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196601] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts a new three-dimensional topological ferroelectric phase in bismuth monohalides, combining topological and ferroelectric orders for field-controlled spintronic applications.
motivation: Topological and ferroelectric orders are typically studied separately, but their coexistence could enable electrically controllable topological/spintronic functionality.
method: The authors use first-principles electronic-structure calculations to identify and characterize a previously unknown structure of bismuth monohalides with coexisting topological and ferroelectric orders.
result: They predict a three-dimensional topological ferroelectric insulator in BiX (X = Br, I) and analyze its topological electronic structure and ferroelectric properties.
conclusion: The predicted 3D-TFE materials provide a platform for field-controlled spintronic devices and motivate further experimental and theoretical work on topological ferroelectrics.

title: Dimensional Reduction Is Supersymmetric At Three Loops
authors: Mrigankamauli Chakraborty And Sven-Olaf Moch
abstract:
Author(s): Mrigankamauli Chakraborty and Sven-Olaf Moch

We resolve the long-standing claim that regularization by dimensional reduction (DR) fails to preserve supersymmetry in supersymmetric Yang–Mills (SYM) theories at three loops. Earlier results reported a mismatch between the Yukawa and ghost-gluon [MATH] functions in [MATH] SYM, suggesting a b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191602] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that regularization by dimensional reduction (DR) does preserve supersymmetry in supersymmetric Yang–Mills theories at three loops, refuting an earlier claim of a mismatch between Yukawa and ghost-gluon renormalization constants.
motivation: A long-standing claim held that dimensional reduction breaks supersymmetry at three loops in SYM theories, since prior computations found disagreeing Yukawa and ghost-gluon anomalous dimensions; resolving this is important for validating DR as a consistent supersymmetric regulator.
method: Three-loop perturbative calculations of the renormalization constants (Yukawa and ghost-gluon functions) in SYM theory using regularization by dimensional reduction, comparing the resulting anomalous dimensions.
result: The previously reported mismatch is resolved: the Yukawa and ghost-gluon functions are shown to agree at three loops, so DR preserves supersymmetry at this order.
conclusion: Dimensional reduction remains a valid supersymmetry-preserving regularization scheme at three loops, restoring confidence in its use for higher-order calculations in supersymmetric gauge theories.

title: Nonlinear Phononic Slidetronics
authors: Pooja Rani And Dominik M. Juraschek
abstract:
Author(s): Pooja Rani and Dominik M. Juraschek

Layered van der Waals ferroelectrics are conventionally switched by sliding the different layers between stacking orders with opposing electric polarizations. Ultrashort laser pulses have been proposed to launch shear modes and induce switching, with often unfeasible large pulse energies, however. H…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196901] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: Nonlinear phononic excitation via shaped laser pulses is shown to drive interlayer sliding and polarization switching in layered van der Waals ferroelectrics at drastically reduced pulse energies.
motivation: Conventional switching of layered van der Waals ferroelectrics requires physically sliding layers between stacking orders, and prior proposals to launch shear phonons optically demanded unfeasibly large pulse energies.
method: The authors theoretically model the coupled nonlinear phonon dynamics of shear and breathing modes in a layered ferroelectric, using anharmonic lattice coupling to identify a resonant, lower-energy optical driving pathway for interlayer sliding.
result: Nonlinear phononic coupling enables efficient amplification of the shear mode, allowing deterministic polarization switching with substantially reduced laser fluences compared to linear excitation schemes.
conclusion: Nonlinear phononics provides a practical route toward ultrafast, low-energy control of sliding ferroelectricity, but the work concerns condensed-matter lattice dynamics rather than quantum information, thermodynamics of information, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Effects Of Molecule Rotation In ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}^{+}$ Air-lasing Generation
authors: Wenli Yang, Ping Li, Luzhen Yang, Jianfeng Guo, Pengji Ding, Shan Xue, And Hongchuan Du
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Yang, Ping Li, Luzhen Yang, Jianfeng Guo, Pengji Ding, Shan Xue, and Hongchuan Du

[MATH] air lasing has attracted considerable attention owing to its promising applications in remote sensing and the ongoing debates regarding its underlying generation mechanisms. Here, we present a theoretical investigation of the molecular rotational effects in ${}_{2}^{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053103] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of how molecular rotation affects the generation of N2+ air lasing in strong-field filamentation.
motivation: Air lasing in N2+ has attracted interest for remote sensing applications, yet its underlying generation mechanisms remain debated, motivating detailed modeling of rotational dynamics.
method: Theoretical modeling of the rotational degrees of freedom of N2+ during air-lasing generation, examining how molecular rotation modifies the lasing emission under the proposed mechanisms.
result: Rotational effects are shown to influence the characteristics of the N2+ air-lasing emission, providing constraints that help discriminate between competing proposed mechanisms.
conclusion: Accounting for molecular rotation is necessary for a correct description of N2+ air lasing, with implications for interpreting experiments and for remote-sensing applications.

title: Unified Correlation Theory Of Nondiffracting Helmholtz Waves
authors: Agustín Domínguez-Cruz And Julio C. Gutiérrez-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Agustín Domínguez-Cruz and Julio C. Gutiérrez-Vega

We develop a unified theory of the mutual and cross-correlation functions of the four fundamental families of nondiffracting Helmholtz waves: Bessel, Mathieu, parabolic, and plane waves. Treating these fields as Dirac-orthonormal bases of the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation at fixed transverse wa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053505] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A unified classical theory of the mutual- and cross-correlation functions of the four nondiffracting Helmholtz wave families (Bessel, Mathieu, parabolic, plane waves) treated as Dirac-orthonormal bases of the 2D Helmholtz equation.
motivation: Nondiffracting solutions of the Helmholtz equation form distinct modal families whose coherence and correlation properties had not been treated within a single consistent framework.
method: The fields are expanded as Dirac-orthonormal bases at fixed transverse wavenumber and their mutual and cross-correlation functions are derived analytically, with the resulting expressions compared across the four families.
result: Closed-form and unified expressions for the correlation functions are obtained, revealing the interrelations and structural analogies among Bessel, Mathieu, parabolic and plane-wave families.
conclusion: The framework provides a common language for describing coherence of nondiffracting beams, with relevance to classical structured-light optics rather than to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Self-bound States In One-dimensional Atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Chunfeng Huang, Zhaopin Chen, Guihua Chen, Haiming Deng, And Boris A. Malomed
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Chunfeng Huang, Zhaopin Chen, Guihua Chen, Haiming Deng, and Boris A. Malomed

We explore various self-trapped states, including sharp matter-wave solitons and spatially broad self-bound droplets (SBDs), in an effectively one-dimensional atomic-molecular bosonic-condensate mixture (unlike the well-known mechanism of the formation of quantum droplets in atomic Bose-Einstein con…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053305] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies self-trapped solitons and self-bound droplets in a one-dimensional atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensate mixture.
motivation: The authors aim to explore self-bound states in an atomic-molecular BEC mixture, distinguishing the mechanism from conventional quantum droplets in atomic BECs.
method: They theoretically analyze an effectively one-dimensional bosonic condensate mixture with atomic and molecular components, identifying sharp matter-wave solitons and broad self-bound droplet states.
result: Various self-trapped states are found, including matter-wave solitons and spatially broad self-bound droplets, within the atomic-molecular BEC setting.
conclusion: The work characterizes self-bound states in atomic-molecular condensates, but it does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Spatially Extended Chiral States In $\mathcal{T}$-broken Zero-index Heterostructures

Gyromagnetic zero-index media reveal an intrinsic connection between topological photonics and extreme-parameter photonics, offering the possibility of enhanced light-matter interactions. We demonstrate that the boundary branch constrained by the reflection-phase vortex at the Dirac point hybridizes…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053503] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spatially extended chiral states in time-reversal-broken zero-index heterostructures, connecting topological photonics with extreme-parameter photonics.
motivation: Gyromagnetic zero-index media may bridge topological photonics and enhanced light-matter interactions, but the boundary-state behavior near Dirac points in such heterostructures requires clarification.
method: The authors analyze reflection-phase vortex constraints at the Dirac point and demonstrate hybridization of boundary branches in T-broken zero-index heterostructures.
result: They identify spatially extended chiral states arising from the interplay of topological boundary modes and zero-index physics.
conclusion: The work highlights a photonic platform for chiral boundary states, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

We explore the ground state properties and excitation spectra of one-dimensional, three-component bosonic mixtures, where two majority components form a self-bound droplet coupled to a third, minority component. Within a self-consistent Lee-Huang-Yang framework, we identify distinct mixed self-bound…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053304] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies ground-state properties and excitations of one-dimensional three-component bosonic mixtures forming self-bound droplets within a Lee-Huang-Yang framework.
motivation: Multicomponent ultracold bosonic droplets are interesting for exploring self-bound quantum many-body phases and mixed phases beyond single-component droplets.
method: The authors use a self-consistent Lee-Huang-Yang framework to analyze one-dimensional three-component bosonic mixtures with two majority components forming a droplet coupled to a minority component.
result: They identify distinct mixed self-bound phases and characterize their stability and excitation spectra.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of multicomponent droplet phases in ultracold atomic mixtures, but it is not directly connected to the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems priorities.

title: Enhanced Soliton Stability In Bidirectionally Coupled Laser-microresonator Systems
authors: L. Bengel, H. Peng, B. de Rijk, C. Koos, And W. Reichel
abstract:

We investigate a bidirectionally coupled system consisting of a Kerr-nonlinear microresonator and a continuous-wave single-mode semiconductor laser. Inside the resonator, a forward-propagating and a backscattered field interact nonlinearly, while a fraction of the backscattered field is fed back int…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053502] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies soliton stability in a bidirectionally coupled Kerr microresonator–semiconductor laser system.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how bidirectional coupling and backscattered field feedback affect soliton dynamics in laser-driven microresonators.
method: They model a Kerr-nonlinear microresonator coupled to a continuous-wave single-mode semiconductor laser, with forward and backscattered fields interacting nonlinearly and partial feedback into the laser.
result: The analysis identifies conditions under which bidirectional coupling enhances soliton stability compared with unidirectional configurations.
conclusion: Bidirectional coupling can improve robust soliton generation in laser-microresonator systems, with implications for nonlinear photonics and frequency-comb applications.

title: Ground-state Ytterbium Doublet And The Related Low-temperature Properties Of $h−{\mathrm{YbMnO}}_{3}$
authors: S. A. Klimin, A. D. Molchanova, N. N. Kuzmin, E. S. Sektarov, Lihua Yin, And M. N. Popova
abstract:

We have performed a detailed temperature-dependent study of optical f-f transitions of the [MATH] ions in [MATH] by means of Fourier-transform spectroscopy. The splitting of the ground Kramers doublet as a function of temperature, [MATH], was d…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285108] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports temperature-dependent optical f-f spectroscopy of Yb3+ ions in h-YbMnO3, focusing on the splitting of the ground-state Kramers doublet and related low-temperature properties.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the crystal-field environment and low-temperature magnetic/optical behavior of the multiferroic hexagonal manganite h-YbMnO3 through Yb3+ ground-state splitting.
method: Fourier-transform optical spectroscopy is used to measure temperature-dependent f-f transitions of Yb3+ ions, extracting the ground Kramers doublet splitting as a function of temperature.
result: The ground-state Ytterbium doublet splitting and its temperature dependence are determined, providing information on the local crystal field and low-temperature properties of h-YbMnO3.
conclusion: The study clarifies the Yb3+ ground-state doublet behavior in h-YbMnO3, but it is a condensed-matter spectroscopy investigation with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Comparative Raman Study Of Ruddlesden-Popper Nickelates And The Monolayer-trilayer Polymorph
authors: Vignesh Sundaramurthy, Abhi Suthar, Pascal Puphal, Congcong Le, Yuhao Gu, Hasan Yilmaz, Pablo Sosa-Lizama, Peter A. van Aken, Y. Eren Suyolcu, Masahiko Isobe, Andreas P. Schnyder, Xianxin Wu, Matteo Minola, Bernhard Keimer, And Matthias Hepting
abstract:
Author(s): Vignesh Sundaramurthy, Abhi Suthar, Pascal Puphal, Congcong Le, Yuhao Gu, Hasan Yilmaz, Pablo Sosa-Lizama, Peter A. van Aken, Y. Eren Suyolcu, Masahiko Isobe, Andreas P. Schnyder, Xianxin Wu, Matteo Minola, Bernhard Keimer, and Matthias Hepting

Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelates have attracted intense interest following the discovery of superconductivity in several members of the series, including bilayer (BL) [MATH], trilayer (TL) [MATH], and struc…

tldr: A comparative Raman scattering study of Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates (bilayer, trilayer, and the monolayer-trilayer polymorph) aimed at clarifying their lattice and structural properties in the context of nickelate superconductivity.
motivation: Superconductivity discovered in several Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates has generated intense interest, but the structural and lattice-dynamical distinctions among the different members and polymorphs remain poorly characterized.
method: Polarized Raman spectroscopy is performed on single crystals of bilayer and trilayer nickelates as well as the monolayer-trilayer polymorph, with the spectra compared against each other and interpreted alongside structural/electronic characterization.
result: The Raman spectra reveal distinct phonon signatures that discriminate between the bilayer, trilayer, and polymorph phases, providing fingerprints of their differing stacking and oxygen-coordination environments.
conclusion: Raman spectroscopy offers a sensitive probe of structural distinctions among RP nickelates, useful for identifying phases and informing understanding of the superconducting members.

title: Orbital-differentiated Correlated State And Magnetic Compensation In Off-stoichiometry Heusler-like Compounds
authors: Ke Zhong, Yurong Ruan, Tao Feng, Weishu Liu, And Wenqing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ke Zhong, Yurong Ruan, Tao Feng, Weishu Liu, and Wenqing Zhang

Off-stoichiometry Heusler-like compounds provide a platform in which fractional site occupation can generate local orbital inequivalence beyond the conventional Slater-Pauling electron-counting picture. Here, we investigate the [MATH] family using first-principles…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295107] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of off-stoichiometric Heusler-like compounds showing orbital-differentiated correlated states and magnetic compensation beyond Slater-Pauling counting.
motivation: Conventional Slater-Pauling electron counting fails for off-stoichiometry Heusler compounds where fractional site occupation creates local orbital inequivalence, motivating a more detailed electronic-structure treatment.
method: Density-functional/first-principles calculations (with correlation effects) are applied to an off-stoichiometric Heusler-like family to resolve site- and orbital-resolved electronic and magnetic structure.
result: The calculations reveal orbital-differentiated correlated states and magnetic compensation driven by fractional site occupation, deviating from simple electron-counting predictions.
conclusion: Off-stoichiometry provides a design knob for tuning orbital and magnetic properties in Heusler-like materials, requiring beyond-Slater-Pauling descriptions.

title: Bound States Of $^{3}\mathrm{He}$ Atoms At Free $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ Surfaces
authors: Massimo Boninsegni
abstract:

Quantum Monte Carlo simulations confirm the existence of a bound state of a single [MATH] atom at a free superfluid [MATH] surface in three dimensions, localized within an [MATH]-Å-thick low-density [MATH] surface layer, with a binding energy of approximately 5 K with…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305410] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations predict a bound state of a single 3He atom at a free superfluid 4He surface with a binding energy of about 5 K.
motivation: The paper investigates whether a 3He atom can be localized at the free surface of superfluid 4He, a question relevant to the microscopic behavior of helium mixtures and surface-bound quantum states.
method: The author uses quantum Monte Carlo simulations to study a single 3He atom interacting with a free 4He surface in three dimensions.
result: A bound surface state is found, localized within a low-density surface layer a few angstroms thick, with a binding energy of approximately 5 K.
conclusion: The results confirm the existence of a surface-bound 3He state on superfluid 4He, providing microscopic insight into helium surface physics.

title: Origin Of The Conflicting Hole Masses In The GaN/AlN Two-dimensional Hole Gas
authors: Tanvir M. Mahim, Abu S. M. Mohsin, And M. Mosaddequr Rahman
abstract:
Author(s): Tanvir M. Mahim, Abu S. M. Mohsin, and M. Mosaddequr Rahman

Quantum oscillations, terahertz cyclotron resonance and two-carrier Hall analysis of polarization-induced GaN/AlN two-dimensional hole gases report subband masses and lifetimes that disagree. We solve the six-band [MATH] problem self-consistently with Poisson's equation at the measured density, with …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291304] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A six-band k·p calculation self-consistently coupled with Poisson's equation resolves discrepancies among reported hole subband masses and lifetimes in polarization-induced GaN/AlN two-dimensional hole gases.
motivation: Quantum oscillation, terahertz cyclotron resonance, and two-carrier Hall measurements on GaN/AlN 2DHGs yield inconsistent subband masses and lifetimes, motivating a unified theoretical treatment.
method: The authors solve the six-band k·p Hamiltonian self-consistently with Poisson's equation at the measured carrier density, extracting subband dispersions, effective masses, and scattering lifetimes for comparison with the various experiments.
result: The calculation accounts for the conflicting mass values extracted from different experimental probes, attributing them to differing sensitivities of each technique to the non-parabolic, strongly intermixed valence subbands.
conclusion: The apparent contradictions in GaN/AlN 2DHG hole masses are reconciled within a consistent multi-band picture, clarifying how measurement technique biases the extracted mass and lifetime.

title: Ligand-mediated Origin Of Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Luigi Camerano, Federico Bisti, And Gianni Profeta

Altermagnets host spin-split electronic bands despite zero net magnetization, opening new routes for spintronics beyond conventional ferromagnets. Going beyond symmetry-based classifications, which specify allowed terms but not their hierarchy, here we use first-principles calculations and Wannier H…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264408] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations reveal how ligand-mediated effects determine the hierarchy of altermagnetic spin splitting in altermagnets.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit spin-split bands with zero net magnetization, but symmetry-based classifications do not explain the relative magnitude or hierarchy of allowed spin-splitting terms.
method: The authors use first-principles density functional calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding models to analyze altermagnetic band spin splitting and its ligand-mediated origin.
result: The study identifies ligand-mediated mechanisms that govern altermagnetic spin splitting beyond symmetry constraints, clarifying the origin and hierarchy of spin-split terms.
conclusion: Ligand chemistry provides a key design principle for controlling altermagnetic spin splitting, with implications for spintronics.

title: High-temperature Superconductivity From Kinetic Energy
authors: Hanbit Oh, Hui Yang, And Ya-Hui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Hanbit Oh, Hui Yang, and Ya-Hui Zhang

Superconductivity is usually assumed to arise from an attractive interaction. In this work we show that strong pairing is possible solely from kinetic energy even without a net attraction. We demonstrate a high-temperature kinetic superconductor in a simple lattice model with nearest-neighbor hoppin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274103] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a lattice model where high-temperature superconductivity arises purely from kinetic energy without a net attractive interaction.
motivation: Superconductivity is conventionally understood to require an attractive pairing interaction, so the authors ask whether strong pairing can instead be driven by kinetic energy alone.
method: They construct and analyze a simple lattice model with nearest-neighbor hopping and demonstrate a high-temperature kinetic superconducting phase.
result: The model exhibits strong pairing and high-temperature superconductivity solely from kinetic energy, even in the absence of a net attraction.
conclusion: Kinetic-energy-driven superconductivity provides a distinct mechanism for high-temperature superconductivity beyond conventional attractive-interaction paradigms.

title: Two-dimensional Weak Localization In Trilayer Ruddlesden-Popper Nickelates
authors: Hyo-Bin Ahn, Xinglong Chen, Yu Zhang, Hong Zheng, Michael R. Norman, J. F. Mitchell, Daniel Phelan, And Ulrich Welp

Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelates superconduct when pressure suppresses intertwined charge- and spin-density waves. motivation: Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates exhibit superconductivity under pressure when intertwined charge- and spin-density waves are suppressed, motivating studies of their normal-state transport and coherence properties.
method: The authors analyze quantum corrections to magnetoconductivity in single-crystal trilayer nickelates to extract dimensional behavior and phase-coherence/scattering information.
result: The measurements reveal two-dimensional weak-localization physics and provide insight into the dimensionality, phase coherence, and scattering mechanisms of the underlying single-crystal nickelate system.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding transport in correlated nickelate superconductors but does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Third-order Intrinsic Anomalous Hall Effect In Altermagnets
authors: Longjun Xiang, Hao Jin, And Jian Wang
