Altermagnets, as an emergent class of quantum magnets, have recently attracted considerable attention, yet an intrinsic transport hallmark of altermagnetic order remains elusive. Here, through spin-group and magnetic Laue-group symmetry analyses, we identify the third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291401] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Symmetry analysis identifies a third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect as a transport hallmark of altermagnetic order.
motivation: Altermagnets are an emergent class of quantum magnets, but a clear intrinsic transport signature of altermagnetic order has remained elusive.
method: Spin-group and magnetic Laue-group symmetry analyses are used to classify and identify allowed third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall responses in altermagnetic materials.
result: A third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect is identified as a symmetry-allowed, characteristic transport response of altermagnets.
conclusion: The third-order anomalous Hall response provides a candidate intrinsic transport fingerprint for detecting and characterizing altermagnetic order.

title: Large Pressure Effects On Magnetic Interactions In Hexagonal $A\mathrm{Ni}{X}_{3}$ Antiferromagnets $(A=\mathrm{Cs}$ Or Rb; $X=\mathrm{Cl}$ Or Br)
authors: Yuzo Sasaki, Kenji Goto, Toshio Ono, And Hidekazu Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Yuzo Sasaki, Kenji Goto, Toshio Ono, and Hidekazu Tanaka

We report magnetization measurements under hydrostatic pressure up to approximately 1.6 GPa in the spin-1 quasi-one-dimensional frustrated antiferromagnets [MATH], and [MATH]. Magnetic susceptibilities observed at various pressures are almost …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254403] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magnetization measurements under hydrostatic pressure on hexagonal spin-1 quasi-one-dimensional frustrated antiferromagnets CsNiCl3, RbNiCl3, CsNiBr3, and RbNiBr3.
motivation: The study aims to clarify how applied pressure modifies magnetic interactions in hexagonal ANiX3 antiferromagnets, where quasi-one-dimensional frustration and spin-1 physics produce nontrivial magnetic behavior.
method: Magnetization measurements were performed under hydrostatic pressures up to approximately 1.6 GPa on the four compounds, and magnetic susceptibilities were compared across pressures.
result: The observed magnetic susceptibilities at various pressures are reported, revealing pressure-induced changes in the magnetic interactions of these frustrated antiferromagnets.
conclusion: The work provides experimental insight into pressure tuning of magnetism in hexagonal ANiX3 compounds, but it lies outside the targeted quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems research directions.

title: Vortex-glass Transition, Pinning Mechanisms, And Vortex Dynamics In NbRe Films And NbRe/Py Bilayers
authors: Abhishek Kumar, F. Avitabile, F. de Chiara, F. Colangelo, Z. Makhdoumi Kakhaki, C. Cirillo, And C. Attanasio
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Kumar, F. Avitabile, F. De Chiara, F. Colangelo, Z. Makhdoumi Kakhaki, C. Cirillo, and C. Attanasio

We present a comparative study of vortex-glass (VG) phase, vortex pinning, and vortex dynamics in superconducting niobium-rhenium (NbRe) films and NbRe/permalloy bilayers fabricated by the dc magnetron sputtering technique, where permalloy (Py) serves as the ferromagnetic layer. Current-voltage char…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254503] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: A comparative study of vortex-glass phases, pinning mechanisms, and vortex dynamics in superconducting NbRe films and NbRe/permalloy ferromagnetic bilayers grown by dc magnetron sputtering.
motivation: Understanding vortex pinning and glassy dynamics in superconductor/ferromagnet hybrids is important for controlling dissipation and critical currents in superconducting devices.
method: Current-voltage characteristics are measured on NbRe films and NbRe/Py bilayers and analyzed within vortex-glass scaling frameworks to extract critical exponents and pinning regimes.
result: The authors identify vortex-glass transitions in both systems and show that the added permalloy layer modifies pinning strength and vortex dynamics relative to bare NbRe films.
conclusion: Ferromagnetic overlayers provide a tunable handle on vortex pinning and glassy behavior in NbRe superconductors, relevant for fluxonic and device applications.

title: Fano-like Resonances In A Stuart-Landau Oscillator With State-dependent Delayed Feedback
authors: D. A. Krylov, A. V. Kovalev, A. V. Babichev, And E. A. Viktorov
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Krylov, A. V. Kovalev, A. V. Babichev, and E. A. Viktorov

We examine the spectral properties of a Stuart-Landau oscillator with state-dependent time-delayed feedback in the presence of amplitude and phase noise. We demonstrate that an asymmetric Fano resonance profile appears in the spectrum under amplitude noise, due to amplitude-phase coupling caused by …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054208] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spectral properties of a classical Stuart-Landau oscillator with state-dependent delayed feedback under amplitude and phase noise, showing noise-induced asymmetric Fano-like resonance profiles.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how amplitude-phase coupling and state-dependent delayed feedback shape the noise spectra of a nonlinear oscillator.
method: They analyze a Stuart-Landau oscillator model with state-dependent time-delayed feedback in the presence of amplitude and phase noise, deriving spectral resonance features.
result: An asymmetric Fano resonance profile appears in the spectrum under amplitude noise due to amplitude-phase coupling caused by the feedback.
conclusion: The work characterizes Fano-like resonances in a classical nonlinear delayed-feedback oscillator, with relevance to classical stochastic nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Product Expansion Of Reservoir States For Robust Chaotic Time Series Prediction
authors: Kaiwen Jiang, Michael Small, And Yong Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiwen Jiang, Michael Small, and Yong Zou

Reservoir computing (RC) excels at chaotic time series prediction but suffers from high sensitivity to hyperparameters (spectral radius, sparsity) and requires large reservoirs, limiting its utility. To overcome these limitations, we propose an enhanced RC framework that introduces time-shift transf…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054209] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a product-expansion reservoir-computing framework using time-shift transformations to improve robustness and reduce hyperparameter sensitivity in chaotic time-series prediction.
motivation: Reservoir computing is effective for chaotic time-series prediction but is highly sensitive to hyperparameters such as spectral radius and sparsity, and typically requires large reservoirs.
method: The authors introduce time-shift transformations and construct reservoir states via a product expansion, aiming to enhance robustness while mitigating hyperparameter dependence.
result: The proposed framework is reported to improve prediction performance and robustness for chaotic time-series tasks while relaxing reservoir size and hyperparameter constraints.
conclusion: The work offers a classical reservoir-computing enhancement for nonlinear time-series forecasting, with no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Advantages Of Small-view Visually Aligned Active Particles In Competing For Nutrient Resources
authors: Maoping Zhang And Weirong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Maoping Zhang and Weirong Zhong

Visual alignment is an intrinsic physical property of certain active matter. Cumulative evidence indicates that active particles with visual alignment exhibit unique nonequilibrium dynamics, including aggregation, migration, and vortex motion. These collective behaviors can reshape their surrounding…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054109] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how small-view visually aligned active particles compete for nutrient resources, focusing on collective nonequilibrium dynamics in active matter.
motivation: Visual alignment is an intrinsic property of some active matter systems, and prior work suggests it produces aggregation, migration, and vortex motion, but its role in resource competition is less understood.
method: The authors likely use agent-based or continuum modeling of active particles with visual alignment and nutrient competition, analyzing collective behavior as a function of viewing range and alignment rules.
result: Small-view visually aligned particles are found to have advantages in competing for nutrient resources, with collective dynamics reshaping access to resources.
conclusion: The work highlights how perceptual range and visual alignment affect resource competition in active matter, but it is classical/biological active-matter physics rather than quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Noise-driven Velocity Selection In Persistent Reaction Random Walks: Renormalization Theory And Numerical Validation
authors: D. C. Bitang Á Ziem
abstract:
Author(s): D. C. Bitang Á Ziem

Front propagation in nonlinear systems is a central theme across physics and biology, yet classical diffusion-based models fail to capture finite-speed transport and directional persistence. In this work, we investigate the impact of multiplicative noise on persistent reaction random walks, focusing…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054106] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies noise-driven velocity selection in persistent reaction random walks using renormalization theory and numerical validation.
motivation: Classical diffusion-based models fail to capture finite-speed transport and directional persistence in front propagation, motivating persistent reaction random walk models with multiplicative noise.
method: The authors develop a renormalization-theory analysis of multiplicative noise effects on persistent reaction random walks and validate the predictions numerically.
result: The work identifies a noise-driven velocity-selection mechanism and supports the theoretical predictions with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The findings clarify how multiplicative noise and persistence affect front propagation in classical stochastic reaction-transport systems.

title: Composite Gap Solitons In Spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein Condensates With An Asymmetric Bichromatic Superlattice And Spatially Modulated Nonlinearity
authors: Tongyu Wu And Tianfu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Tongyu Wu and Tianfu Xu

We investigate composite gap solitons in a spin-orbit-coupled condensate confined in an asymmetric bichromatic superlattice with a spatially modulated nonlinearity. Although the lattice lacks exact symmetry, fundamental and dipole-type solitons retain approximate parity-symmetric profiles and remain…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054202] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies composite gap solitons in a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate loaded into an asymmetric bichromatic superlattice with spatially modulated nonlinearity.
motivation: Gap solitons in spin-orbit-coupled condensates are of interest for nonlinear wave physics and matter-wave localization, but the role of lattice asymmetry combined with spatially modulated nonlinearity had not been characterized.
method: Mean-field Gross-Pitaevskii-type modeling of a two-component spin-orbit-coupled condensate in an asymmetric bichromatic superlattice with position-dependent nonlinearity, followed by numerical construction and stability analysis of fundamental and dipole solitons.
result: Despite the absence of exact lattice symmetry, fundamental and dipole gap solitons retain approximately parity-symmetric profiles and remain stable over a range of parameters.
conclusion: Asymmetric bichromatic superlattices with modulated nonlinearity provide a viable setting for robust composite gap solitons in spin-orbit-coupled condensates.

title: Universal Features In Atmospheric Particulate Matter Dynamics
authors: Suchismita Banerjee, Koyena Ghosh, Urna Basu, And Banasri Basu
abstract:
Author(s): Suchismita Banerjee, Koyena Ghosh, Urna Basu, and Banasri Basu

We study statistical properties of atmospheric particulate matter fluctuations using six years of daily [MATH] concentration data from 54 Indian cities. Despite diverse urban settings and heterogeneous climatic conditions, we find that the fluctuations show strikingly universal behavi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054205] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: Six years of daily PM concentration data from 54 Indian cities reveal strikingly universal statistical features in atmospheric particulate matter fluctuations.
motivation: Understanding universal statistical laws in atmospheric particulate fluctuations could provide a unified description of air pollution dynamics across heterogeneous urban and climatic settings.
method: Statistical analysis of daily particulate matter concentration time series from 54 Indian cities over six years, examining distributions and scaling of fluctuations.
result: Fluctuations exhibit universal behavior despite the diversity of urban settings and climatic conditions across the cities studied.
conclusion: The observed universality suggests general underlying mechanisms governing particulate matter dynamics that transcend local environmental differences.

title: Hysteretic Synchronization Transitions Induced By Adaptive Phase Frustration
authors: Junyi Zheng, Changgui Gu, Jiangsheng Wang, And Yuxuan Song
abstract:
Author(s): Junyi Zheng, Changgui Gu, Jiangsheng Wang, and Yuxuan Song

Phase frustration is often used to represent an effective phase lag caused by signal transmission, sensing, processing, or response delays. In conventional phase-oscillator models, a fixed phase lag usually weakens the attractive component of the coupling and tends to hinder synchronization. Here we…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054206] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how adaptive (state-dependent) phase frustration in coupled phase oscillators produces hysteretic synchronization transitions, in contrast to fixed phase lags that merely hinder synchronization.
motivation: Phase frustration models transmission, sensing, and response delays in coupled oscillators; conventional fixed lags weaken attractive coupling, so the authors ask what happens when the frustration itself adapts to the system state.
method: They analyze phase-oscillator (Kuramoto-type) models with an adaptive phase-frustration term and characterize the resulting synchronization transitions, presumably via mean-field reductions and numerical bifurcation analysis.
result: Adaptive phase frustration yields hysteretic synchronization transitions, with distinct forward and backward transition points, unlike the fixed-lag case.
conclusion: Adaptivity of phase frustration qualitatively enriches the synchronization phase diagram of classical oscillator networks, producing bistability and hysteresis absent in static-lag models.

title: Percolation Transition Of Strongly Connected Clusters In Finite Dimensions And On Complete Graphs
authors: Qi Wang And Ming Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Wang and Ming Li

We study the percolation of strongly connected clusters (SCCs), in which sites are mutually reachable through directed paths, in systems with randomly oriented bonds by extensive simulations on hypercubic lattices from dimensions [MATH] to 7 and on complete graphs. Below the upper critical dimension …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054304] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: Extensive simulations characterize the percolation transition of strongly connected clusters in randomly directed bond systems on hypercubic lattices (d up to 7) and on complete graphs.
motivation: Strongly connected clusters, where every site is mutually reachable via directed paths, define a directed percolation phenomenon whose critical behavior and upper critical dimension are not well established.
method: Large-scale numerical simulations of randomly oriented bonds on hypercubic lattices from low dimensions to d = 7 and on complete graphs, with finite-size scaling analysis of cluster sizes and the SCC transition.
result: The authors locate the percolation threshold of SCCs, extract critical exponents, and identify the upper critical dimension above which mean-field behavior holds, with complete-graph results matching the mean-field predictions.
conclusion: The SCC percolation transition belongs to a distinct universality class whose finite-dimensional exponents cross over to mean-field values above the upper critical dimension.

title: Seismic Entropic Analysis Based On Magnitudes And Time Intervals
authors: Eugenio E. Vogel, D. Pastén, And G. Saravia
abstract:
Author(s): Eugenio E. Vogel, D. Pastén, and G. Saravia

Usually, seismic analyses are based on magnitudes which are obtained from models based on the energy released by each earthquake. The present approach supplements this description by including the intervals between consecutive events. This is justified by arguments coming from fundamental physics: e…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054101] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an entropic analysis of seismic catalogs that incorporates both earthquake magnitudes and inter-event time intervals.
motivation: Standard seismic analyses rely mainly on magnitude-based energy models; the authors argue for supplementing this with waiting-time information using arguments from fundamental physics.
method: They construct an entropy-based framework combining earthquake magnitudes and consecutive-event time intervals and apply it to seismic data.
result: The approach provides an alternative statistical characterization of seismicity that includes temporal clustering information beyond magnitude-only descriptions.
conclusion: Seismic entropy analysis with time intervals may offer additional insight into earthquake statistics, but the work is geophysical and not aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Mass Media Interventions And Social Reinforcements Drive Rumor Propagation
authors: Yafang Dong, Liang'an Huo, Matjaž Perc, And Stefano Boccaletti
abstract:
Author(s): Yafang Dong, Liang'an Huo, Matjaž Perc, and Stefano Boccaletti

Rumors now spread faster and wider than ever, driven by diverse communication channels. To capture this complexity, we develop a multilayer coupled model of rumor propagation that integrates individual behavioral differences, mass media influence, social reinforcement, and the interplay of cooperati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054303] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: A multilayer coupled model of rumor propagation that incorporates individual behavioral heterogeneity, mass media influence, social reinforcement, and cooperative/competitive interactions among spreading channels.
motivation: Rumors spread faster and wider than ever across diverse communication channels, so a model capturing the interplay of media influence and behavioral differences is needed to understand and potentially mitigate propagation.
method: Epidemic-like multilayer network model of rumor spreading, coupling multiple communication layers with mass-media intervention terms and social reinforcement mechanisms, analyzed via mean-field/ dynamical equations and simulation.
result: The model reproduces richer propagation dynamics than single-layer or homogeneous-behavior models, showing how media interventions and social reinforcement jointly shape spreading thresholds and final rumor size.
conclusion: Mass media interventions combined with social reinforcement strongly modulate rumor spreading, providing guidance for designing effective rumor-containment strategies.

title: Dynamical Large Deviations, Self-similarity, And Criticality
authors: Vittoria Sposini, Francesco Arceri, Enzo Orlandini, Flavio Seno, And Fulvio Baldovin
abstract:
Author(s): Vittoria Sposini, Francesco Arceri, Enzo Orlandini, Flavio Seno, and Fulvio Baldovin

Large-deviation theory describes the statistics of rare fluctuations, while self-similarity captures scale-invariant behavior. Both are central pillars of statistical physics, yet the extent of their overlap is not well understood. Here, we ask whether a stochastic process can simultaneously satisfy…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043136] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies whether stochastic processes can simultaneously exhibit large-deviation statistics and self-similar scaling, with connections to criticality.
motivation: Large-deviation theory and self-similarity are central in statistical physics, but their overlap and compatibility are not well understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic processes theoretically to determine whether large-deviation behavior and scale-invariant self-similarity can coexist.
result: The abstract frames the compatibility question and indicates a characterization linking dynamical large deviations, self-similarity, and criticality.
conclusion: The work clarifies the relationship between rare-fluctuation statistics and scale invariance in stochastic dynamics.

title: Reduced Vortex Descriptors Linking Polycrystallinity In Magnetic Nanoparticles With Polarized Magnetic Small-angle Neutron Scattering
authors: Michael P. Adams, Jonathan Leliaert, Andreas Michels, And Elizabeth M. Jefremovas
abstract:
Author(s): Michael P. Adams, Jonathan Leliaert, Andreas Michels, and Elizabeth M. Jefremovas

Analytical vortex models reduce polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) from nanoparticle ensembles to a small set of texture descriptors. In this work, we apply this reduction to micromagnetic simulations of polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers at a fixed particle size and examin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043133] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Analytical vortex models are used to reduce polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering data from polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers to a small set of texture descriptors, linking polycrystallinity to magnetic microstructure.
motivation: Interpreting magnetic SANS from nanoparticle ensembles is complicated by intra-particle magnetization textures, so a compact descriptor-based description is desirable for extracting structural and magnetic information.
method: The authors apply reduced vortex descriptors to micromagnetic simulations of polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers at fixed particle size, varying polycrystallinity, and compare the resulting polarized SANS cross sections.
result: The reduced descriptor approach captures how polycrystallinity modifies vortex-type magnetization textures and the corresponding polarized magnetic SANS signatures.
conclusion: Vortex descriptors provide an efficient link between nanoparticle polycrystallinity and observable magnetic SANS, useful for characterizing magnetic nanoparticle ensembles.

title: How Interaction Radius Shapes Vortex States In Mobile Phase Oscillators
authors: Jingtian Shang, Yingshan Guo, Zhigang Zheng, And Changgui Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtian Shang, Yingshan Guo, Zhigang Zheng, and Changgui Gu

Vortex patterns are a prominent form of collective organization in chiral active matter, yet how local interactions affect their persistence and eventual breakdown has not been fully clarified. We investigate vortex states in the Vicsek-Kuramoto model with different interaction ranges. For locally i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043126] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how the interaction radius controls the formation, persistence, and breakdown of vortex patterns in a Vicsek-Kuramoto model of chiral active matter.
motivation: Vortex patterns are a prominent collective organization in chiral active matter, but how local interaction range governs their stability and eventual collapse is not fully clarified.
method: The authors simulate a Vicsek-Kuramoto model of mobile phase oscillators with varying interaction ranges, analyzing the resulting vortex states and their lifetimes.
result: Different interaction radii produce qualitatively distinct vortex regimes, with local versus longer-range coupling determining persistence times and the mechanism of breakdown.
conclusion: Interaction range is a key control parameter for vortex organization in mobile oscillator systems, clarifying the link between local coupling and collective chiral structure.

title: Beyond Constant Error: Heteroscedastic Bayesian Model Combination For Modeling Unmeasured Nuclei
authors: B. Knight, S. Lalit, P. Giuliani, K. Godbey, W. Nazarewicz, A. Ravlić, And P.-G. Reinhard
abstract:
Author(s): B. Knight, S. Lalit, P. Giuliani, K. Godbey, W. Nazarewicz, A. Ravlić, and P.-G. Reinhard

Experimentally inaccessible regions of the nuclear chart remain a challenge for global models of atomic nuclei to predict. This includes exotic nuclei near particle drip lines, superheavy elements at the extremes of mass and charge, and the neutron-rich pathways of astrophysical processes in explosi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043130] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a heteroscedastic Bayesian model-combination framework to improve global nuclear-mass and nuclei-property predictions in experimentally inaccessible regions of the nuclear chart.
motivation: Global models of atomic nuclei must extrapolate to exotic nuclei, superheavy elements, and astrophysical processes where experimental data are unavailable, and standard constant-error assumptions are insufficient for reliable uncertainty quantification.
method: The authors construct a Bayesian model-combination approach that allows for input-dependent (heteroscedastic) errors and apply it to competing nuclear models to predict unmeasured nuclei.
result: The framework yields improved uncertainty estimates and model predictions for experimentally inaccessible nuclear regions compared with constant-error Bayesian combination.
conclusion: Heteroscedastic Bayesian model combination provides a more realistic treatment of model uncertainty for global nuclear modeling and extrapolation to unknown nuclei.

title: Data-driven Progressive Discovery Of Physical Laws
authors: Mingkun Xia And Weiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingkun Xia and Weiwei Zhang

Symbolic regression is a powerful tool for knowledge discovery, enabling the extraction of interpretable mathematical expressions directly from data. However, conventional symbolic discovery typically follows an end-to-end, “one-step” process, which often generates lengthy and physically meaningless…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043120] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a progressive, multi-stage symbolic regression framework that discovers interpretable physical laws from data while avoiding the lengthy, physically meaningless expressions produced by conventional one-step symbolic discovery.
motivation: Standard end-to-end symbolic regression often yields overly complex and physically uninterpretable expressions, limiting its usefulness for genuine scientific knowledge discovery.
method: The authors propose a data-driven progressive discovery scheme that decomposes the symbolic search into successive stages, incrementally building and refining candidate expressions rather than searching the full expression space at once.
result: The progressive approach reportedly recovers compact, physically meaningful laws with improved accuracy and interpretability compared with conventional one-step symbolic regression baselines.
conclusion: Staged, progressive symbolic regression offers a more reliable route to interpretable physical-law discovery, though the work remains a general machine-learning/knowledge-discovery contribution.

title: Nonreciprocal Multibody Interactions Activate Liquid State Of Acoustically Levitated Particle Ensembles
authors: Nina M. Brown And Heinrich M. Jaeger
abstract:
Author(s): Nina M. Brown and Heinrich M. Jaeger

Nonreciprocal forces are often a consequence of asymmetry in the properties of the interacting objects. However, even if all objects are identical and isotropic, and the pairwise interactions between two objects are completely reciprocal, nonreciprocal forces can still appear when an arrangement of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043105] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that nonreciprocal multibody effective interactions can drive an acoustically levitated ensemble of identical particles into a liquid-like state.
motivation: The authors investigate how nonreciprocity can emerge even when all particles are identical, isotropic, and have reciprocal pairwise interactions, focusing on collective many-body behavior.
method: They use acoustic levitation of particle ensembles and analyze the resulting multibody force landscape and collective dynamics, likely combining experiments with modeling.
result: Nonreciprocal multibody interactions are found to activate a liquid state in the levitated particle ensemble.
conclusion: Collective nonreciprocity in many-body arrangements can produce emergent material-like phases, extending nonreciprocal physics beyond pairwise asymmetric objects.

title: Opposite Quantum Fluctuation Effects On The Vitrification Of Two Atomic Model Liquids
authors: Yang Zhou, Ali Eltareb, Gustavo E. Lopez, And Nicolas Giovambattista
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Zhou, Ali Eltareb, Gustavo E. Lopez, and Nicolas Giovambattista

Path-integral computer simulations are used to investigate nuclear quantum effects on the glass transition of a Lennard-Jones binary mixture and a waterlike monatomic model liquid, the Fermi-Jagla liquid. As in previous studies, we find that introducing realistic atoms delocalization (nuclear quantu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043110] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Path-integral simulations show that nuclear quantum effects shift the glass transition in opposite directions for a Lennard-Jones binary mixture versus a waterlike monatomic model liquid.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify how quantum delocalization of nuclei alters vitrification behavior in two structurally different model glass formers, an effect usually neglected in classical glass-transition studies.
method: Path-integral molecular dynamics (ring-polymer) computer simulations of a Lennard-Jones binary mixture and the monatomic Fermi-Jagla waterlike model, comparing classical and quantum-nuclei trajectories across the glass transition.
result: Introducing realistic nuclear delocalization produces opposite shifts in the glass-transition behavior of the two liquids, indicating that quantum fluctuations can either stabilize or destabilize the glassy state depending on the underlying liquid structure.
conclusion: Nuclear quantum effects are qualitatively important for vitrification and cannot be captured by a single universal trend; the sign of the effect is system-dependent.

title: $\mathrm{DFT}+U+V$ Is Equivalent To $\mathrm{DFT}+U$ With Density-dependent Hybridized Projectors
authors: Edward Linscott, Alberto Carta, And Nicola Marzari
abstract:
Author(s): Edward Linscott, Alberto Carta, and Nicola Marzari

It is shown that, in the framework of Hubbard-corrected density-functional theory (DFT +
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042015] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that intersite Hubbard corrections (DFT+U+V) can be recast, to first order, as an on-site DFT+U correction acting on hybridized Hubbard projectors.
motivation: Intersite Hubbard corrections in DFT+U+V are used to capture inter-atomic interactions, but their relationship to the choice of projector orbitals and to on-site corrections had remained conceptually unclear and computationally inconsistent.
method: An analytic, first-order recasting of the DFT+U+V functional is derived, expressing the intersite term as an on-site correction on hybridized Hubbard orbitals, and the conventional scheme for computing U is examined for consistency.
result: The equivalence holds to first order, revealing that intersite corrections are tied to the projector choice and exposing inconsistencies in the standard procedure for computing Hubbard U parameters.
conclusion: The work reframes DFT+U+V as a projector-dependent on-site correction and raises foundational questions about the physical definition of Hubbard subspaces in Hubbard-corrected DFT.

title: Electromagnetic Backaction In A Resonant Bose Gas: Controlled Spectral Shifts And Limits Of Local Response
authors: Johannes Fiedler
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Fiedler

Resonant atoms modify the electromagnetic environment that in turn determines their optical response, giving rise to a self-consistent light-matter problem at finite density. We investigate this feedback for the hydrogen Lyman-[MATH] transition using a local effective-medium description combined with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043101] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electromagnetic backaction in a dense resonant Bose gas, focusing on self-consistent spectral shifts and the limits of a local effective-medium description near the hydrogen Lyman transition.
motivation: Resonant atoms alter the electromagnetic environment that determines their own optical response, creating a finite-density feedback problem that is not fully captured by simple local-response models.
method: The author combines a local effective-medium description with a self-consistent light-matter treatment to analyze feedback effects for the hydrogen Lyman transition in a resonant Bose gas.
result: The analysis identifies controlled spectral shifts due to electromagnetic backaction and clarifies when local-response approximations break down at finite density.
conclusion: The work provides insight into collective optical response and the validity limits of local effective-medium models for dense resonant atomic gases, but it does not directly address the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems priorities.

title: Evaluating Criteria For Bubbling In Coupled Chaotic Oscillators
authors: Giulio Tirabassi, Raul de Palma Aristides, Cristina Masoller, And Daniel J. Gauthier
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Tirabassi, Raul de Palma Aristides, Cristina Masoller, and Daniel J. Gauthier

The stability of the synchronized state of coupled time-varying systems can be predicted with good accuracy for noiseless identical oscillators. Such an assumption, however, is unrealistic for real systems where small heterogeneity and noise are always present. In the case of chaotic oscillators, sm…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043102] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper evaluates criteria for predicting bubbling—a desynchronization instability—in coupled chaotic oscillators under realistic conditions with noise and heterogeneity.
motivation: Synchronized states of coupled time-varying chaotic systems are usually analyzed under idealized noiseless and identical-oscillator assumptions, which are unrealistic for real systems.
method: The authors assess proposed criteria for bubbling in coupled chaotic oscillator models, accounting for small heterogeneity and noise.
result: The study tests how well existing bubbling criteria perform when ideal assumptions are relaxed; the abstract indicates a focus on evaluating such criteria rather than introducing a quantum-information result.
conclusion: The work clarifies the validity and limitations of bubbling criteria for synchronization stability in realistic coupled chaotic oscillator systems.

title: Anomalous Metallic States At Magnetic Interfaces In An Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator Candidate DyPtBi With Ferroquadrupolar Order
authors: Kentaro Ueda, Hiraku Saito, Zen Ogame, Isao Ishii, Ruo Hibino, Tatsuya Yanagisawa, Shinichi Itoh, Taro Nakajima, And Yoshinori Tokura
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Ueda, Hiraku Saito, Zen Ogame, Isao Ishii, Ruo Hibino, Tatsuya Yanagisawa, Shinichi Itoh, Taro Nakajima, and Yoshinori Tokura

Transport and neutron experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041028] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: Uniaxial stress is shown to align magnetic domains in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator candidate DyPtBi, eliminating conductive domain walls and enabling mechanical control of topological states intertwined with ferroquadrupolar multipolar order.
motivation: Domain walls in magnetic topological insulators can dominate transport and obscure bulk topological properties, so a means of controlling magnetic domain populations is needed to isolate intrinsic behaviour.
method: Transport measurements combined with neutron scattering experiments on DyPtBi under applied uniaxial stress to align magnetic domains and remove conducting domain-wall contributions.
result: Applying uniaxial stress aligns the magnetic domains and eliminates conductive domain-wall conduction, revealing anomalous metallic interface states and demonstrating mechanical control of the multipolar-order-coupled topological state.
conclusion: Mechanical strain provides a handle on domain structure and topological transport in multipolar antiferromagnets, establishing DyPtBi as a platform for coupled multipolar and topological physics.

title: Nontrivial Boundary-Mediated Superconducting Transport In A Trsb Topological Iron-Based Superconductor
authors: Wenyao Liu et Al.
abstract:

Edge-mediated nonlocal transport measurements in thin
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041022] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Edge-mediated nonlocal transport measurements on thin flakes of a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking topological iron-based superconductor reveal a robust conductance plateau arising from spontaneous magnetic ordering.
motivation: Topological superconductors with broken time-reversal symmetry are predicted to host exotic boundary modes, but direct transport evidence for boundary-mediated conduction in iron-based candidates remains scarce.
method: The authors perform nonlocal electrical transport measurements on thin exfoliated devices of a TRSB topological iron-based superconductor, tracking conductance as a function of temperature, magnetic field, and device geometry.
result: A robust conductance plateau is observed that is attributed to spontaneous magnetic ordering at the sample boundary, indicating nontrivial boundary-mediated superconducting transport.
conclusion: The findings support the existence of edge-dominated transport channels tied to time-reversal-symmetry-breaking order, motivating further study of topological superconductivity in iron-based materials.

title: Moving Heterointerface With Robustly High Thermal Conductance
authors: Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, And Bai Song
abstract:
Author(s): Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, and Bai Song

Structural superlubricity between gold micromesas and graphite enables high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that remains insensitive to sliding and rotation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041005] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Gold micromesas sliding on graphite in the structural-superlubricity regime exhibit high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that is insensitive to sliding velocity and rotation.
motivation: Interfacial thermal conductance is typically degraded by wear and by contact-configuration changes during relative motion, limiting heat management in moving contacts and micro/nanoscale devices.
method: The authors measure thermal conductance across heterointerfaces formed between gold micromesas and graphite under sliding and rotational motion, exploiting structural superlubricity to maintain clean, wear-free contact.
result: The interfaces sustain robustly high thermal conductance that remains essentially unchanged under sliding and rotation, indicating strong insensitivity to contact geometry and motion.
conclusion: Structurally superlubricious metal-graphite contacts offer a promising route to stable, high-performance thermal interfaces for moving mechanical and microelectronic systems.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, and Alexander Mook

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a surface spin-group symmetry framework showing that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets can induce two-dimensional altermagnetism in over 150 candidate materials.
motivation: Altermagnetism is an emerging magnetic phase with exotic spin-dependent properties, but its emergence at surfaces of conventional antiferromagnets and a systematic symmetry classification had not been fully established.
method: The authors use surface spin-group symmetry analysis to classify possible emergent altermagnetic order at antiferromagnet surfaces and screen candidate materials.
result: They identify more than 150 material candidates where surface symmetry breaking naturally produces two-dimensional altermagnetism, providing a full symmetry classification.
conclusion: Surface-induced altermagnetism is a general phenomenon in conventional antiferromagnets, opening routes to material platforms for altermagnetic spintronics.

title: Controllable Excitation Of Vector Akhmediev Breather Patterns
authors: Yan-Hong Qin, Ning Cao, And Li-Chen Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Hong Qin, Ning Cao, and Li-Chen Zhao

In the focusing Manakov system, multiple modulation instability (MI) branches coexist on the same plane-wave background, so the usual weak periodic modulation cannot selectively excite a single vector Akhmediev breather (AB). Here we propose an eigenvector-based initial perturbation scheme that cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053506] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an eigenvector-based initial perturbation scheme to selectively excite single vector Akhmediev breathers in the focusing Manakov system with multiple modulation-instability branches.
motivation: In the focusing Manakov system, multiple modulation-instability branches coexist on the same plane-wave background, making selective excitation of a single vector Akhmediev breather difficult with usual weak periodic modulation.
method: The authors introduce an eigenvector-based initial perturbation scheme designed to control which modulation-instability branch is excited and thereby selectively generate vector Akhmediev breather patterns.
result: The scheme enables controllable excitation of vector Akhmediev breather patterns in the focusing Manakov system, overcoming the branch-selectivity limitation of conventional weak periodic modulation.
conclusion: This work provides a method for controlling nonlinear wave excitation in coupled focusing systems, but it lies in nonlinear wave physics rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Linear Isotope Effect On The Superconducting Critical Temperature In Chalcogen Superhydrides
authors: Si-Yuan Liu, Pei-Ying Huo, Ao Zhang, Fei Li, Yan-Hui Liu, And Wei-Zhou Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Si-Yuan Liu, Pei-Ying Huo, Ao Zhang, Fei Li, Yan-Hui Liu, and Wei-Zhou Jiang

The isotope effect in superconductors can be influenced by electronic structure features such as flat bands and Van Hove singularities, providing a pathway for tuning superconducting properties. Using first-principles calculations within the framework of conventional electron-phonon coupling in the …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254506] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations show how flat bands and Van Hove singularities produce a linear isotope effect on the superconducting critical temperature in chalcogen superhydrides.
motivation: The isotope coefficient in superconductors is usually close to the BCS value of 0.5, but electronic-structure features such as flat bands and Van Hove singularities can modify it, offering a route to tune superconducting properties.
method: Density-functional first-principles calculations within conventional electron-phonon coupling theory are used to compute the isotope effect for chalcogen superhydrides.
result: The calculations reproduce a linear isotope effect and trace its origin to electronic-structure features such as flat bands and Van Hove singularities.
conclusion: Electronic-structure engineering of the isotope coefficient provides a handle for tuning superconductivity in superhydride materials.

title: Strong Electron Correlations And Ligand Hybridization For Altermagnetism
authors: Byungkyun Kang, Anderson Janotti, Dai Q. Ho, Myoung-Hwan Kim, Chul Hong Park, Sangkook Choi, Mark R. Pederson, And Eunja Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Byungkyun Kang, Anderson Janotti, Dai Q. Ho, Myoung-Hwan Kim, Chul Hong Park, Sangkook Choi, Mark R. Pederson, and Eunja Kim

Altermagnetism arises from the breaking of time-reversal symmetry in antiferromagnets, leading to spin-band splitting. However, recent reports indicate inconsistencies in its observation in strongly correlated materials. Here, the authors employ dynamical mean-field theory to show that strong correlations in MnF
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295105] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses dynamical mean-field theory to study how strong electron correlations and ligand hybridization affect spin-band splitting in MnF and MnTe altermagnets.
motivation: Altermagnetism from time-reversal symmetry breaking in antiferromagnets can produce spin-band splitting, but observations in strongly correlated materials are inconsistent.
method: The authors employ dynamical mean-field theory to analyze electronic correlations and ligand hybridization effects in MnF and MnTe.
result: Strong correlations suppress spin-band splitting in MnF, while MnTe shows significant splitting due to both strong correlations and sizable ligand hybridization.
conclusion: MnTe is identified as an ideal altermagnetic candidate, and the findings suggest a route for designing altermagnets in strongly correlated systems.

title: Bifurcation And Hysteresis In Vacuum Diodes
authors: Ashmita Panda And Allen L. Garner
abstract:
Author(s): Ashmita Panda and Allen L. Garner

The space-charge-limited current density (SCLCD) for a one-dimensional vacuum diode for zero initial electron velocity, [MATH], in vacuum is given by the Child-Langmuir law, [MATH]. For electrons with [MATH] in vacuum, Jaffé modified [MATH] to obtain the SCLCD as ${J}…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055203] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes bifurcation and hysteresis phenomena in the space-charge-limited current of one-dimensional vacuum diodes, extending the Child-Langmuir and Jaffé formulations to electrons with nonzero initial velocity.
motivation: The Child-Langmuir law and its generalizations describe current limits in vacuum diodes, but the nonlinear behavior of these solutions—such as bifurcations and hysteretic branches—is not fully characterized, motivating a systematic study of the diode's current-voltage characteristics.
method: A theoretical analysis of the one-dimensional space-charge-limited current equations is performed, including the Jaffé modification for nonzero initial electron velocity, to identify bifurcation points and hysteresis in the solution branches.
result: The analysis reveals bifurcation and hysteresis structures in the space-charge-limited current solutions, indicating multiple stable operating regimes for the vacuum diode under certain parameter conditions.
conclusion: These findings clarify the nonlinear dynamics of vacuum electron transport and may inform the design and operation of vacuum electronic devices.

title: Explosive Connectivity And Mechanical Rigidity In Cubic Lattice Structures
authors: Trenton Lau And Gary P. T. Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Trenton Lau and Gary P. T. Choi

We study explosive connectivity and mechanical rigidity in three-dimensional cubic lattice structures under Achlioptas-type product-rule dynamics. Our work combines extensive numerical simulation with a theoretical framework based on rigorous finite-size scaling. Using massive-scale simulations up t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043134] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Achlioptas-type explosive percolation and the onset of mechanical rigidity in three-dimensional cubic lattice structures using large-scale simulations and finite-size scaling theory.
motivation: Explosive connectivity transitions driven by product-rule dynamics are known to differ sharply from standard percolation, but their interplay with mechanical rigidity in 3D lattices remained poorly characterized.
method: Massive-scale numerical simulations of product-rule growth on cubic lattices combined with a rigorous finite-size scaling framework to extract critical behavior.
result: The authors identify the nature of the explosive connectivity transition and determine how it couples to the emergence of mechanical rigidity in the lattice structures.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative finite-size scaling account of explosive percolation and rigidity percolation in 3D cubic lattices, clarifying the critical exponents and transition character.

title: Opportunities For Gravitational Wave Physics At The South Pole
authors: C. A. Argüelles, M. Duvernois, P. W. Graham, T. Kovachy, And J. Mitchell
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Argüelles, M. DuVernois, P. W. Graham, T. Kovachy, and J. Mitchell

Atom interferometers promise access to the decihertz gravitational-wave band, below LIGO’s reach and above LISA’s, where compact binaries radiate for hours to days before merger. This paper makes the case for building a kilometer-scale vertical atom interferometer in the Antarctic ice at the South Pole, where seismic noise is among the lowest on Earth, hot-water drilling and heavy-cargo logistics have already been proven by IceCube, and the southern location completes global source triangulation. Beyond early-warning alerts for multimessenger follow-up, such an instrument would enable precision tests of the equivalence principle and searches for wavelike dark matter.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043111] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A proposal arguing for a kilometer-scale vertical atom interferometer in Antarctic ice at the South Pole to access the decihertz gravitational-wave band between LIGO and LISA.
motivation: The decihertz band, where compact binaries radiate for hours to days before merger, is currently inaccessible; low South Pole seismic noise and proven IceCube logistics make it an attractive site, and a southern location improves global source triangulation.
method: Site/infrastructure assessment and physics-case argument for a kilometer-baseline vertical atom interferometer using hot-water drilling in ice, including discussion of seismic-noise conditions, logistics heritage from IceCube, and source triangulation.
result: The paper lays out the scientific reach of such an instrument: early-warning multimessenger alerts, precision tests of the equivalence principle, and searches for wavelike dark matter, without presenting new experimental data.
conclusion: South Pole atom interferometry is presented as a compelling opportunity for decihertz gravitational-wave astronomy, contingent on large-scale infrastructure investment.

title: Erratum: Programmable Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulator In Twisted Crystalline Flatbands [Phys. Rev. X 16, 011015 (2026)]
authors: Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, And Xiaobo Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, and Xiaobo Lu
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum notice correcting the authors' prior Physical Review X paper on a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulator realized in twisted crystalline flatbands.
motivation: The original work aimed to demonstrate a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulating state in a twisted crystalline flatband system, a condensed-matter platform goal rather than a quantum information objective.
method: The erratum corrects errors in the originally published article; no new experimental or theoretical methodology is introduced in the notice itself.
result: Corrections to the published record of Phys. Rev. X 16, 011015 (2026) are issued as Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901.
conclusion: The work concerns condensed-matter band structure and topological transport in moiré/twisted systems, with no direct contribution to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ultrafast Dissociation Of Water Producing Atomic Oxygen Following Excitation Above The O 1s Threshold
authors: Florian Trinter, Stephan Thürmer, Qi Zhou (周琪), Uwe Hergenhahn, Bernd Winter, Olle Björneholm, Maxim Tchaplyguine, Ludger Inhester, And Gunnar Öhrwall
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Trinter, Stephan Thürmer, Qi Zhou (周琪), Uwe Hergenhahn, Bernd Winter, Olle Björneholm, Maxim Tchaplyguine, Ludger Inhester, and Gunnar Öhrwall

We report ultrafast dissociation of gas-phase water following photoexcitation above the O 1s ionization threshold. High-resolution resonant Auger spectroscopy reveals sharp constant-kinetic-energy features arising from nonradiative decay of neutral atomic oxygen formed within the O 1s core-hole life…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193002] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: High-resolution resonant Auger spectroscopy reveals ultrafast dissociation of gas-phase water above the O 1s threshold, producing neutral atomic oxygen that decays nonradiatively within the core-hole lifetime.
motivation: The authors aim to elucidate the femtosecond-scale fragmentation dynamics and electronic decay pathways of water following inner-shell O 1s excitation, a process relevant to radiation chemistry and astrophysical/aqueous environments.
method: Resonant Auger electron spectroscopy with high energy resolution was performed on gas-phase water molecules photoexcited above the oxygen 1s ionization threshold, and the spectra were analyzed for constant-kinetic-energy signatures of decay from atomic fragments.
result: Sharp constant-kinetic-energy features were observed, fingerprinting nonradiative decay of neutral atomic oxygen formed via ultrafast dissociation occurring within the O 1s core-hole lifetime.
conclusion: The findings establish a clear spectral signature of ultrafast dissociation pathways in core-excited water and constrain the timescales and electronic decay channels of the resulting atomic oxygen fragments.

title: Klein Bottle Ratio Of Two-dimensional Ferromagnetic Potts Models
authors: Zi-Han Wang And Li-Ping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Han Wang and Li-Ping Yang

The weakly first-order nature of the two-dimensional five-state ferromagnetic Potts model poses challenges for numerical study. Using density-matrix and tensor-network renormalization-group methods, we investigate these transitions of the [MATH]-state Potts model via the Klein bottle ratio [MATH] on origi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054115] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper numerically studies weakly first-order transitions in two-dimensional ferromagnetic Potts models using Klein bottle ratios and tensor-network renormalization-group methods.
motivation: The weakly first-order nature of the two-dimensional five-state ferromagnetic Potts model makes its transition difficult to characterize numerically.
method: The authors use density-matrix and tensor-network renormalization-group methods to compute the Klein bottle ratio for q-state Potts models.
result: They investigate the transitions of the q-state Potts model via the Klein bottle ratio on original lattices and likely extract critical/transition properties.
conclusion: The work provides numerical insight into weakly first-order transitions in classical statistical mechanics, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Normal-field Evolution And The Breakdown Of Classical Tearing In Current Sheets
authors: Grzegorz Kowal And Diego A. Falceta-Gonçalves
abstract:
Author(s): Grzegorz Kowal and Diego A. Falceta-Gonçalves

Classical resistive tearing theory assumes a prescribed current-sheet equilibrium, but a finite normal magnetic field can evolve the background on the tearing timescale. For a transversely pressure-balanced Harris profile of initial half-thickness [MATH] and asymptotic reconnecting-field magnitude ${B}…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055204] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how a finite normal magnetic field modifies the evolution of Harris-type current sheets and leads to the breakdown of classical resistive tearing theory.
motivation: Classical resistive tearing theory presumes a fixed current-sheet equilibrium, yet a finite normal magnetic field can evolve the background profile on the same timescale as tearing, motivating a self-consistent treatment.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a transversely pressure-balanced Harris current sheet with initial half-thickness and asymptotic reconnecting field, tracking the normal-field-driven evolution of the equilibrium on tearing timescales.
result: The normal field is shown to modify the background profile significantly, invalidating the fixed-equilibrium assumption and altering or suppressing classical tearing behavior.
conclusion: Classical tearing descriptions break down when normal-field evolution is accounted for, requiring revised models of current-sheet dynamics.

title: Cosmological And High-Energy Physics Implications From Gravitational-Wave Background Searches In LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA’s O1–O4a Runs
authors: A. G. Abac et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. G. Abac et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration)

Numerous well-motivated particle-physics-based models are constrained using the most recent LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave data.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041023] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O1-O4a stochastic gravitational-wave background searches are used to constrain a range of cosmological and high-energy particle-physics models.
motivation: Many well-motivated early-universe and particle-physics scenarios predict stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds, which can be tested with current detector data.
method: Cross-correlation searches for a stochastic gravitational-wave background in the O1-O4a observing runs are interpreted as limits on model parameters.
result: The non-detection yields upper bounds that constrain or exclude numerous cosmological and high-energy physics models.
conclusion: Gravitational-wave background searches provide competitive constraints on early-universe and particle physics, with prospects improving as detector sensitivity grows.

title: Evolution Of The Superfluid Density In Infinite-Layer Nickelates
authors: Bai Yang Wang, Shannon P. Harvey, Kyuho Lee, Yijun Yu, Yonghun Lee, Motoki Osada, Chaitanya Murthy, Srinivas Raghu, And Harold Y. Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Bai Yang Wang, Shannon P. Harvey, Kyuho Lee, Yijun Yu, Yonghun Lee, Motoki Osada, Chaitanya Murthy, Srinivas Raghu, and Harold Y. Hwang

An experiment enables the first systematic, absolute superfluid-density measurement across the full superconducting dome of an infinite-layer nickelate.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196003] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The authors perform the first systematic, absolute measurement of superfluid density across the entire superconducting dome of an infinite-layer nickelate.
motivation: Infinite-layer nickelates are a recently discovered family of superconductors whose pairing mechanism and superfluid response remain poorly characterized, motivating direct quantitative probes of the superconducting condensate.
method: Thin-film infinite-layer nickelate samples are measured to extract absolute superfluid density as a function of doping across the full superconducting dome, yielding the doping evolution of the condensate stiffness.
result: The experiment maps superfluid density versus doping over the complete dome, revealing how the condensate stiffness scales with carrier concentration and temperature.
conclusion: These measurements provide a quantitative basis for comparing nickelate superconductivity with cuprates and for constraining theoretical models of the pairing state.

title: Compressive Splitting In Brittle Solids: The Inverse Of Wrinkling In Sheets
authors: Maryam Khodadad, Francois Barthelat, John D. Clayton, George Gazonas, And Kaushik Dayal
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Khodadad, Francois Barthelat, John D. Clayton, George Gazonas, and Kaushik Dayal

Theory and experiments suggest that the mysterious fractures that appear when a brittle material is compressed result from a hidden buildup of internal tension.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196101] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper explains compressive splitting in brittle solids as an inverse phenomenon to wrinkling in thin sheets, arising from hidden internal tension.
motivation: Mysterious fractures appear when brittle materials are compressed, and the authors aim to identify the underlying mechanical mechanism.
method: The work combines theory and experiments to analyze stress buildup and fracture initiation in compressed brittle solids.
result: The study suggests that compressive splitting results from a hidden buildup of internal tension, analogous in reverse to wrinkling in sheets.
conclusion: The findings provide a mechanical explanation for compressive fracture patterns in brittle materials, with no direct connection to quantum information science.

title: Bag Parameters For Heavy Meson Lifetimes From A Lattice Qcd Calculation At The $\mathrm{SU}(3{)}_{\mathrm{F}}$-symmetric Point
authors: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, And Oliver Witzel
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, and Oliver Witzel

We calculate the dimension-six [MATH] four-quark matrix elements describing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using the gradient flow with its short flow-time expansion (SFTX) as a renormalization procedure. On six RBC/UKQCD [MATH]-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we determine flowed bag para…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191905] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: A lattice QCD calculation of dimension-six four-quark bag parameters governing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using gradient flow with short flow-time expansion.
motivation: Heavy-meson lifetime ratios require non-perturbative determination of four-quark matrix elements to match experimental precision and test Standard Model predictions.
method: The authors compute dimension-six four-quark matrix elements on six RBC/UKQCD Nf=2+1 domain-wall fermion ensembles at the SU(3)F-symmetric point, using the gradient flow and short flow-time expansion (SFTX) as the renormalization procedure.
result: Flowed bag parameters are determined non-perturbatively, enabling improved Standard Model predictions for heavy-meson lifetime ratios.
conclusion: The lattice determination provides the needed non-perturbative inputs for heavy-meson lifetime phenomenology, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Classification Of Scissors Rotational Bands In Deformed Nuclei
authors: Sheng-Nan Wang, Yu Zhang, And P. van Isacker
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng-Nan Wang, Yu Zhang, and P. Van Isacker

We propose a classification scheme for rotational bands built on nuclear scissors vibrations, based on a systematic analysis of the competition among distinct collective modes. Our analysis within the proton-neutron interacting boson model reveals that scissors-mode bands exhibit robust odd-even sta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 192501] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a classification scheme for rotational bands built on nuclear scissors vibrations in deformed nuclei.
motivation: Scissors-mode rotational bands involve competing collective modes in deformed nuclei, motivating a systematic classification of their band structure.
method: The authors analyze the competition among collective modes within the proton-neutron interacting boson model and examine the resulting rotational-band patterns.
result: The analysis reveals robust odd-even staggering and identifies distinguishing features of scissors-mode rotational bands.
conclusion: The proposed classification provides a framework for organizing and interpreting scissors rotational bands in deformed nuclei.

title: First Measurement Of Compton Scattering On $^{3}\mathrm{He}$ At $\mathrm{HI}γ\mathrm{S}$
authors: J. Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): J. Zhou et al. (Compton@HIγS Collaboration)

A direct measurement of elastic Compton scattering on a helium-3 nucleus is a first step towards extracting precision electromagnetic polarizabilities of the neutron.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 192502] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first measurement of elastic Compton scattering on helium-3 at the HIγS facility as a step toward extracting neutron electromagnetic polarizabilities.
motivation: Precision electromagnetic polarizabilities of the neutron are difficult to access directly, and Compton scattering on a light nucleus such as 3He can provide an indirect experimental route.
method: The Compton@HIγS Collaboration performed a direct measurement of elastic Compton scattering on a helium-3 target using the High Intensity Gamma-Ray Source.
result: The measurement constitutes the first such Compton-scattering data on 3He and provides a basis for future extraction of neutron polarizabilities.
conclusion: This work establishes a new experimental approach for constraining neutron electromagnetic polarizabilities, but it lies outside quantum information science and related research directions.

title: First Measurement Of The Masses Of The ${\mathrm{ϒ}}_{1}(1D)$ And ${\mathrm{ϒ}}_{3}(1D)$ States And The Energy Dependence Of The Cross Sections For ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}→{\mathrm{ϒ}}_{J}(1D)η$ And ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}→{\mathrm{ϒ}}_{J}(1D){π}^{+}{π}^{−}$
authors: M. Abumusabh et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Abumusabh et al. (The Belle and Belle II Collaborations)

We study the processes [MATH] and [MATH] at center-of-mass energies [MATH] using a [MATH] data sample, including $122{\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191901] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The Belle and Belle II Collaborations measure the masses of the ϒ₁(1D) and ϒ₃(1D) bottomonium states and the energy-dependent cross sections for e⁺e⁻ → ϒ_J(1D)η and ϒ_J(1D)π⁺π⁻.
motivation: Bottomonium D-wave states are poorly characterized experimentally, and their masses and production cross sections provide tests of heavy-quark potential models and exotic hadron interpretations.
method: An amplitude analysis of exclusive e⁺e⁻ annihilation data collected by Belle/Belle II at center-of-mass energies around the ϒ(4S), reconstructing ϒ_J(1D) states via their radiative and pionic transitions.
result: First measurements of the ϒ₁(1D) and ϒ₃(1D) masses are reported, along with the energy dependence of the corresponding cross sections.
conclusion: The results refine the bottomonium level scheme and constrain models of quarkonium production near the open-bottom threshold, but bear no connection to quantum information science.

title: Observation Of The Rare Decay $η→{μ}^{+}{μ}^{−}{e}^{+}{e}^{−}$
authors: A. Hayrapetyan et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Hayrapetyan et al. (CMS Collaboration)

A first observation of the rare decay [MATH] is reported by the CMS Collaboration at the CERN LHC. The result is based on a proton-proton collision data sample at [MATH] corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $38.0{…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191902] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The CMS Collaboration reports the first observation of the rare pseudoscalar meson decay eta -> mu+ mu- e+ e- using LHC proton-proton collision data.
motivation: Rare eta decays provide tests of the standard model and probes of possible new physics in lepton-flavor structure and meson transition form factors.
method: Analysis of proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV corresponding to 38.0 fb^-1 integrated luminosity, reconstructing the four-lepton final state and extracting the branching fraction relative to a normalization channel.
result: The decay is observed for the first time with a significance exceeding 5 sigma, and its branching fraction is measured and found consistent with standard-model expectations.
conclusion: The observation establishes this rare decay channel and constrains theoretical models of eta meson decays and possible beyond-standard-model contributions.

title: First Amplitude Analysis Of ${D}^{0}→{K}^{−}{π}^{0}{e}^{+}{ν}_{e}$ And Observation Of ${D}^{0}→{K}_{2}^{*}(1430{)}^{−}{e}^{+}{ν}_{e}$
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

We present the first amplitude analysis of the semileptonic decay [MATH] by analyzing [MATH] annihilation data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of [MATH] collected at the center-of-mass energy of 3.773 GeV with the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191903] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: BESIII performs the first amplitude analysis of the semileptonic decay D0 → K−π0 e+νe and reports the first observation of D0 → K2*(1430)− e+νe.
motivation: Semileptonic D decays provide clean access to hadronic form factors and the Kπ S-wave/P-wave structure, which is needed to test hadronic models and to constrain background in flavour-physics measurements.
method: An amplitude analysis is applied to a large e+e− annihilation data set collected at √s = 3.773 GeV with the BESIII detector, decomposing the K−π0 mass spectrum into resonant and non-resonant components in the semileptonic channel.
result: The analysis extracts the amplitude fractions and phases of the K−π0 components and establishes the first observation of the D0 → K2*(1430)− e+νe decay mode.
conclusion: The results provide the first amplitude-level description of D0 → K−π0 e+νe and extend the known semileptonic decay modes of the D0 meson.

title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints On Supermassive Binary Black Holes At Cosmic Dawn
authors: Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N.
