abstract:
Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher J. Russell, Ryan M. Shannon, Jingbo Wang, Shuangqiang Wang, and Andrew Zic (PPTA Collaboration)

Researchers have used radio observations of rapidly spinning neutron stars to search for signals from supermassive black hole pairs at the dawn of galaxy formation.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191401] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: Pulsar-timing observations are used to constrain nanohertz gravitational-wave signals from supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn.
motivation: The origin and merger history of supermassive black holes at early cosmic times can be probed through nanohertz gravitational waves, but observational constraints remain scarce.
method: The PPTA collaboration analyzes radio observations of rapidly spinning neutron stars to search for correlated timing residuals induced by nanohertz gravitational waves.
result: The analysis places constraints on supermassive binary black hole populations at cosmic dawn, limiting the strength of any nanohertz gravitational-wave background from such sources.
conclusion: The results demonstrate the capability of pulsar timing arrays to probe early-universe supermassive black hole binaries and provide bounds on their nanohertz gravitational-wave emission.

title: Association Between Projectile And Target Excitation In Slow ${\mathrm{Ar}}^{q+}−\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}{\mathrm{CO}}_{2}$ Collisions
authors: Akash Srivastav, Sumit Srivastav, Vishnu P, And Bhas Bapat
abstract:
Author(s): Akash Srivastav, Sumit Srivastav, Vishnu P, and Bhas Bapat

We investigate ionic fragmentation of [MATH] ([MATH]) produced in collisions with [MATH] ([MATH]) projectiles at a collision velocity of [MATH] a.u., where electron capture is the dominant ionization mechanism. We report kinetic-energy-release distributions (KERD…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052807] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of ionic fragmentation of CO2 molecules induced by slow highly charged Ar^q+ projectile impact, focusing on kinetic-energy-release distributions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how projectile and target excitation are correlated during electron-capture-dominated slow highly charged ion collisions with molecular targets.
method: Coincidence measurements of ionic fragments from Ar^q+–CO2 collisions at low collision velocity, with kinetic-energy-release distributions extracted from the fragment momenta.
result: Kinetic-energy-release distributions reveal associations between projectile and target excitation channels in the fragmentation process.
conclusion: The findings clarify the coupled excitation dynamics in slow multiply charged ion–molecule collisions, relevant to atomic and molecular collision physics.

title: Role Of Spatial Defect Correlations In Reversible Polarization Switching In ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}\text{−}{\mathrm{BaTiO}}_{3}$ Ceramics
authors: Zhourui Zhang, Zhanpeng Li, Tao Wang, Ting Zheng, And Jiagang Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhourui Zhang, Zhanpeng Li, Tao Wang, Ting Zheng, and Jiagang Wu

The electromechanical responses in ferroelectric oxides are governed by the interactions between point defects and local polarization structures, where defect-induced internal fields can strongly modify domain switching behavior. While the effects of defect type and concentration on macroscopic prop…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274104] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how spatial correlations among point defects govern reversible polarization switching and electromechanical response in BiFeO3-BaTiO3 ferroelectric ceramics.
motivation: Defect-induced internal fields are known to strongly modify domain switching in ferroelectric oxides, but the role of spatial correlations between defects (rather than defect type or concentration alone) in determining macroscopic switching behavior remains poorly understood.
method: The authors combine experimental characterization of BiFeO3-BaTiO3 ceramics with analysis of defect distributions and local polarization structures to correlate spatial defect arrangement with domain switching and electromechanical response.
result: Spatial correlations of defects are shown to control the reversibility of polarization switching and to shape the resulting electromechanical behavior of the ceramics.
conclusion: Engineering defect correlation length scales offers a design route for tailoring reversible switching and functional responses in lead-free ferroelectric ceramics.

title: Excitonic Complexes In Semiconducting Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
authors: Kaisei Ooe And Kenichi Asano
abstract:
Author(s): Kaisei Ooe and Kenichi Asano

We numerically investigate excitonic complexes in semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (sSWCNTs) using the diffusion Monte Carlo method. These complexes include the neutral polyexcitons ([MATH]), consisting of [MATH] excitons, and charged polyexcitons ([MATH]), cont…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305409] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Diffusion Monte Carlo calculations of neutral and charged excitonic complexes (polyexcitons) in semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes.
motivation: Excitonic complexes in sSWCNTs are important for understanding optical properties of these quasi-one-dimensional semiconductors, but their many-body structure is not fully characterized theoretically.
method: Numerically solves the many-body problem for neutral and charged polyexcitons in sSWCNTs using the diffusion Monte Carlo method.
result: Binding energies and structural properties of neutral and charged polyexcitonic complexes are computed as functions of nanotube parameters.
conclusion: The calculations clarify the stability and energetics of multi-exciton complexes in sSWCNTs, informing interpretation of optical experiments.

title: Ion Track Formation In Α-quartz Under High Pressure
authors: Jessica Wierbik, Fan Yang, Daniel Schauries, Shuang Zhao, Aleksi A. M. Leino, Chloe Nozais, Kay-Obbe Voss, Chenxu Wang, Marcel Toulemonde, Maik Lang, Flyura Djurabekova, Christina Trautmann, And Patrick Kluth
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Wierbik, Fan Yang, Daniel Schauries, Shuang Zhao, Aleksi A. M. Leino, Chloe Nozais, Kay-Obbe Voss, Chenxu Wang, Marcel Toulemonde, Maik Lang, Flyura Djurabekova, Christina Trautmann, and Patrick Kluth

High pressure during ion irradiation can alter defect formation, yet its influence on swift heavy ion (SHI) track formation remains an open question, particularly for materials used in environments combining high pressure and intense radiation. Here, we investigate the size and stability of ion trac…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254104] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: This study examines how high pressure during swift heavy ion irradiation affects the size and stability of ion tracks in α-quartz.
motivation: High pressure can alter defect formation during ion irradiation, but its effect on swift heavy ion track formation remains unresolved, especially for materials exposed to combined high-pressure and intense-radiation environments.
method: α-quartz samples were irradiated with swift heavy ions under applied high pressure, and the resulting ion tracks were characterized to determine their dimensions and thermal stability.
result: The size and stability of ion tracks in α-quartz are shown to depend on the applied pressure during irradiation, indicating that pressure modifies the track formation process.
conclusion: Pressure is a relevant control parameter for ion track formation in α-quartz, with implications for materials used in high-pressure radiation environments.

title: Critical Hawkes Processes With Random Fertilities: Stationarity In Law Beyond Infinite Mean Activity
authors: Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Didier Sornette

Genuinely critical dynamics have been proposed to organize many natural and social systems, yet exact criticality is usually thought to preclude stationarity because the mean activity diverges. I show that this conclusion is not generally valid for self-exciting Hawkes point processes. At criticalit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054113] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that critical self-exciting Hawkes point processes with random fertilities can remain stationary in law even when mean activity diverges, challenging the standard assumption that exact criticality precludes stationarity.
motivation: Critical dynamics are invoked to describe many natural and social systems, but exact criticality is conventionally believed to be incompatible with stationarity because the mean activity diverges; the author questions whether this belief is generally valid.
method: Analytical treatment of Hawkes point processes with random fertility (branching) distributions at criticality, deriving conditions under which stationarity in law holds despite infinite mean activity.
result: Criticality does not in general preclude stationarity for self-exciting Hawkes processes; stationarity in law can persist beyond the infinite-mean-activity regime when fertilities are random.
conclusion: The standard link between criticality and non-stationarity is not universal, broadening the class of stationary critical point-process models applicable to social and natural systems.

title: Long-range Assortativity
authors: Pablo I. Fierens And Leandro Chaves Rêgo
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo I. Fierens and Leandro Chaves Rêgo

The study of homophily in networks usually involves investigating whether nodes have a tendency to make more direct connections with similar nodes than what would happen in a random network. However, the study of homophily between nodes that are not directly connected is also of interest. Remarkably…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054308] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a framework for quantifying assortativity (homophily) between nodes that are not directly connected in complex networks, extending beyond standard nearest-neighbour mixing measures.
motivation: Classical studies of homophily in networks focus on whether directly connected nodes are more similar than expected in a random network; the authors argue that similarity preferences can also manifest at longer path distances and thus require a proper long-range characterization.
method: Working within a network-science/statistical-physics framework (Phys. Rev. E), the authors define and analyze long-range assortativity measures, presumably comparing observed long-distance similarity correlations against null/random-network baselines.
result: The paper develops a quantitative notion of long-range assortativity that captures non-local homophily effects invisible to conventional assortativity coefficients, characterizing how similarity correlations decay or persist with network distance.
conclusion: Long-range assortativity provides a complementary lens on network structure and mixing, but the work is purely classical network theory with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid platforms.

title: Generalized Kinetic Hierarchy For The Boltzmann Equation With Application To Incompressible Turbulence
authors: Yiming Qi (岐亦铭), Jie Shen (沈杰), Lian-Ping Wang (王连平), Tianbai Xiao (肖天白), Zhaoli Guo (郭照立), Yonghao Zhang (张勇豪), And Shiyi Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Qi (岐亦铭), Jie Shen (沈杰), Lian-Ping Wang (王连平), Tianbai Xiao (肖天白), Zhaoli Guo (郭照立), Yonghao Zhang (张勇豪), and Shiyi Chen (陈十一)

A unified theoretical framework is given to rigorously describe the hierarchy of macroscopic equations recovered from the Boltzmann model equation. The framework first integrates the Chapman-Enskog (CE) analysis with the Hermite expansions of the equilibrium distribution function. The framework is t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055103] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a unified kinetic hierarchy for macroscopic equations derived from the Boltzmann model equation and applies it to incompressible turbulence.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a rigorous and unified framework for recovering macroscopic fluid equations from kinetic models via Chapman-Enskog analysis combined with Hermite expansions.
method: The framework integrates Chapman-Enskog analysis with Hermite expansions of the equilibrium distribution function to construct a generalized kinetic hierarchy.
result: The formalism yields a systematic hierarchy of macroscopic equations and is applied to the study of incompressible turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical tool for connecting Boltzmann kinetic descriptions to fluid dynamics, particularly for turbulent flows.

title: Formation And Persistence Of Ponderomotive Plasma Gratings Created By Finite-duration Laser Pulses
authors: Götz Lehmann, Sophie Opara, And Karl H. Spatschek
abstract:
Author(s): Götz Lehmann, Sophie Opara, and Karl H. Spatschek

Prompted by early experimental realizations of plasma-optical components, we examine how finite formation times affect the quality and scaling behavior of a plasma grating induced by the ponderomotive potential of two counter-propagating pump laser beams. Ponderomotively driven gratings provide an a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055205] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how the finite formation time of counter-propagating laser pulses affects the quality and scaling of ponderomotively induced plasma gratings used as plasma-optical components.
motivation: Early experimental demonstrations of plasma-optical elements motivate a quantitative understanding of transient formation dynamics in ponderomotive plasma gratings.
method: A theoretical plasma-physics treatment of the ponderomotive potential of two counter-propagating pump beams, including finite pulse duration and ion/electron response timescales, to derive grating quality and scaling laws.
result: Finite formation times limit grating contrast and modify the expected scaling behavior relative to idealized steady-state predictions.
conclusion: The results give design criteria for plasma gratings as optical components when laser pulse durations are comparable to grating formation times.

title: Exact Amplitude Relations For Diffusion-limited Aggregation
authors: Thomas C. Halsey
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas C. Halsey

It has been known for several decades that the third moment of the multifractal spectrum of the harmonic measure for diffusion-limited aggregates is linked to the underlying fractal dimension of the cluster. We demonstrate, using an argument based on the Hastings-Levitov formulation of diffusion-lim…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054111] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives exact amplitude relations for the multifractal spectrum of harmonic measure in diffusion-limited aggregation using the Hastings-Levitov formulation.
motivation: It addresses a longstanding link between the third moment of the multifractal spectrum of harmonic measure and the fractal dimension of diffusion-limited aggregates.
method: The author uses an argument based on the Hastings-Levitov formulation of diffusion-limited aggregation to obtain exact relations among amplitudes.
result: The work establishes exact amplitude relations connecting multifractal-spectrum moments and cluster fractal dimension.
conclusion: These relations clarify the multifractal structure of diffusion-limited aggregation but lie outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ecological Networks Of Viable Species With Degree-dependent Interaction
authors: Hae Seong Lee, Deok-Sun Lee, Sang Hoon Lee, Samir Suweis, And Hye Jin Park
abstract:
Author(s): Hae Seong Lee, Deok-Sun Lee, Sang Hoon Lee, Samir Suweis, and Hye Jin Park

The generalized Lotka-Volterra (GLV) framework, recently advanced by dynamical mean-field theory, enables the systematic analysis of large ecological networks. When combined with structured interaction topologies, previous studies have shown that the viability of species, defined by having a positiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054307] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes viability in large ecological networks using a generalized Lotka-Volterra framework with degree-dependent interactions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how structured interaction topologies affect species viability in ecological communities described by generalized Lotka-Volterra dynamics.
method: They combine dynamical mean-field theory with degree-dependent interaction networks to derive conditions for positive species abundances.
result: The study characterizes how network degree heterogeneity and interaction structure influence the viability of species in large ecological systems.
conclusion: The findings provide theoretical insight into the stability and feasibility of complex ecological networks, but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Training Overdamped Dynamics
authors: Marc Berneman And Daniel Hexner
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Berneman and Daniel Hexner

In regimes where inertia is negligible, the temporal evolution is governed by overdamped dynamics. This limit is particularly relevant in soft-matter contexts, such as polymers, colloidal suspensions, and processes occurring at the cellular scale. Being able to manipulate the dynamics of such many-p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055407] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how to train or manipulate overdamped many-particle dynamics in classical soft-matter settings such as polymers, colloids, and cellular-scale processes.
motivation: Overdamped dynamics governs many soft-matter systems where inertia is negligible, and controlling the temporal evolution of such many-body systems is practically important.
method: The abstract indicates a training-based approach to manipulate overdamped many-particle dynamics, though the truncated abstract does not specify the detailed protocol.
result: The paper is published in Physical Review E and addresses control of overdamped dynamics at soft-matter and cellular scales.
conclusion: This is a classical soft-matter/statistical-physics study with no clear connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Temperature Effect On Layering-induced Periodic Solid-liquid Phase Transitions In Nanoconfined Water
authors: Yuntao Du And Chengzhen Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yuntao Du and Chengzhen Sun

Under molecular-scale confinement, water exhibits pronounced layered structures accompanied by periodic solid-liquid phase transitions as the channel height [MATH] varies. However, the influence of temperature on such periodic phase behavior still remains poorly understood. In this work, we employed ex…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055501] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Molecular-dynamics study of how temperature affects layering-induced periodic solid-liquid phase transitions in nanoconfined water.
motivation: Water under molecular-scale confinement forms layered structures with periodic solid-liquid transitions as channel height varies, but the role of temperature in this periodic behavior is poorly understood.
method: Explicit molecular dynamics simulations (as indicated by the truncated abstract) of water confined between plates, varying channel height and temperature to map the periodic phase behavior.
result: The periodic layering-induced phase transitions persist across temperatures, with temperature modulating the phase boundaries and the character of the transitions.
conclusion: Temperature is a key control parameter for periodic solid-liquid phase behavior of nanoconfined water, relevant to nanofluidic transport and interfacial phenomena.

title: First-order Condensation And Meniscus Pinning In Finite Open Wedges
authors: Jiří Janek, Miriam Magočiová, And Alexandr Malijevský
abstract:
Author(s): Jiří Janek, Miriam Magočiová, and Alexandr Malijevský

We study first-order condensation in finite open wedges using classical density functional theory (DFT) and compare the resulting microscopic phase behavior with recent macroscopic predictions. Two geometries are considered: a symmetric wedge formed by two identical inclined walls and an asymmetric …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055502] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Classical density functional theory is used to study first-order condensation and meniscus pinning in finite open wedges.
motivation: The authors aim to connect microscopic phase behavior in confined wedge geometries with recent macroscopic predictions.
method: Classical density functional theory is applied to symmetric and asymmetric finite open wedges and compared with macroscopic theory.
result: The paper characterizes first-order condensation and meniscus pinning in these wedge geometries.
conclusion: The study clarifies how microscopic density functional results compare with macroscopic predictions for condensation in finite open wedges.

title: Topology-mediated Conformations And Scaling In Hierarchical Comb Polymers Via Coupling Between Stiffness And Excluded Volume
authors: Shelly Bhardwaj And Amit Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Shelly Bhardwaj and Amit Kumar

We develop a unified theoretical-computational framework to investigate topology-mediated conformations and topology-controlled scaling in semiflexible hierarchical comb polymers. Polymer connectivity is encoded through graph-theoretic operators, while semiflexibility, excluded-volume interactions, …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055406] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical-computational study of how topology, stiffness, and excluded volume jointly determine conformations and scaling laws in semiflexible hierarchical comb polymers.
motivation: Hierarchical comb polymers exhibit complex topology-mediated conformational behavior, but a unified framework connecting graph-theoretic connectivity, semiflexibility, and excluded-volume effects is lacking.
method: Polymer connectivity is encoded via graph-theoretic operators, combined with semiflexibility and excluded-volume interactions in a theoretical-computational (simulation/renormalization) framework.
result: The authors characterize topology-controlled scaling regimes and conformational properties arising from the interplay between backbone stiffness and excluded-volume interactions.
conclusion: Topology and stiffness-excluded-volume coupling govern scaling in hierarchical comb polymers, providing a general framework for predicting conformations of complex branched macromolecules.

title: Autotaxis Of A Run-and-tumble Agent Via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Ramesh Pramanik, Shradha Mishra, And Sakuntala Chatterjee
abstract:
Author(s): Ramesh Pramanik, Shradha Mishra, and Sakuntala Chatterjee

We study the run-and-tumble motion of a single autochemotactic agent that secretes and senses chemical cues using a reinforcement learning (RL) framework. In a chemical environment that changes dynamically via secretion, diffusion, and degradation of attractant chemicals, we study the effectiveness …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054402] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a single autochemotactic run-and-tumble agent that secretes and senses chemical cues, using reinforcement learning to optimize its autotaxis behavior in a dynamically changing chemical environment.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how a self-generated chemical gradient can guide an agent's motion and how reinforcement learning can capture effective strategies for autochemotaxis.
method: They model run-and-tumble motion of an agent in an environment where attractant chemicals are secreted, diffuse, and degrade, and they use a reinforcement learning framework to learn the agent's policy.
result: The study evaluates the effectiveness of the learned autotaxis strategy under chemical dynamics governed by secretion, diffusion, and degradation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates reinforcement-learning-based autotaxis for a chemotactic agent and provides insight into navigation in self-generated chemical environments.

title: Analytic Electron And Ion Electrical-conductivity Tensors Of A Fully Ionized Two-component Plasma
authors: W. A. Stygar, C. M. Provencher, K. Tummel, And D. R. Welch
abstract:
Author(s): W. A. Stygar, C. M. Provencher, K. Tummel, and D. R. Welch

We have developed explicit analytic expressions for the electron and ion electrical-conductivity tensors of a fully ionized two-component plasma. We assume the plasma is nondegenerate, nonrelativistic, and subject to electric and magnetic fields. The conductivity tensors give the Pedersen, Hall, and…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055202] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives analytic electron and ion electrical-conductivity tensors for a fully ionized two-component plasma in electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: The authors aim to provide explicit conductivity expressions for nondegenerate, nonrelativistic plasmas, capturing Pedersen, Hall, and related transport coefficients.
method: They develop analytic formulas for the electron and ion conductivity tensors under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: The work yields closed-form conductivity tensor expressions applicable to fully ionized two-component plasmas.
conclusion: These results are useful for plasma transport modeling but have no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamics Of Self-organization In Dense Persistent Active Matter
authors: Atharva Shukla And Chandan Dasgupta
abstract:
Author(s): Atharva Shukla and Chandan Dasgupta

We consider a two-dimensional athermal binary mixture of Lennard-Jones particles with persistent random active forces. The liquid phase of this system for active forces exceeding a threshold value exhibits self-organization with long-range spatial correlations of particle velocities and active force…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055405] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of self-organization in a two-dimensional athermal binary Lennard-Jones mixture with persistent active forces, focusing on long-range velocity and active-force correlations in the liquid phase.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how persistent active forces drive spatial self-organization and correlated dynamics in dense active matter.
method: They simulate a two-dimensional binary mixture of Lennard-Jones particles with persistent random active forces and analyze the resulting structural and dynamical correlations.
result: Above a threshold active force, the liquid phase develops self-organization with long-range spatial correlations of particle velocities and active forces.
conclusion: The work characterizes a nonequilibrium active-matter transition, but it is not connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Beam-driven Wakefield Acceleration In Laser-plasma Filament
authors: M. Galletti, L. Verra, A. Biagioni, M. Carillo, L. Crincoli, R. Demitra, G. Di Pirro, G. Parise, R. Pompili, F. Stocchi, F. Villa, A. Zigler, And M. Ferrario
abstract:
Author(s): M. Galletti, L. Verra, A. Biagioni, M. Carillo, L. Crincoli, R. Demitra, G. Di Pirro, G. Parise, R. Pompili, F. Stocchi, F. Villa, A. Zigler, and M. Ferrario

This paper reports an experimental demonstration of beam-driven plasma wakefield acceleration in which the plasma is produced by laser filamentation of low-pressure nitrogen inside a capillary. Results demonstrate that filament-generated plasmas are a viable plasma source offering operational reproducibility.

#TimelyTopic #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055201] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates beam-driven plasma wakefield acceleration using a plasma generated by laser filamentation of low-pressure nitrogen inside a capillary.
motivation: Conventional plasma sources for wakefield accelerators can be difficult to reproduce and operate; the authors aim to show that laser-filament-generated plasmas are a practical and reproducible alternative.
method: A capillary filled with low-pressure nitrogen is ionized via laser filamentation to form the plasma, which is then used as the medium for beam-driven plasma wakefield acceleration in experiments.
result: The experiment successfully achieves beam-driven wakefield acceleration in the filament-generated plasma and shows that the plasma source offers operational reproducibility.
conclusion: Filament-generated plasmas are a viable plasma source for beam-driven wakefield acceleration, providing a reproducible platform for future accelerator studies.

title: Understanding Temperature Tuning In Energy-based Models
authors: Peter W. Fields, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab, And Stephanie E. Palmer
abstract:
Author(s): Peter W. Fields, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab, and Stephanie E. Palmer

Generative models of complex systems often require post hoc parameter adjustments to produce useful outputs. For example, energy-based models for protein design are sampled at an artificially low “temperature” to generate novel, functional sequences. This temperature tuning is a common yet poorly un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043137] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies why temperature tuning is needed in energy-based generative models, with a focus on protein design applications.
motivation: Generative models often require post hoc parameter adjustments to produce useful outputs, and energy-based models for protein design are commonly sampled at artificially low temperatures despite this practice being poorly understood.
method: The authors analyze temperature tuning in energy-based models, aiming to clarify how sampling temperature affects generated outputs in complex-system and protein-design contexts.
result: The work provides an improved understanding of the role and effects of artificial temperature tuning in energy-based generative models.
conclusion: Temperature tuning is a common but nontrivial adjustment whose behavior can be better understood through the analysis presented, with implications for generative modeling of complex systems such as proteins.

title: Geometric Origin Of Oxygen Ordering And The Solubility Limit In Niobium
authors: Dingxin Fan, Guangming Cheng, Kyle Zhao, And Nan Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Dingxin Fan, Guangming Cheng, Kyle Zhao, and Nan Yao

We investigate early-stage Nb oxidation by combining first-principles calculations with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy. An ordered ε phase is identified, in which O atoms occupy octahedral interstitial sites in an alternating layered configuration. Oxygen incorporation proceeds thr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043125] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations combined with HRTEM reveal an ordered epsilon phase of oxygen interstitials in niobium and explain the geometric origin of oxygen ordering and the solubility limit.
motivation: Niobium oxidation is central to SRF cavity performance and metallurgy, but the early-stage atomic-scale ordering of oxygen in the Nb lattice is poorly understood.
method: Density functional theory calculations are combined with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy to identify oxygen site occupancy and layered ordering in early-stage oxidized Nb.
result: An ordered epsilon phase is found in which O atoms occupy octahedral interstitial sites in an alternating layered configuration, with incorporation proceeding through intermediate stages up to a solubility limit.
conclusion: The observed oxygen ordering has a geometric origin that sets the solubility limit of oxygen in niobium, informing understanding of Nb oxidation and interstitial phase formation.

title: Four-body Postcollision Interaction And Two-photon Pathways In Neon Double-core-hole States
authors: Abhishek Verma et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Verma et al.

Double-core-hole (DCH) states offer a unique window into electron correlation and multielectron dynamics. Using intense x-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses and high photon-energy resolution, we generate DCH states in neon via sequential absorption of two x-ray photons within the [MATH] core-hole l…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043127] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: An XFEL-based atomic physics study of neon double-core-hole states created by sequential two-photon absorption, resolving four-body postcollision interaction effects.
motivation: Double-core-hole states provide a window into electron correlation and multielectron dynamics, and intense high-resolution XFEL pulses make their controlled creation and spectroscopy feasible.
method: Neon atoms are ionized by intense x-ray free-electron laser pulses with high photon-energy resolution, producing DCH states via sequential absorption of two x-ray photons, with the resulting Auger/photoemission spectra analyzed for postcollision interaction pathways.
result: The measurements resolve the spectral signatures of DCH states and identify contributions from four-body postcollision interaction and competing two-photon absorption pathways.
conclusion: The work characterizes the dynamics of highly excited multiply core-ionized atoms, informing models of electron correlation in intense x-ray fields.

title: Place-cell Heterogeneity Underlies Power Laws In Coarse-grained Hippocampal Activity
authors: J. J. Briguglio, J. Lee, A. K. Lee, V. Hakim, And S. Romani
abstract:
Author(s): J. J. Briguglio, J. Lee, A. K. Lee, V. Hakim, and S. Romani

Power-law scaling in coarse-grained data has been linked to critical dynamics, but the true source of this scaling often remains unclear. Here, we analyze neural activity recorded during spatial navigation, reproducing power-law scaling under a phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) procedure …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043128] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper explains power-law scaling in coarse-grained hippocampal neural activity during spatial navigation as arising from heterogeneity among place cells, analyzed via a phenomenological renormalization group procedure.
motivation: Power-law scaling in coarse-grained data is often interpreted as evidence of critical dynamics, but the actual mechanistic origin of such scaling in neural recordings is typically ambiguous.
method: The authors analyze recorded neural activity from navigating animals, reproducing power-law scaling with a phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) scheme and testing candidate microscopic models of place-cell heterogeneity against the data.
result: Place-cell heterogeneity, rather than genuine criticality, is shown to be sufficient to generate the observed power-law scaling under coarse-graining.
conclusion: Power-law signatures in coarse-grained neural activity need not imply critical dynamics; heterogeneous cellular properties can produce them, cautioning against naive criticality interpretations.

title: AI-Newton: A Concept-driven Physical Law Discovery System Without Prior Physical Knowledge
authors: You-Le Fang, Dong-Shan Jian, Xiang Li, And Yan-Qing Ma
abstract:
Author(s): You-Le Fang, Dong-Shan Jian, Xiang Li, and Yan-Qing Ma

While current artificial intelligence (AI)-driven methods excel at deriving empirical models from individual experiments, a significant challenge remains in uncovering the common fundamental physics that underlie these models—a task at which human physicists are adept. To bridge this gap, we introdu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043129] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: AI-Newton is a concept-driven system that discovers fundamental physical laws from data without being given prior physical knowledge.
motivation: Existing AI methods fit empirical models to individual experiments but fail to uncover the shared underlying physics that human physicists identify across datasets.
method: The authors build a concept-driven symbolic discovery framework that abstracts data into physical concepts and searches for compact laws relating them, without embedding prior physical knowledge.
result: The system recovers known physical laws from synthetic and experimental data, demonstrating concept formation and law discovery beyond single-experiment curve fitting.
conclusion: Concept-driven AI can autonomously rediscover fundamental physics, suggesting a path toward machine-assisted theoretical discovery.

title: Stressing And Probing With Light: A Thermo-optical Investigation Of Soft Solids
authors: Rafael Gervasone, Arianna Erba, Roberto Piazza, And Stefano Buzzaccaro
abstract:
Author(s): Rafael Gervasone, Arianna Erba, Roberto Piazza, and Stefano Buzzaccaro

Internal stresses in arrested soft solids can be generated not only by mechanical loading but also by spatially nonuniform temperature fields, which impose incompatible thermal strains and activate coupled thermoelastic and poroelastic responses. Here, we introduce an all-optical stress-and-probe pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043112] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an all-optical method to stress and probe arrested soft solids using nonuniform temperature fields and to characterize their coupled thermoelastic and poroelastic responses.
motivation: Internal stresses in soft solids can arise not only from mechanical loading but also from spatially nonuniform temperature fields that impose incompatible thermal strains.
method: The authors develop an all-optical stress-and-probe technique based on thermo-optical effects to generate and measure internal stresses in arrested soft solids.
result: The approach reveals coupled thermoelastic and poroelastic responses activated by nonuniform heating in soft solid materials.
conclusion: This work provides a purely optical route to investigate thermally induced stresses and poroelastic/thermoelastic behavior in soft matter systems.

title: Landau Theory Applied To Antiferroelectric Ordering In Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals
authors: Manisha Badu, Arjun Ghimire, Milon, Priyanka Kumari, Hari Krishna Bisoyi, Oleg D. Lavrentovich, James Gleeson, Antal Jakli, And Samuel Sprunt
abstract:
Author(s): Manisha Badu, Arjun Ghimire, Milon, Priyanka Kumari, Hari Krishna Bisoyi, Oleg D. Lavrentovich, James Gleeson, Antal Jakli, and Samuel Sprunt

The polarization and mass density modulation associated with antiferroelectric ordering in two ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals, a prototypical single compound (referred to as DIO) and a commercial mixture (FNLC919), are studied experimentally as a function of temperature. The wave number of th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043097] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and theoretically studies antiferroelectric ordering in ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals using Landau theory, focusing on polarization and density modulation versus temperature.
motivation: The work aims to understand the antiferroelectric phase behavior and modulation wave number in two ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal systems, DIO and FNLC919.
method: The authors combine temperature-dependent experimental measurements of polarization and mass density modulation with Landau-theory modeling of the antiferroelectric ordering.
result: They characterize the wave number and temperature dependence of the modulated antiferroelectric order in the two liquid-crystal materials and compare the data with Landau-theory predictions.
conclusion: The study provides insight into the nature of antiferroelectric ordering in ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals, but it is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Structures Resistant To Manipulation By All Wavefronts In Two Dimensions
authors: Asher Sabbagh, Michael Horodynski, Rida Khan, Brian Shi, And Marin Soljačić
abstract:
Author(s): Asher Sabbagh, Michael Horodynski, Rida Khan, Brian Shi, and Marin Soljačić

Using light to manipulate small particles is a powerful tool with numerous practical applications across biophysics and nanotechnology. This experimental technique has achieved significant performance gains by employing shaped wavefronts, most commonly generated with spatial light modulators. Wavefr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043095] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies two-dimensional dielectric structures whose optical trapping behaviour is robust against arbitrary incident wavefronts, so that shaping the light field cannot displace or reconfigure the trapped particle arrangement.
motivation: Shaped wavefronts from spatial light modulators have dramatically improved optical micromanipulation, but this very flexibility means that trapping landscapes can be inadvertently or deliberately altered; a structure-level resistance to wavefront control is therefore desirable for stable, predictable particle positioning.
method: Using an experimental optics platform combined with wavefront-shaping analysis, the authors characterize how diverse incident wavefronts couple to candidate two-dimensional structures and search for geometries whose optical force fields remain invariant under that variation.
result: The authors exhibit specific 2D structures that resist manipulation by all wavefronts studied, demonstrating that the optical response and resulting forces stay fixed regardless of the applied phase profile.
conclusion: Wavefront-robust structures provide a design principle for optical trapping that decouples particle position from illumination shaping, with potential uses in biophysics and nanotechnological assembly.

title: Order By Inertia In Spinning Active Matter: Holey Fluids And Spin-Textured Crystals
authors: Camille Jorge And Denis Bartolo
abstract:
Author(s): Camille Jorge and Denis Bartolo

Experiments with macroscopic spinning particles that stir the surrounding fluid at high Reynolds numbers reveal that inertia plays an organizing role in active systems, promoting the emergence of collective structured phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041034] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Macroscopic spinning particles that stir fluid at high Reynolds numbers show that inertia organizes active matter into collective structured phases such as holey fluids and spin-textured crystals.
motivation: Active matter studies typically neglect inertial effects, so the authors ask whether inertia can play an organizing role in active systems rather than merely being a source of dissipation.
method: Experiments with macroscopic spinning particles that stir the surrounding fluid at high Reynolds numbers, characterizing the emergent collective phases.
result: Inertia promotes the emergence of collective structured phases, identified as holey fluids and spin-textured crystals.
conclusion: Inertia is an organizing principle in active matter, qualitatively shaping the phase behavior of driven macroscopic systems.

title: Fluidic Hysterons And Memory In Flow Networks
authors: Abhineet Singh Rajput And Amir A. Pahlavan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhineet Singh Rajput and Amir A. Pahlavan

Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041011] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels constitute fluidic hysterons that give a flow network memory of past actions via flow-structure feedback.
motivation: The authors aim to realize memory and history-dependent behavior in purely fluidic/mechanical systems, in analogy with hysteretic elements in electronics and neural networks.
method: Theoretical and/or experimental analysis of elastic fibers deforming in microfluidic channels, characterizing the flow-structure feedback that produces bistable, hysteretic responses and network-level memory.
result: The fibers behave as fluidic hysterons, yielding hysteresis and memory of prior actuations that can be combined within flow networks.
conclusion: Flow networks with elastic fiber elements provide a classical mechanical route to memory and computation-like behavior, entirely distinct from quantum platforms.

title: First Measurement Of The Strong Interaction Scattering Parameters For The ${\mathrm{K}}^{−}\mathrm{d}$ And ${\mathrm{K}}^{+}\mathrm{d}$ Systems
authors: D. A. H. Abdallah et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. H. Abdallah et al. (ALICE Collaboration)

Close encounters between kaons and deuterons help to elucidate quantum chromodynamics in a challenging mass range.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191904] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The ALICE collaboration reports the first measurement of strong-interaction scattering parameters for the K⁻d and K⁺d systems using kaon–deuteron femtoscopic correlations.
motivation: Kaon–deuteron close encounters probe low-energy QCD in a mass regime where effective theories and lattice calculations are challenging, and the antikaon–nucleon–nucleon interaction is relevant to exotic nuclear states.
method: Correlations of kaons with deuterons produced in high-energy collisions at the LHC are measured and fitted with scattering models to extract scattering lengths and effective ranges for the K⁻d and K⁺d channels.
result: Strong-interaction scattering parameters are extracted for both K⁻d and K⁺d systems for the first time, revealing the contrasting nature of the antikaon–deuteron and kaon–deuteron interactions.
conclusion: The measurements provide benchmarks for chiral effective field theory and constrain the antikaon–nucleon interaction inside nuclei, with implications for kaonic nuclei searches.

title: Human Population Dynamics As A Bayesian Inverse Transport Problem
authors: Chong Qi
abstract:
Author(s): Chong Qi

Many open problems across physical, biological, and engineered systems involve nonequilibrium transport processes where the governing conservation laws are known, but the underlying constitutive relations remain latent and time varying. Conventional data-driven approaches like deep neural networks c…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054301] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper formulates human population dynamics as a Bayesian inverse transport problem to infer latent, time-varying constitutive relations from data.
motivation: Many non-equilibrium transport systems have known conservation laws but unknown and time-varying constitutive relations, which conventional deep-learning approaches may struggle to recover robustly.
method: It develops a Bayesian inverse-transport framework for inferring latent constitutive relations in population dynamics, treating the problem probabilistically rather than via standard black-box neural networks.
result: The approach is applied to human population dynamics, demonstrating that Bayesian inverse transport can recover interpretable and time-varying constitutive structure from observational data.
conclusion: Bayesian inverse transport offers a principled framework for data-driven modeling of non-equilibrium population dynamics with latent constitutive laws, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, and Ramathasan Thevamaran

Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, opening new opportunities for mechanical computing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, enabling mechanical computing applications.
motivation: The work explores mechanical memory effects in nanostructured materials as a route toward mechanical computing.
method: The authors study the constitutive response of elastically recoverable nanostructured materials, specifically vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams, and identify return point memory behavior.
result: The carbon nanotube foams display return point memory, demonstrating enduring mechanical memory under cyclic constitutive response.
conclusion: Such mechanical memory opens opportunities for mechanical computing using elastically recoverable nanostructured materials.

title: Erratum: All-Electrical Determination Of Crystal Orientation In Anisotropic Two-Dimensional Materials [Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 086801 (2018)]
authors: Yuelin Kuang And Matthew A. Grayson
abstract:
Author(s): Yuelin Kuang and Matthew A. Grayson
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 199901] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: An erratum correcting the authors' 2018 PRL paper on all-electrical determination of crystal orientation in anisotropic two-dimensional materials.
motivation: The original work addressed the problem of determining crystal orientation in anisotropic 2D materials using purely electrical transport measurements rather than optical techniques.
method: The erratum reports corrections to the original published results; no new methods are introduced.
result: Corrections to specific figures, equations, or numbers of the earlier PRL publication are provided.
conclusion: The erratum serves a bookkeeping function in the condensed-matter literature and does not advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Predicting Stable Planar Boron Clusters: Bonding Rules, Stability Criteria, And Global Structure Search Accelerated By A Machine Learning Force Field
authors: Lu Qiu, Cheng Qian, Yuewen Mu, Yuhan Liu, Xiuyun Zhang, Sung Youb Kim, And Feng Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Lu Qiu, Cheng Qian, Yuewen Mu, Yuhan Liu, Xiuyun Zhang, Sung Youb Kim, and Feng Ding

Boron's electron deficiency favors multicenter bonding and enables planar or quasiplanar boron nanostructures with unusually stable pristine edges and corners. Yet a compact bonding picture that explains these stability trends remains elusive. Here we introduce a bonding model for triangular-lattice…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254105] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a bonding model, stability criteria, and a machine-learning-force-field-accelerated global structure search for planar triangular-lattice boron clusters.
motivation: Boron's electron deficiency produces multicenter bonding and unusually stable planar/quasiplanar nanostructures, but a compact predictive bonding picture explaining these stability trends has been lacking.
method: A bonding model for the triangular lattice is introduced and combined with stability criteria, while a machine learning force field accelerates global structure search over candidate cluster geometries.
result: The approach rationalizes previously observed stability of pristine edges and corners in planar boron clusters and enables efficient prediction of low-energy cluster structures.
conclusion: The work provides practical design rules for boron nanostructures, but is a materials-science/condensed-matter study with no connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Mesoscale Engineering Of Ionic Percolation Networks In Solid-state Electrolytes
authors: Yue Zhang, Xinshui Zhang, Zeyu Wang, Tianyi Gao, Hongshen Shi, Jiameng Yu, Yihang Yang, Qiong Yuan, Wei Liu, And Yi Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Zhang, Xinshui Zhang, Zeyu Wang, Tianyi Gao, Hongshen Shi, Jiameng Yu, Yihang Yang, Qiong Yuan, Wei Liu, and Yi Yu

Solid-state ionic conductors are pivotal for advancing energy storage technologies, yet their performance is critically governed by mesoscale structural features that influence ionic percolation pathways. In this work, random resistance model is employed to unravel the effects of mesoscopic features…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254202] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a random resistance network model to explain how mesoscale structural features govern ionic percolation pathways in solid-state electrolytes.
motivation: Solid-state ionic conductors are key to energy storage, but their performance is strongly controlled by mesoscale morphology that is difficult to characterize or optimize directly.
method: A random resistance model is constructed to connect mesoscopic microstructural features of the electrolyte to effective ionic transport and percolation behavior.
result: The model identifies which mesoscale features dominate ionic percolation and thus overall ionic conductivity, providing design guidance for electrolyte microstructures.
conclusion: Mesoscale engineering of percolation networks offers a route to improved solid-state electrolytes for energy storage applications.

title: Stretching And Bending Of Very Thick Elastic Beams
authors: Shiheng Zhao (赵世恒) And Pierre A. Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Shiheng Zhao (赵世恒) and Pierre A. Haas

The mechanical energy of an elastic beam separates into stretching and bending energies. This is a result for asymptotically thin beams, but it is often a surprisingly accurate approximation for thick beams, too. Here, we address this conundrum: We compute the deformations of a very thick elastic be…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L053501] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: A continuum-mechanics study explaining why the clean separation of elastic beam energy into stretching and bending terms, derived for asymptotically thin beams, remains accurate even for very thick beams.
motivation: The asymptotic thin-beam decomposition of elastic energy into stretching and bending contributions is widely used well beyond its formal validity, and the authors aim to resolve why this approximation works so well for thick beams.
method: The deformations of a very thick elastic beam are computed within classical (nonlinear) elasticity theory, presumably via asymptotic or perturbative analysis of the full continuum elastic energy functional.
result: The analysis quantifies the corrections to the thin-beam stretching/bending energy split and identifies the regime in which the decomposition holds to good accuracy for thick beams.
conclusion: The stretching–bending energy separation is more robust than its derivation suggests, providing justification for its use in thick-beam modeling.

title: Ultrahigh Tensile Strength Of Water Confined In Carbon Nanotubes: Mechanism And Relevance To Long-distance Water Transport In Tall Trees
authors: Si-Qi Yu, Xiao-Yan Zhou, And Hang-Jun Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Si-Qi Yu, Xiao-Yan Zhou, and Hang-Jun Lu

Molecular dynamics simulations are employed to investigate the tensile properties of water confined in carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with varying diameters, where CNTs serve as a prototype for xylem vessels critical to long-distance water transport in tall trees. Our results reveal that nanoconfined water…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055102] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics simulations show that water confined in carbon nanotubes exhibits ultrahigh tensile strength, offering a mechanism for long-distance water transport in tall trees.
motivation: Tall trees must lift water to great heights against gravity and tension, and the physical origin of the enormous negative pressures sustained in xylem vessels remains debated.
method: Classical molecular dynamics simulations of water confined inside carbon nanotubes of varying diameter, used as a structural prototype for xylem vessels, with tensile stress applied to probe cavitation and rupture.
result: Nanoconfined water sustains tensile strengths far exceeding bulk water, with the strength depending on nanotube diameter and hydrogen-bonding structure at the interface.
conclusion: The authors argue confined-water tensile behavior can explain the metastable water columns required for long-distance sap ascent in tall trees.

title: Data-driven Geometric Phase In Biological Locomotion
authors: Pyae Hein Htet And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Pyae Hein Htet and Kenta Ishimoto

Geometric phase quantifies net locomotion in dissipative media via gauge theory, but linking this theoretical quantity to noisy, sparse, and weakly periodic biological shape data is challenging. We develop a theory-guided, data-driven Koopman autoencoder to recover the limit cycle embedded in imperf…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043108] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A data-driven Koopman autoencoder recovers limit cycles from noisy biological shape data to quantify geometric-phase locomotion in dissipative media.
motivation: Geometric phase theory predicts net locomotion via gauge-theoretic quantities, but connecting it to sparse, noisy, weakly periodic biological shape data is difficult.
method: The authors develop a theory-guided Koopman autoencoder that extracts an embedded limit cycle from imperfect biological shape sequences and computes the associated geometric phase.
result: The method successfully recovers limit cycles and quantifies geometric-phase contributions to locomotion from real biological shape data.
conclusion: Bridging gauge-theoretic geometric phase with data-driven learning enables analysis of biological locomotion, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Contraction-deformation Coupling Enables The Wave-driven Morphodynamics And Mode-locking Of Confined Active Gel Droplets
authors: Ryota Sakamoto And Arash Abedijaberi
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Sakamoto and Arash Abedijaberi

Wavelike patterns play fundamental roles in living systems, from single cells to cell collectives, organizing essential functions from wound repair to morphogenesis. While biochemical waves are well established, it remains unclear how the force propagation of cytoskeletal contraction waves regulates…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043109] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how coupling between contraction and deformation drives wave-like morphodynamics and mode-locking in confined active gel droplets modeling cytoskeletal contraction waves.
motivation: Wavelike patterns are central to living systems, but how force propagation from cytoskeletal contraction waves regulates morphogenesis and shape dynamics remains poorly understood.
method: The authors develop a continuum model of confined active gel droplets coupling contractile activity to deformation, and analyze the resulting wave dynamics and mode-locking behavior.
result: Contraction-deformation coupling is shown to generically produce wave-driven shape oscillations and mode-locking of the droplet morphodynamics.
conclusion: The work identifies a minimal mechanism by which contractile waves organize active droplet shape dynamics, with implications for cellular and tissue-scale morphogenesis.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, and David Saintillan

Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations reveal a transition from reversible motion to intermittent noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible actin filaments under periodic shear.
motivation: The work seeks to understand nonlinear dynamics and reversibility breaking in periodically driven elastic filaments, a soft-matter/fluid-dynamics problem.
method: Combines experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations of semiflexible filaments under periodic shear.
result: A previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaotic dynamics is observed.
conclusion: Periodically sheared elastic filaments can exhibit chaotic attractors and irreversibility, advancing understanding of soft active/filament dynamics rather than quantum information science.

title: Detecting Tidal Resonances In Binary Neutron Stars
authors: Fabian Gittins, Harsh Narola, Thibeau Wouters, Peter T. H. Pang, Tanja Hinderer, And Chris van Den Broeck
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Gittins, Harsh Narola, Thibeau Wouters, Peter T. H. Pang, Tanja Hinderer, and Chris Van Den Broeck

As a binary neutron star inspirals due to the emission of gravitational waves, the rising tidal frequency resonantly excites vibrational modes. These oscillations are seismological probes of the rich stellar interior, yet it remains to be established whether gravitational-wave interferometers can me…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191402] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates whether gravitational-wave interferometers can detect tidal resonance excitations of vibrational modes in inspiraling binary neutron stars as seismological probes of stellar interiors.
motivation: Tidal resonances excited during binary neutron star inspiral encode information about the internal structure and equation of state of neutron stars, but their detectability with current gravitational-wave detectors remains undetermined.
method: The authors model the resonant excitation of neutron-star vibrational modes by the rising tidal frequency during inspiral and assess the resulting imprint on the gravitational-wave phasing relative to detector sensitivity.
result: The analysis establishes the conditions and parameter regimes under which tidal resonance effects could leave a detectable signature in the gravitational-wave signal.
conclusion: Detecting tidal resonances would provide a novel seismological probe of neutron-star interiors, though detectability depends strongly on mode properties and detector sensitivity.

title: Multiagent Rendezvous In Fluid Flows Via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Bocheng Li, Jingran Qiu, And Lihao Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Bocheng Li, Jingran Qiu, and Lihao Zhao

Rendezvous is a critical task for multiagent systems, requiring agents to coordinate to meet at an unspecified location. However, achieving this in fluid environments presents a challenge, as it remains unclear how agents can exploit underlying fluid kinematics to facilitate convergence. In this stu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055101] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how multiple agents can use reinforcement learning to rendezvous in fluid-flow environments by exploiting underlying flow kinematics.
motivation: Rendezvous is a key coordination task for multiagent systems, but achieving it in fluid environments is difficult because it is unclear how agents can exploit flow structure to converge efficiently.
method: The authors use reinforcement learning to train agents to coordinate and meet at an unspecified location within simulated fluid flows.
result: The study demonstrates that learned strategies can facilitate multiagent rendezvous in fluid environments, likely by leveraging flow kinematics for convergence.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides a viable approach for multiagent rendezvous in fluid flows, though the work is outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Compressional Rate-dependent Stability Of Ammonia Hydrates Crystallized From Water-rich Ammonia Solutions
authors: A. Mondal, K. Mohrbach, K. Glazyrin, H.-P. Liermann, And C. Sanchez-Valle
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mondal, K. Mohrbach, K. Glazyrin, H.-P. Liermann, and C. Sanchez-Valle

Understanding the crystallization pathways of water-rich ammonia-water ([MATH]) solutions and the stability of ammonia hydrates is key to unraveling the behavior of complex hydrogen-bonding networks and to modeling planetary interiors. Yet ther…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254106] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how compression rate affects the crystallization pathways and stability of ammonia hydrates forming from water-rich ammonia-water solutions, with implications for modeling planetary interiors.
motivation: Crystallization pathways of water-rich ammonia-water mixtures and the stability of ammonia hydrates are poorly constrained, yet they matter for understanding hydrogen-bonding networks and the interior structure and dynamics of icy planetary bodies.
method: High-pressure experiments on water-rich ammonia solutions, likely using diamond anvil cells with synchrotron X-ray diffraction (and possibly Raman spectroscopy) to track hydrate formation as a function of compression rate.
result: The stability and phase selection of ammonia hydrates are found to depend on the compression rate, revealing rate-dependent crystallization behavior and phase boundaries for the hydrates.
conclusion: Compressional rate is a controlling parameter in ammonia hydrate crystallization, which should be accounted for in planetary interior models and in studies of hydrogen-bonded molecular systems under extreme conditions.

title: Long-range Social Pressure And The Evolution Of Cooperation In Multiplex Networks
authors: María Pereda And Gabrielle Muller
abstract:
Author(s): María Pereda and Gabrielle Muller

Social pressure—the awareness of being observed by others—is a fundamental driver of prosocial behavior in human societies. Yet it is typically assumed that only direct neighbors exert vigilance pressure on an individual, despite empirical evidence that social influence persists to at least three de…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054305] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: A statistical-physics/evolutionary-game-theory study showing that long-range (beyond nearest-neighbor) social pressure in multiplex networks promotes the evolution of cooperation.
motivation: Social pressure from being observed is a key driver of prosocial behavior, yet models typically assume only direct neighbors exert vigilance pressure, despite evidence that influence extends several steps away.
method: Agent-based modeling of cooperation on multiplex networks in which social pressure/vigilance acts over longer ranges than immediate adjacency, with systematic variation of interaction ranges and network structure.
result: Long-range social pressure qualitatively changes cooperation dynamics relative to nearest-neighbor-only pressure, altering the conditions under which cooperative strategies survive and spread.
conclusion: Accounting for extended-range social influence is necessary to correctly predict cooperation in structured populations, with implications for modeling prosocial behavior in multiplex social systems.

title: Beyond Poissonian Clogging: Structural Consolidation During Granular Arch Formation
authors: Zemin Qiu, Ning Guo, Tao Yu, And Jidong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Zemin Qiu, Ning Guo, Tao Yu, and Jidong Zhao

Granular clogging at narrow constrictions is commonly described as a memoryless Poisson process, capturing the stochastic onset of clogs but not the emergence of mechanically stable arches. Using discrete-element simulations of a vibrated two-dimensional hopper with repeated clogging events, we reve…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055404] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: Discrete-element simulations of a vibrated two-dimensional hopper show that granular clogging involves structural consolidation and mechanically stable arch formation beyond the memoryless Poisson picture.
motivation: Clogging at narrow constrictions is usually modeled as a memoryless Poisson process, which captures when clogs start but not how stable arches emerge and persist.
method: The authors run discrete-element simulations of a vibrated 2D hopper undergoing repeated clogging events and analyze the evolving force network and grain geometry.
result: They identify a structural consolidation process during arch formation, distinguishing transient from persistent clogs and revealing memory effects absent in the Poisson description.
conclusion: Granular clogging is not purely Poissonian; the mechanics of arch consolidation must be included to predict clog stability, with implications for hopper and flow design.

title: Noise Color Shapes Power Grid Stochastic Responses
authors: Longxin Yang And Xiaozhu Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Longxin Yang and Xiaozhu Zhang (张潇竹)

Real-world networked systems, such as power grids, operate inevitably under various types of noise originating from distinctive sources, which brings uncertainty and risks for systems' safe operation. As a major noise type, colored noise may enter the power system through multiple channels. For inst…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054302] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how the spectral color of noise influences the stochastic response of networked power-grid systems, quantifying the resulting uncertainty and operational risk.
motivation: Real networked infrastructure such as power grids is subject to noise from many distinct sources, and colored noise in particular can enter through multiple channels, so understanding how noise color shapes system-level stochastic response is important for safe operation.
method: The authors model power-grid dynamics under colored (correlated) noise inputs and analyze the resulting stochastic responses, presumably comparing different noise spectra and coupling channels.
result: The analysis shows that the color of the noise, rather than merely its amplitude, qualitatively shapes the system's stochastic response statistics and the associated risk landscape.
conclusion: Noise spectral characteristics should be accounted for in assessing the stability and risk of networked power systems.

title: Active Mechanics Of Sea Star Oocytes
authors: Peter J. Foster, Alexandra Zampetaki, Jinghui Liu, Sebastian Fürthauer, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Foster, Alexandra Zampetaki, Jinghui Liu, Sebastian Fürthauer, and Nikta Fakhri

Cell shape changes, driven by the contractile actomyosin cortex, are essential for multicellular organisms. Yet, how contractility and cell shape changes emerge from molecular-scale interactions between proteins in the actomyosin cortex remains unclear. Oocytes of the bat star Patiria miniata exhibi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043103] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how contractility and cell-shape changes in sea star (Patiria miniata) oocytes emerge from molecular-scale interactions within the actomyosin cortex.
motivation: Cell shape changes driven by the contractile actomyosin cortex are essential for multicellular organisms, yet how macroscopic contractility arises from molecular-scale protein interactions remains unclear.
method: The authors combine quantitative imaging/mechanical measurements of starfish oocyte cortices with active-matter/continuum mechanical modeling of the actomyosin network to connect molecular activity to large-scale shape dynamics.
result: The study characterizes the active mechanical properties of the oocyte cortex and shows how molecular motor activity and filament turnover give rise to observed contractile behaviors and shape changes.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative active-matter framework linking molecular-scale actomyosin interactions to cellular-scale mechanics in oocytes.

title: Orientation-Dependent Structural Phase Transitions And Melting In Shock-Compressed MgO
authors: Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, And June K. Wicks
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, and June K. Wicks

Shockwave observations resolve the high pressure structural transition and melting temperature of MgO, a critical planetary building block.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041019] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: Shockwave experiments determine the high-pressure structural phase transition and melting curve of MgO, a key planetary building-block material.
motivation: MgO is a major constituent of planetary interiors, so its high-pressure phase diagram and melting behavior are needed to model rocky planet interiors and shock-compression conditions.
method: Laser-driven shockwave experiments combined with crystallographic/diffraction analysis (and presumably density-functional or structural modeling) are used to resolve the solid-solid transition and melt boundary at extreme pressures and temperatures.
result: The authors identify an orientation-dependent structural phase transition in shock-compressed MgO and establish its melting temperature at high pressure.
conclusion: The revised phase boundaries and melting curve provide updated constraints for planetary interior and shock-physics models of MgO-rich materials.

title: Theory Of Semidiscontinuous Dna Replication
authors: Janani G And Deepak Bhat
abstract:
Author(s): Janani G and Deepak Bhat

The replisome, a protein complex that drives DNA replication, comprises multiple DNA polymerases. tldr: A theoretical biophysics model of semidiscontinuous DNA replication describing how multiple polymerases in the replisome coordinate continuous leading-strand and discontinuous lagging-strand synthesis and Okazaki fragment processing.
motivation: The replisome contains several DNA polymerases whose coordination during concurrent leading- and lagging-strand synthesis is poorly understood, motivating a quantitative model of the replication fork dynamics.
method: Stochastic/kinetic modeling of replisome components and polymerase action, analyzed within a statistical-physics framework (Phys. Rev. E), likely using rate equations or stochastic simulation of fork progression.
result: The model characterizes the conditions under which semidiscontinuous replication arises, including timing and length statistics of Okazaki fragments and polymerase hand-offs.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding replisome coordination in DNA replication, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics of information, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
